sentences.zh: =徐台英=徐台英，字佩章，廣東南海人。

translations.literal: =Xu Taiying= Xu Taiying, style name Peizhang, was a native of Nanhai in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Taiying, whose style was Peizhang, came from Nanhai in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，授湖南華容知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of the Daoguang reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Huarong in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1841 and was appointed magistrate of Huarong in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 俗好訟，台英謂訟獄糾纏，由於上下不通。

translations.literal: The custom was fond of litigation; Taiying said that lawsuits and cases became entangled because communication between above and below was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The locals were fond of lawsuits. Taiying held that litigation became entangled because there was no open communication between officials and the people.

sentences.zh: 與民約，傳到即審結，胥役需索者痛懲之。

translations.literal: He made an agreement with the people that when a document arrived it would be tried and concluded at once; clerks and runners who demanded extortion were severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed with the people that every petition would be heard and decided as soon as it arrived, and he severely punished any clerk or runner who extorted them.

sentences.zh: 一日，閱呈詞，不類訟師胥吏筆，鞫之，果諸生也。

translations.literal: One day, reviewing a petition, it did not resemble the hand of a litigation master or clerk; he questioned the man and it turned out to be a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was reviewing a petition whose style did not match that of a pettifogger or clerk. He questioned the author and found that he was indeed a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 拘至，試以詩、文，文工而詩劣。

translations.literal: He was brought in custody and tested with poetry and prose; his prose was skilled but his poetry inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The man was brought in and tested in poetry and prose. His prose was accomplished but his poetry poor.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「詩本性情，汝性情卑鄙，宜其劣。

translations.literal: He admonished him, saying: "Poetry springs from one's nature; your nature is base and petty, so it is fitting that it is inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Taiying told him, "Poetry expresses one's character. Your character is base, so it is only right that your poetry is poor.

sentences.zh: 念初犯，姑宥，其改行！」

translations.literal: Considering it was a first offense, for the moment I pardon you—reform your conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: As this is your first offense, I will spare you for now—but mend your ways!"

sentences.zh: 其人感泣去。

translations.literal: That person, moved to tears, departed.
translations.idiomatic: The man left in tears, deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 規复沱江書院，月自課之。

translations.literal: He planned to restore the Tuojiang Academy and each month examined the students himself.
translations.idiomatic: He set out to restore the Tuojiang Academy and personally examined the students there each month.

sentences.zh: 曰：「陸清獻作令，日與諸生講學。

translations.literal: He said: "Lu Qingxian, when serving as magistrate, daily lectured with the students on learning.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "When Lu Qingxian served as magistrate, he lectured to his students every day.

sentences.zh: 吾不曉講學，若教人作文，因而誘之讀書立品，是吾志也。」

translations.literal: I do not understand lecturing on learning; if I teach people to write compositions and thereby lead them to read books and establish character, that is my aim."
translations.idiomatic: I do not know how to lecture as he did, but if I can teach students to write essays and thereby draw them toward reading and upright character, that will satisfy my purpose."

sentences.zh: 縣田有圻田、埦田、山田之分。

translations.literal: The county's fields were divided into qi fields, wan fields, and mountain fields.
translations.idiomatic: The county's lands were classified as qi fields, wan fields, and mountain fields.

sentences.zh: 瀕湖地，旱少潦多，埦、圻例有蠲緩，田無底冊，影射多。

translations.literal: Land bordering the lake: drought was few and flooding many; wan and qi fields by precedent had remission and deferment, but fields had no base register and shadow-registration was frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Lands along the lake suffered more from flood than drought. Wan and qi fields were customarily granted tax relief, but with no master land register, many owners shifted their holdings onto other categories to evade tax.

sentences.zh: 書役墊徵，官給空票。

translations.literal: Clerk-runners advanced collection; the magistrate gave blank tickets.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks advanced tax payments on their own and the magistrate issued them blank receipts.

sentences.zh: 花戶糧數，任其自註。

translations.literal: The grain quota for each registered household was left to them to annotate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Households were allowed to record their own tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 役指為欠者，拘而索之，官不知所徵之數。

translations.literal: Runners designated who owed, arrested and demanded payment, while the magistrate did not know the amounts being collected.
translations.idiomatic: Runners would name debtors, seize them, and demand payment, while the magistrate had no idea how much was actually being collected.

sentences.zh: 保戶包納漕米，相沿以為便，挾制浮收，無過問者。

translations.literal: Guarantor households packaged payment of tribute grain, which was handed down as convenient; they coerced and collected excessively, and none investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Guarantor households had long handled consolidated grain tribute payments as a convenience, but they used their position to extort inflated collections, and no one held them accountable.

sentences.zh: 積欠數万，官民交病。

translations.literal: Arrears accumulated to tens of thousands; both officials and people were afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears mounted to tens of thousands of taels, to the mutual distress of officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 台英知其弊，乃清田冊，注花戶糧數、姓名、住址，立碑埦上，使冊不能改。

translations.literal: Taiying knew these abuses; he cleared the land registers, noted each household's grain quota, name, and address, erected a stele on the wan embankment so the register could not be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing these abuses, Taiying compiled a clear land register listing each household's quota, name, and address, and had it inscribed on a stone tablet at the wan embankment so the record could not be tampered with.

sentences.zh: 應緩、應徵者可親勘，而影射之弊絕。

translations.literal: Those who should be deferred or those who should be levied could be personally surveyed, and the abuse of shadow-registration ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He could personally verify who qualified for relief and who owed tax, which put an end to fraudulent reassignment of land categories.

sentences.zh: 申糧隨業轉之例，即時過割，而飛灑之弊絕。

translations.literal: He reported the precedent that grain tax follows transfer of property, with immediate registration of transfer, and the abuse of "scattered flying" ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the rule that tax liability follows the transfer of land, requiring prompt registration of every sale, which ended the practice of leaving tax obligations on the previous owner.

sentences.zh: 收漕分設四局，俾升合小戶，就近輸納，免保戶之加收，而包納之弊絕。

translations.literal: For collecting tribute grain he set up four offices separately, enabling small households to pay nearby, exempting guarantor surcharges, and the abuse of packaged payment ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He divided grain collection among four offices so that even small households could pay nearby, removing the guarantors' surcharges and ending consolidated collection abuses.

sentences.zh: 埦田舊有堤修費，出田主。

translations.literal: Wan fields formerly had embankment repair fees, borne by field owners.
translations.idiomatic: Owners of wan fields had traditionally paid embankment repair fees.

sentences.zh: 有挪埦田作圻田，冀免堤費者；

translations.literal: Some shifted wan fields to register as qi fields, hoping to escape embankment fees;
translations.idiomatic: Some reclassified wan fields as qi fields to avoid embankment fees;

sentences.zh: 有賣田留稅，派費賠累者；

translations.literal: some sold the field but retained the tax, with repair fees assigned causing losses;
translations.idiomatic: others sold their land but left the tax registered in their name, leaving them liable for fees;

sentences.zh: 有賣稅留田，派費不至者：堤費不充。

translations.literal: some sold the tax but retained the field, so fees did not arrive: embankment funds were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: and still others sold the tax obligation but kept the land, so fees never reached the fund: embankment revenues ran short.

sentences.zh: 一埦堤潰，他埦同希豁免。

translations.literal: When one wan embankment burst, other wan fields likewise hoped for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When one wan embankment failed, owners of neighboring wan fields all hoped for the same exemption.

sentences.zh: 凡借帑修堤者，久無償，相率亡匿。

translations.literal: All who had borrowed treasury funds to repair embankments, long without repayment, fled and hid in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had borrowed government funds for repairs had long failed to repay and fled in numbers.

sentences.zh: 台英丈田均費，低窪者許減派，不許匿畝。

translations.literal: Taiying measured fields and equalized fees; low-lying land was permitted reduced assignment, and concealing acreage was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Taiying surveyed the fields and apportioned fees evenly, allowing reductions for low-lying plots while forbidding concealed acreage.

sentences.zh: 其人戶俱絕，歸宗祠管業承費。

translations.literal: Where the household line was extinct, it reverted to the lineage shrine to manage the property and bear the fees.
translations.idiomatic: Where a household had died out, the ancestral hall took over the land and assumed the fees.

sentences.zh: 巨族有抗者罪之。

translations.literal: Great clans who resisted were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families who resisted were punished.

sentences.zh: 行之期年，堤工皆固，逋賦盡輸。

translations.literal: After carrying this out for a year, embankment works were all solid and arrears were fully paid.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the embankments were secure and all arrears were paid.

sentences.zh: 調耒陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Leiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Leiyang.

sentences.zh: 耒陽徵糧，由櫃書裡差收解，取入倍於官。

translations.literal: In Leiyang grain collection was handled by cabinet clerks and village agents who collected and forwarded it, taking in double what reached the government.
translations.idiomatic: In Leiyang, tax collection was handled by clerks and village agents who forwarded grain, pocketing twice what they delivered to the government.

sentences.zh: 刁健之戶輕。

translations.literal: Crafty and sturdy households were lightly taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Aggressive households were under-assessed.

sentences.zh: 良善之戶重，民積忿。

translations.literal: Good and honest households were heavily taxed; the people accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Honest households bore the heaviest burdens, and popular resentment mounted.

sentences.zh: 有楊大鵬者，以除害為名，欲揭竿為亂。

translations.literal: There was one Yang Dapeng who, under the name of removing harm, wished to raise a banner in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Yang Dapeng, claiming he would remove these abuses, sought to raise rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事平，台英遂盡革裡差。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Taiying then completely abolished village agents.
translations.idiomatic: After the disturbance was suppressed, Taiying abolished the village agents entirely.

sentences.zh: 時上官欲命舉甲長以代裡差，仍主包收包解。

translations.literal: At that time superiors wished to order selection of ward heads to replace village agents, still in charge of packaged collection and forwarding.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors then proposed appointing ward heads to replace the agents, still handling consolidated collection and delivery.

sentences.zh: 台英以甲長之害，與里差同。

translations.literal: Taiying considered that the harm of ward heads was the same as village agents.
translations.idiomatic: Taiying argued that ward heads would cause the same harm as the agents had.

sentences.zh: 因集鄉紳問之曰：「巡撫命汝等舉甲長，何如？」

translations.literal: He therefore gathered rural gentry and asked them, saying: "The governor has ordered you to recommend ward heads—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the local gentry and asked, "The governor has ordered you to nominate ward heads. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 曰：「無人原充。」

translations.literal: They said: "No one is willing to serve."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "No one is willing to serve."

sentences.zh: 台英曰：「甲長所慮在不知花戶住址，汝等所慮在甲長包收。

translations.literal: Taiying said: "What ward heads fear is not knowing registered households' addresses; what you fear is ward heads' packaged collection.
translations.idiomatic: Taiying said, "Ward heads worry about not knowing where taxpayers live; you worry about ward heads collecting taxes for themselves.

sentences.zh: 吾今併戶於村，分村立冊。

translations.literal: I now combine households by village and establish registers divided by village.
translations.idiomatic: I will group households by village and compile a register for each village.

sentences.zh: 以各村糧數合一鄉，以四鄉糧數合一縣。

translations.literal: Each village's grain quotas combine into one for the township; four townships' quotas combine into one for the county.
translations.idiomatic: Each village's totals will roll up to the township, and four townships will roll up to the county.

sentences.zh: 各村納糧，就近投櫃，糧入串出，胥吏不得預。

translations.literal: Each village pays grain nearby into the cabinet; when grain enters, receipts are issued—clerks may not intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Each village will pay at the nearest office; when grain is received, receipts are issued immediately, without clerk interference.

sentences.zh: 甲長祗任催科，無昔日包收之害。

translations.literal: Ward heads only bear responsibility for urging payment, without the former harm of packaged collection.
translations.idiomatic: Ward heads will only urge payment, without the old abuses of consolidated collection.

sentences.zh: 此可行否？」

translations.literal: Can this be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Will this work?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆拜曰；

translations.literal: All bowed and said;
translations.idiomatic: All bowed and said,

translations.literal: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: "We agree."

sentences.zh: 台英曰；

translations.literal: Taiying said;
translations.idiomatic: Taiying asked,

sentences.zh: 「隱匿何由核？」

translations.literal: "How will concealment be verified?"
translations.idiomatic: "How will hidden households be found?"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「取清冊磨對，有漏，補入可耳。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "Take the clear register and compare—if there are omissions, they can be added in."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Compare against the master register; any omissions can simply be added."

sentences.zh: 曰：「虛糧何由墊？」

translations.literal: He said: "How will phantom quotas be covered?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Who will cover phantom quotas?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「虛糧無幾，有則按畝勻攤可耳。」

translations.literal: They said: "Phantom quotas are few; if any, they can be evenly apportioned by mu."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "There are few; any shortfall can be spread evenly by acreage."

sentences.zh: 數月而清冊成，糧法大定。

translations.literal: Within a few months the clear register was completed and grain law was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months the register was complete and the tax system was firmly established.

sentences.zh: 大鵬之亂，誘脅者多。

translations.literal: In Dapeng's rebellion, many were enticed and coerced.
translations.idiomatic: Many had been coerced into joining Dapeng's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 台英禁告訐，一縣獲安。

translations.literal: Taiying forbade informers; the whole county obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Taiying forbade malicious informers, and the whole county returned to peace.

sentences.zh: 以憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office due to bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，詔起用，發浙江，署台州知府，未任，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict recalled him to service; he was sent to Zhejiang and appointed acting prefect of Taizhou, but before taking office he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was recalled by imperial edict, assigned to Zhejiang as acting prefect of Taizhou, but died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: =牛樹梅=牛樹梅，字雪橋，甘肅通渭人。

translations.literal: =Niu Shumei= Niu Shumei, style name Xueqiao, was a native of Tongwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Shumei, whose style was Xueqiao, came from Tongwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，授四川彰明知縣，以不擾為治。

translations.literal: In Daoguang 21 he was a jinshi, appointed magistrate of Zhangming in Sichuan; he governed by not disturbing.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1841, he was appointed magistrate of Zhangming in Sichuan, governing on the principle of leaving the people unmolested.

sentences.zh: 決獄明慎，民隱無不達，咸愛戴之。

translations.literal: He decided cases clearly and cautiously; no popular grievance failed to reach him; all loved and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He judged cases with clarity and care, and no popular grievance failed to reach his ears; the people all loved him.

sentences.zh: 鄰縣江油匪徒何遠富糾眾劫中壩場，地與彰明之太平場相近。

translations.literal: In neighboring Jiangyou, bandit He Yuanfu gathered a crowd to plunder Zhongba market; the place bordered Zhangming's Taiping market.
translations.idiomatic: In neighboring Jiangyou, the bandit He Yuanfu gathered followers to raid Zhongba market, near Zhangming's Taiping market.

sentences.zh: 樹梅率民團御之，匪言我不踐彰明一草一木也。

translations.literal: Shumei led civilian militia to resist; the bandits said we will not tread on a single blade of grass or tree of Zhangming.
translations.idiomatic: Shumei led local militia against them. The bandits declared they would not touch a single blade of grass in Zhangming.

sentences.zh: 迨官軍擊散匪眾，遠富匿下莊白鶴洞​​，恃險負隅。

translations.literal: When government troops scattered the bandit host, Yuanfu hid in Baihe Cave at Xiazhuang, relying on dangerous terrain in obstinate resistance.
translations.idiomatic: After government troops routed the band, Yuanfu hid in Baihe Cave at Xiazhuang, holding a defensible position.

sentences.zh: 遙呼曰：「須牛青天來，吾即出。」

translations.literal: He called from afar: "Only when Niu the Blue Heaven comes will I come out."
translations.idiomatic: He shouted from a distance, "Send Niu the Just Magistrate, and I will surrender."

sentences.zh: 樹梅至，果自縛出。

translations.literal: Shumei arrived and indeed he bound himself and came out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shumei arrived, Yuanfu bound himself and came out as promised.

sentences.zh: 擢茂州直隸州知州，尋署寧遠知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Mao Prefecture directly governed, soon acting prefect of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Maozhou and soon served as acting prefect of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 地大震，全城陷沒，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: A great earthquake struck; the whole city sank, with very many dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: A great earthquake struck, swallowing the whole city and killing countless people.

sentences.zh: 樹梅壓於土，獲生。

translations.literal: Shumei was buried under earth but survived.
translations.idiomatic: Shumei was buried in the rubble but survived.

sentences.zh: 蜀人謂天留牛青天以勸善。

translations.literal: The people of Shu said Heaven left Niu the Blue Heaven to encourage goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Sichuan said Heaven had spared Niu the Just Magistrate to encourage virtue.

sentences.zh: 樹梅自咎德薄，不能庇民，益修省。

translations.literal: Shumei blamed himself that his virtue was thin and could not protect the people, and redoubled self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Shumei blamed himself for insufficient virtue that had failed to protect his people, and devoted himself still more to moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 所以賑恤災黎甚厚，民愈戴之。

translations.literal: In his relief and care for disaster victims he was very generous; the people revered him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He gave generously in relief to the afflicted, and the people revered him all the more.

sentences.zh: 父憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office due to father's bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，尚書徐澤醇薦其樸誠廉幹，詔參陝甘總督舒興阿軍事。

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 3, Minister Xu Zechun recommended his plain sincerity, integrity, and competence; an edict ordered him to participate in Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Shu Xing'a's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 Minister Xu Zechun recommended him for his honesty and capability, and he was ordered to serve on Governor-General Shu Xing'a's staff in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 八年，湖廣總督官文薦循良第一，發湖北，病未往。

translations.literal: In year 8, Huguang Governor-General Guan Wen recommended him first among exemplary officials; he was sent to Hubei but illness prevented him from going.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 Governor-General Guan Wen of Huguang ranked him first among exemplary officials and assigned him to Hubei, but illness kept him from going.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，四川總督駱秉章复薦之，擢授四川按察使，百姓喜相告曰：「牛青天再至矣！」

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 1, Sichuan Governor-General Luo Bingzhang again recommended him; he was promoted to Sichuan Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; the people joyfully told one another: "Niu the Blue Heaven comes again!"
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Governor-General Luo Bingzhang of Sichuan recommended him again, and he was appointed provincial surveillance commissioner. The people rejoiced, saying, "Niu the Just Magistrate is coming back!

sentences.zh: 三年，內召，以老病不出，主成都錦江書院。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was summoned to the capital; citing age and illness he did not go, and headed the Jinjiang Academy in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he was summoned to the capital but declined on account of age and illness, and became head of the Jinjiang Academy in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時甘肅回匪尚熾，樹梅眷念鄉里，遺書當事，論剿回宜用土勇。

translations.literal: At that time Gansu Hui bandits were still fierce; Shumei thought fondly of his homeland and left a letter to authorities, discussing that suppressing the Hui should use local braves.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebels were still active in Gansu, and Shumei, mindful of his homeland, wrote to the authorities urging that local militia be used against them.

sentences.zh: 略云：「軍興以來，劇寇皆南勇所掃蕩。

translations.literal: In summary it said: "Since military campaigns began, fierce bandits have all been swept away by southern braves.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in part, "Since the wars began, the fiercest rebels have been defeated by southern militia.

sentences.zh: 今金積堡既平，河州水土猶惡。

translations.literal: Now Jinjibao is already pacified; Hezhou's water and soil are still harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jinjibao has fallen, the terrain around Hezhou remains harsh.

sentences.zh: 若參用本省黑​​頭勇，其利有六：飽粗糲，耐冰霜，一也；

translations.literal: If one employs local "black-head" braves of the province, there are six advantages: they are sated on coarse fare and endure frost and ice—that is one;
translations.idiomatic: If local militia from the province were also employed, there would be six advantages: first, they are accustomed to coarse food and harsh winters;

sentences.zh: 有父母兄弟妻子之仇，有田園廬墓之戀，二也；

translations.literal: they have the vendetta of parents, brothers, wives, and children, and the attachment to fields, gardens, houses, and graves—that is two;
translations.idiomatic: second, they fight with personal vengeance for kin and attachment to home and ancestral graves;

sentences.zh: 給南勇半餉，即樂為用，三也；

translations.literal: given half the pay of southern braves, they are glad to be used—that is three;
translations.idiomatic: third, they would serve gladly for half southern militia pay;

sentences.zh: 無歸之民，收之，不致散為賊，四也；

translations.literal: displaced people, if recruited, would not scatter and become bandits—that is four;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, recruiting the displaced would keep them from turning bandit;

sentences.zh: 久戰狄、河一帶，不費操練，五也；

translations.literal: long fighting in the Di and He region, no need to spend on drilling—that is five;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, they already know the Di and He region from long conflict and need little training;

sentences.zh: 地勢熟習，設伏用奇，無意外虞，六也。」

translations.literal: familiar with terrain, laying ambushes and using stratagems, no unexpected worry—that is six."
translations.idiomatic: sixth, they know the terrain and can set ambushes without surprise.

sentences.zh: 後總督左宗棠採其說，主用甘軍，卒收其效。

translations.literal: Later Governor-General Zuo Zongtang adopted his view, chiefly using Gansu troops, and in the end achieved its effect.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zuo Zongtang later adopted this advice and relied chiefly on Gansu forces, with eventual success.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，歸里，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu he returned home and died, age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu era he returned home and died at eighty-four.

sentences.zh: =何曰愈=何曰愈，字云亹，廣東香山人。

translations.literal: =He Yueyu= He Yueyu, style name Yunwei, was a native of Xiangshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He Yueyu, whose style was Yunwei, came from Xiangshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 父文明，河南洧川知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: His father Wenming was magistrate of Weichuan in Henan and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenming had served as magistrate of Weichuan in Henan, where his benevolent governance won esteem.

sentences.zh: 曰愈少隨父宦，讀書勵志，有幹材。

translations.literal: Yueyu in youth followed his father in official service, studied diligently, and had executive ability.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yueyu accompanied his father in office, studied diligently, and showed administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 道光初，授四川會理州吏目。

translations.literal: Early in Daoguang he was appointed clerk of Huili Prefecture in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Daoguang era he was appointed clerk of Huili Prefecture in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 土司某桀驁，所部夷人殺漢民，知州檄曰愈往驗，以賄乞免，卻之。

translations.literal: A certain chieftain was arrogant; tribesmen under him killed Han civilians; the prefect ordered Yueyu to go investigate; they offered bribes to beg exemption and he refused.
translations.idiomatic: A rebellious native chieftain's tribesmen killed Han civilians. The prefect dispatched Yueyu to investigate; when they offered bribes to avoid prosecution, he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃率眾來劫，不為動，卒成驗而還。

translations.literal: They then led a crowd to rob him; he was unmoved, and in the end completed the investigation and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then led a mob against him, but he stood firm and completed his investigation before returning.

sentences.zh: 獄上，大吏廉得直，曰愈由是知名。

translations.literal: When the case was reported upward, high officials found the facts correct; Yueyu from this became known.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported upward, senior officials confirmed that he had been right, and Yueyu won renown.

sentences.zh: 捐升知縣，以習邊事，辦西藏糧台，三載，還補岳池縣。

translations.literal: By purchased promotion he became magistrate; because he was versed in border affairs he managed the Tibet grain depot for three years, then returned to fill the post of Yuechi County.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased promotion to magistrate, then spent three years managing the Tibet grain depot for his expertise in frontier affairs, and afterward was appointed to Yuechi County.

sentences.zh: 不畏強禦，豪右斂戢。

translations.literal: He did not fear the powerful; great families reined themselves in.
translations.idiomatic: He stood up to the powerful, and local magnates restrained themselves.

sentences.zh: 練鄉團，繕城郭，庀器械。

translations.literal: He trained local militia, repaired city walls and ramparts, and prepared weapons and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled the local militia, repaired the fortifications, and stockpiled arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 逾數年，滇匪犯岳池，後令賴所遺械以拒賊，時比張孟談之治晉陽雲。

translations.literal: After several years, Yunnan bandits invaded Yuechi; the succeeding magistrate relied on the weapons he had left behind to repel the bandits, and people at the time compared this to Zhang Mengtan's governance of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when Yunnan bandits attacked Yuechi, the magistrate who followed him used the arms Yueyu had stockpiled to hold off the enemy—a feat likened at the time to Zhang Mengtan's defense of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 調署平山，以母憂去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as acting magistrate of Pingshan, then left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act as magistrate of Pingshan, then resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，服闋，寧遠府野夷出巢焚掠，大吏檄曰愈參建昌鎮軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Xianfeng reign, when his mourning period ended, wild tribes in Ningyuan Prefecture emerged from their lairs to burn and plunder; senior officials issued an order summoning Yueyu to assist in Jianchang garrison military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, when his mourning ended, tribal peoples in Ningyuan Prefecture came out of the hills to burn and loot. Senior officials ordered Yueyu to assist in military affairs at the Jianchang garrison.

sentences.zh: 川西倮夷凡數十支，自雷波、瓘邊，滇南二十四塞，頻年肆擾。

translations.literal: The Luo tribes of western Sichuan numbered several dozen branches; from Leibo and Guanbian to the twenty-four passes of southern Yunnan, they had harassed the border year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of Luo tribal bands in western Sichuan, from Leibo and Guanbian to the twenty-four passes on the southern Yunnan frontier, had been raiding the region for years.

sentences.zh: 值西昌縣告變，曰愈馳至，眾大譁，曰：「夷傷吾人。」

translations.literal: When Xichang County reported an emergency, Yueyu rode there at speed; the crowd was greatly agitated and said: "The tribes have harmed our people."
translations.idiomatic: When Xichang County raised the alarm, Yueyu hurried there. The crowd was in an uproar: "The tribes have hurt our people."

sentences.zh: 曰愈曰：「若等平日欺夷如鹿豕，使無所控告，故釀禍。

translations.literal: Yueyu said: "You people usually bully the tribes as if they were deer and pigs, leaving them with nowhere to appeal, and so you brought this disaster upon yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yueyu replied, "You ordinarily treat the tribes like deer and pigs, denying them any way to seek redress—that is how this trouble came about.

sentences.zh: 今且少息，吾為若治之。」

translations.literal: For now calm yourselves a little; I will settle it for you."
translations.idiomatic: For the moment, calm down—I will handle this for you."

sentences.zh: 乃集兵練出不意搗夷巢，夷皆匍匐聽約束。

translations.literal: Then he assembled troops and militia and, catching them unprepared, struck at the tribal lairs; the tribes all prostrated themselves and submitted to his orders.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered soldiers and militia and, taking them by surprise, attacked their camps. The tribes submitted on their knees and accepted his terms.

sentences.zh: 漢民屋毀粟罄，夷請以山木供屋材，並貸穀為食。

translations.literal: Han Chinese households had their houses destroyed and grain exhausted; the tribes offered mountain timber for building materials and also lent grain for food.
translations.idiomatic: Han households had lost their homes and run out of grain. The tribes offered timber from the hills for rebuilding and lent grain to feed them.

sentences.zh: 曰愈諭民曰：「此見夷人具有天良，若等毋再生釁。」

translations.literal: Yueyu instructed the people, saying: "This shows the tribes still possess a conscience; you must not provoke trouble again."
translations.idiomatic: Yueyu told the people, "You can see these tribes still have a conscience. Do not pick another fight."

sentences.zh: 漢、夷遂相安。

translations.literal: Han and tribes thereupon lived in mutual peace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chinese and tribal communities thereafter lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 曰愈既益悉夷、番之情偽，山川之險隘，擬綏邊十二策，格不得上。

translations.literal: Yueyu came to understand more fully the true and false aspects of tribal and Tibetan affairs and the perilous mountain passes, and drafted twelve strategies for pacifying the frontier, but they were blocked and never reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Having learned the ins and outs of tribal and Tibetan affairs and the mountain passes, Yueyu drafted twelve proposals for pacifying the border, but they were blocked and never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，滇匪韓登鸞糾眾入會理州境，聲言與回民尋仇。

translations.literal: Before long, the Yunnan bandit Han Dengluan gathered a host and entered Huili Prefecture, claiming he sought vengeance against the Hui people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, the Yunnan rebel Han Dengluan led a force into Huili Prefecture, claiming he had come to settle a score with the Hui community.

sentences.zh: 回民疑漢民召匪，因焚民居。

translations.literal: The Hui suspected Han Chinese had summoned the bandits, and so they burned Han dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: The Hui, suspecting that Han Chinese had brought the bandits in, burned Han homes in retaliation.

sentences.zh: 曰愈率一旅往，聞流言奸細伏城內，乃下令毋閉城。

translations.literal: Yueyu led a detachment there; hearing rumors that spies were hidden inside the city, he ordered that the gates not be closed.
translations.idiomatic: Yueyu marched in with a detachment. Hearing rumors that enemy agents were hiding in the city, he ordered the gates left open.

sentences.zh: 三日後，按戶搜查，容奸細者從軍法。

translations.literal: Three days later he searched house by house; anyone who harbored spies would be dealt with under military law.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he searched house by house and declared that anyone who harbored spies would be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 越三日，城內外賊黨悉遁。

translations.literal: After another three days, all bandit sympathizers inside and outside the city had fled.
translations.idiomatic: Within three more days, every bandit accomplice inside and outside the city had fled.

sentences.zh: 曰愈曰：「吾不閉門、不遽搜者，正開其逃路耳。」

translations.literal: Yueyu said: "The reason I did not shut the gates or search at once was precisely to leave them an escape route."
translations.idiomatic: Yueyu explained, "I left the gates open and delayed the search so they would have a way to escape."

sentences.zh: 眾皆服。

translations.literal: Everyone was convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd accepted his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 遣人持榜文諭登鸞，遵示釋怨退去。

translations.literal: He sent men bearing a proclamation to instruct Dengluan; complying with the order, Dengluan released his grievances and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a proclamation to Dengluan, who obeyed, abandoned his feud, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 复持諭回民，回民曰：「昔日被水災，田廬盡沒。

translations.literal: He also carried the proclamation to the Hui people; the Hui said: "In the past we suffered a flood disaster and our fields and dwellings were entirely submerged.
translations.idiomatic: He also delivered the proclamation to the Hui, who replied, "Years ago we were hit by a flood and lost our fields and homes.

sentences.zh: 何公一騎渡​​水賑我，又為我濬河，至今無水患。

translations.literal: Master He alone crossed the water on horseback to bring us relief, and also dredged the river for us; to this day we have no flood calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Master He came alone on horseback through the water to bring us relief, then dredged the river for us—we have had no floods since.

sentences.zh: 戴德未忘，今敢不遵諭！

translations.literal: We have not forgotten that debt of gratitude; how dare we now disobey your proclamation!
translations.idiomatic: We have never forgotten his kindness. How could we refuse his word now?

sentences.zh: 違者誅之。」

translations.literal: Whoever disobeyed would be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who defied it would be executed."

sentences.zh: 自是回民亦不擾州境。

translations.literal: From then on the Hui also ceased to disturb the prefectural territory.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Hui ceased to molest the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事定，鎮府上其功，會有攘之者，遂不敘。

translations.literal: When matters were settled, the garrison and prefecture reported his achievements, but someone claimed the credit for himself, and so no record of merit was made.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, the garrison submitted a report of his merits, but a rival claimed the credit and no reward was recorded.

sentences.zh: 比粵匪犯蜀，曰愈數陳機宜，當事不能用。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese bandits invaded Sichuan, Yueyu repeatedly set forth strategic plans, but those in charge could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping rebels invaded Sichuan, Yueyu repeatedly offered strategic advice that the authorities ignored.

sentences.zh: 退居灌縣，後歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He retired to live in Guan County, later returned home, and died at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to Guan County, eventually went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 子璟，官至閩浙總督。

translations.literal: His son Jing rose to the post of Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing rose to become Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: =吳應連=吳應連，江西南城人。

translations.literal: =Wu Yinglian= Wu Yinglian was a native of Nancheng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yinglian came from Nancheng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光元年舉人，以知縣揀發四川。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the first year of the Daoguang reign, he was selected and assigned as a magistrate to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in 1821 and was assigned to Sichuan as a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷署天全、涪州、永川、安岳、蒲江、新津、綿竹、仁壽諸州縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as acting magistrate of Tianquan, Fuzhou, Yongchuan, Anyue, Pujiang, Xinjin, Mianzhu, Renshou, and other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served in acting posts at Tianquan, Fuzhou, Yongchuan, Anyue, Pujiang, Xinjin, Mianzhu, Renshou, and other Sichuan prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 補石泉，調彭縣。

translations.literal: He received a formal appointment to Shiquan, then was transferred to Peng County.
translations.idiomatic: He received a regular appointment at Shiquan and was later transferred to Peng County.

sentences.zh: 宦蜀先後二十年，所至修塘堰，濬河渠，平治水陸道塗，捕盜賊、土豪，撫災民，皆有實政。

translations.literal: In office in Sichuan for twenty years in all, wherever he went he repaired ponds and dikes, dredged rivers and canals, leveled and maintained roads and paths on land and water, captured bandits and local bullies, and comforted disaster victims—all solid achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Over two decades in Sichuan he built ponds and dikes, dredged waterways, repaired roads, captured bandits and local bullies, and relieved disaster victims wherever he served—concrete achievements every time.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，蜀匪漸熾，應連在彭縣，編團儲械，以備不虞。

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng reign, bandits in Sichuan grew increasingly fierce; Yinglian was at Peng County, organizing militia units and storing weapons to guard against unforeseen trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng era, as banditry spread in Sichuan, Yinglian organized militia and stockpiled arms against the threat while serving in Peng County.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，悍匪迭來犯，賴鄉勇保全危城，民思遺績，留殯於城內三忠祠旁，歲時祀之。

translations.literal: Before long, fierce bandits repeatedly came to attack; thanks to the local militia the endangered city was preserved. The people recalled his legacy, kept his coffin beside the Three Loyalty Shrine inside the city, and offered sacrifices to him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Soon fierce bandits attacked repeatedly; the militia he had organized saved the city. Grateful townspeople kept his coffin beside the Three Loyalty Shrine inside the walls and honored him with seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 涪州、安岳、永川、石泉、仁壽先後請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Fuzhou, Anyue, Yongchuan, Shiquan, and Renshou successively petitioned for him to be enshrined in the shrine of distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou, Anyue, Yongchuan, Shiquan, and Renshou each petitioned to enshrine him in their local shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: =劉秉琳=劉秉琳，字昆圃，湖北黃安人。

translations.literal: =Liu Binglin= Liu Binglin, style name Kunpu, was a native of Huang'an in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Binglin, whose style was Kunpu, came from Huang'an in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，授順天寶坻知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of the Xianfeng reign, he was appointed magistrate of Baodi in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1852 and was appointed magistrate of Baodi in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 持躬清苦，恤孤寡，懲豪猾，悉去雜派及榷酤贏餘者。

translations.literal: He kept himself upright and frugal, cared for orphans and widows, punished the powerful and cunning, and abolished all miscellaneous levies and surplus profits from the salt and liquor monopolies.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly, cared for orphans and widows, punished local bullies, and abolished every miscellaneous levy and monopoly surcharge.

sentences.zh: 索倫兵伐民墓樹，縱馬躪田禾，反誣村民縶其馬，秉琳力爭得直。

translations.literal: Solon soldiers cut down trees at commoners' graves and let their horses trample the crops, then falsely accused the villagers of seizing their horses; Binglin argued forcefully and obtained justice.
translations.idiomatic: Solon soldiers cut down trees in village graveyards and let their horses trample crops, then falsely accused the villagers of seizing their horses. Binglin fought the case and won justice for them.

sentences.zh: 蝗起，督民自捕，集貲購之，被蝗者得錢以代賑，且免踐田苗。

translations.literal: When locusts appeared, he ordered the people to catch them themselves, collected funds to purchase them, so those afflicted by locusts received money in lieu of relief grain and the crops were spared from being trampled.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts swarmed, he organized villagers to catch them and paid cash bounties so afflicted households could eat without trampling crops for relief grain.

sentences.zh: 遷宛平京縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wanping, a capital county.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wanping, one of the capital counties.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍犯京師，秉琳奉檄赴營議犒，納刀鞾中，慮以非禮相加，義不受辱。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied armies invaded the capital; Binglin received an order to go to the enemy camp to discuss consolation gifts, concealed a knife in his boot, fearing ill treatment, resolved that on principle he would not suffer disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, when Anglo-French forces reached Beijing, Binglin was ordered to the enemy camp to negotiate tribute gifts. He hid a knife in his boot, ready to die rather than accept humiliation.

sentences.zh: 抗論無少屈，犒具皆如議。

translations.literal: He debated without yielding in the least, and the consolation gifts were all provided as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He stood his ground without yielding, and every item of tribute was supplied as agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon after he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 穆宗登極，有密薦者，復至直隸，署任丘。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne, someone secretly recommended him; he returned to Zhili and served as acting magistrate of Renqiu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tongzhi Emperor came to the throne, a secret recommendation brought him back to Zhili as acting magistrate of Renqiu.

sentences.zh: 民以驛車為累，籌貲招僱，永除其害。

translations.literal: The people were burdened by courier wagons; he raised funds to hire carriers permanently and removed that hardship forever.
translations.idiomatic: Courier wagons had become a burden on the people; he raised funds to hire permanent carriers and ended the abuse for good.

sentences.zh: 擢深州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Shenzhou Direct Prefecture in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Shenzhou Prefecture in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻匪張總愚竄畿輔，且至。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Nian bandit Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region and was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 the Nian rebel Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region and was nearing the city.

sentences.zh: 人勸其眷屬可避，秉琳曰：「吾家人皆食祿者，義不可去。」

translations.literal: People advised that his family could flee; Binglin said: "My household lives on official salaries; on principle we cannot leave."
translations.idiomatic: When others urged his family to flee, Binglin said, "We all live on the state's salary—we cannot abandon our post."

sentences.zh: 授兵登陴，鄉民及鄰境聞之，咸挈入保，至十餘萬人。

translations.literal: He issued arms and mounted the walls; villagers and people from neighboring districts, hearing of this, all brought their families in for protection, reaching more than one hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He armed the defenders and took to the walls. Villagers and people from neighboring districts heard and streamed inside for protection—more than a hundred thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 嬰城四十餘日，賊圍之，不破。

translations.literal: They defended the city for more than forty days; the bandits besieged it but could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: The city held for more than forty days under siege without falling.

sentences.zh: 秉琳上書統帥，言賊入滹沱，河套勢益蹙，宜兜圍急擊，緩將偷渡東竄。

translations.literal: Binglin wrote to the commander-in-chief, saying that if the bandits entered the Hutuo River the terrain in the river bend would tighten further; they should be encircled and struck urgently—if delayed, the bandits would slip across and flee east.
translations.idiomatic: Binglin wrote the commander warning that once the rebels crossed the Hutuo the river bend would trap them; he urged an immediate encirclement, warning that delay would let them slip east across the river.

sentences.zh: 卒如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it happened just as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 寇平，優敘。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he received superior commendation for merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he received an exceptional merit citation.

sentences.zh: 州地多斥鹵，民以鹽為恆產，課與常賦埒，水旱不得報災，非漉鹽無以應正供。

translations.literal: Much of the prefecture's land was saline; the people's constant livelihood was salt production; the salt tax equaled the regular land tax; in flood or drought they could not report disaster; without extracting salt they could not meet official obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the prefecture was saline wasteland where people relied on salt-making; the salt levy matched regular taxes, and without panning salt they could not pay their dues—even in flood or drought they could not claim disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 秉琳議官銷法，以杜私販，民悅服。

translations.literal: Binglin proposed a government marketing method to stop private trafficking; the people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Binglin introduced government sales of salt to stop illegal trade, and the people accepted it willingly.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢正定知府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to prefect of Zhengding.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he was promoted to prefect of Zhengding.

sentences.zh: 滹沱溢，發所儲兵米以賑。

translations.literal: When the Hutuo overflowed, he released stored military grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hutuo flooded, he opened military grain stores for relief.

sentences.zh: 築曹馬口、回水、斜角三堤，水不齧城，民用安集。

translations.literal: He built three dikes at Caomakou, Huishui, and Xiejiao; the water no longer gnawed at the city, and the people's livelihoods were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes at Caomakou, Huishui, and Xiejiao so floodwaters no longer threatened the city and the people could settle in safety.

sentences.zh: 郡與山西接壤，固關守弁，苛稅煤鐵，商販委物於路，聚眾上訴。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered Shanxi; the garrison officer at Guguan imposed harsh taxes on coal and iron; merchants abandoned their goods on the road and gathered in a crowd to petition higher authority.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered Shanxi; the officer at Guguan Pass levied exorbitant taxes on coal and iron until merchants abandoned goods on the road and marched en masse to protest.

sentences.zh: 秉琳往解散，除其重徵。

translations.literal: Binglin went and dispersed them, abolishing the heavy levies.
translations.idiomatic: Binglin went out, dispersed the crowd, and abolished the oppressive taxes.

sentences.zh: 鎮將獲盜三，已誣服，秉琳鞫之，乃兵挾負博嫌，栽贓刑逼，以成其獄，釋三人者而重懲其兵。

translations.literal: The garrison general had captured three bandits who had already falsely confessed under coercion; Binglin tried the case and found that soldiers, bearing a grudge over gambling debts, had planted evidence and tortured them to fabricate the case; he released the three men and severely punished the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander had seized three men who had already confessed under torture. Binglin retried the case, found soldiers had framed them over gambling debts, released the three, and severely punished the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，擢天津河間道，兼轄南運河工。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Guangxu reign he was promoted to the Tianjin-Hejian circuit, also overseeing works on the South Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was promoted to the Tianjin-Hejian circuit and put in charge of South Grand Canal projects.

sentences.zh: 請復歲修銀額，河兵口食足，乃無偷減工料之弊。

translations.literal: He requested restoration of the annual repair silver quota; once the canal laborers' rations were sufficient, there was no longer the abuse of skimping on materials and work.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the annual repair budget so canal workers were fully fed, eliminating the old practice of skimming materials and labor.

sentences.zh: 築中亭河北堤，涸出腴田千餘頃。

translations.literal: He built the north bank dike of the Zhongting River, reclaiming more than a thousand qing of fertile fields from dried land.
translations.idiomatic: He built the north bank dike on the Zhongting River, reclaiming more than a thousand qing of fertile land.

sentences.zh: 時方旱，流民集天津，設粥廠，躬親其事，所活甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time there was drought; displaced people gathered at Tianjin; he set up gruel kitchens and personally attended to the work; a great many were kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought, refugees flooded Tianjin; he opened soup kitchens and personally oversaw relief, saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 嘗太息曰：「哺飢衣寒，救荒末策也。

translations.literal: He once sighed and said: "Feeding the hungry and clothing the cold—relief is the least of strategies for famine.
translations.idiomatic: He once sighed, "Feeding the hungry is only the last resort in a famine.

sentences.zh: 本計當於河渠書、農桑譜中求之。」

translations.literal: The fundamental plan ought to be sought in books on rivers and canals and treatises on farming and sericulture."
translations.idiomatic: The real answer lies in books on waterworks and manuals of farming and sericulture."

sentences.zh: 四年，乞病歸，數年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home; several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he retired on grounds of illness; he died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 同治初年，軍事漸定，始課吏治。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi reign, as military affairs gradually settled, assessment of official governance began.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi era, as fighting subsided, the court began to hold officials accountable for good governance.

sentences.zh: 大學士曾國籓為直隸總督，下車即舉賢員，如李文敏、任道鎔、李秉衡，後並至巡撫。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan served as Governor-General of Zhili; as soon as he took office he recommended worthy officials such as Li Wenmin, Ren Daorong, and Li Bingheng, who all later rose to provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor-General of Zhili, Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan immediately recommended able men such as Li Wenmin, Ren Daorong, and Li Bingheng—all of whom later became provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 秉琳及陳崇砥、夏子齡、蕭世本諸人，治行皆卓著，當時風氣為之一振雲。

translations.literal: Binglin and Chen Chongdi, Xia Ziling, Xiao Shiben, and others all had outstanding records in governance, and the prevailing climate was thereby greatly invigorated.
translations.idiomatic: Binglin, Chen Chongdi, Xia Ziling, Xiao Shiben, and others all achieved outstanding records in office, and official morale across the region sharply improved.

sentences.zh: 崇砥，字亦香，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Chongdi, style name Yixiang, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chongdi, whose style was Yixiang, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年舉人，咸豐三年，大挑知縣，發直隸，授獻縣。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the twenty-fifth year of the Daoguang reign, in the third year of Xianfeng he was selected in the great allotment for magistrates, assigned to Zhili, and appointed magistrate of Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exam in 1845. In 1853 he was selected as a magistrate, assigned to Zhili, and appointed to Xian County.

sentences.zh: 盜賊充斥，嚴緝捕，渠魁多就擒。

translations.literal: Bandits swarmed the region; he strictly pursued arrests, and many ringleaders were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rampant; he cracked down hard and captured most of the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 治鄉團十六區，合千五百人，分班輪值，邑以有備。

translations.literal: He organized local militia in sixteen districts totaling fifteen hundred men, with rotating shifts on duty, and the county thereby had defenses in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: He organized sixteen militia districts with fifteen hundred men on rotating shifts, leaving the county well defended.

sentences.zh: 捻匪張錫珠擾畿輔，崇砥開城納逃亡，誓眾效死。

translations.literal: The Nian bandit Zhang Xizhu harassed the capital region; Chongdi opened the city gates to admit refugees and swore the people to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian rebel Zhang Xizhu ravaged the capital region, Chongdi opened the gates to refugees and pledged the city to fight to the last.

sentences.zh: 縣境臧家橋為通衢，河間守欲毀橋阻賊，崇砥謂：「方宜安集難民，遙為聲援，豈可夷險示弱？

translations.literal: Zangjia Bridge in the county was a major thoroughfare; the prefect of Hejian wanted to destroy the bridge to block the bandits; Chongdi said: "Just now we ought to settle refugees and serve as distant support—how can we level defenses and show weakness?
translations.idiomatic: Zangjia Bridge was a vital crossing in the county. The Hejian prefect wanted to destroy it to block the rebels. Chongdi objected, "We should be sheltering refugees and standing as a rear guard—how can we tear down our defenses and show weakness?

sentences.zh: 且委東鄉於賊，非計也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to abandon the eastern part of the county to the bandits is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: And abandoning the eastern countryside to the enemy is no strategy at all."

sentences.zh: 竟不毀橋，賊旋引去。

translations.literal: In the end the bridge was not destroyed, and the bandits soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the bridge intact, and the rebels soon moved on.

sentences.zh: 大學士祁俊藻疏薦之，擢保定府同知，筦水利。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Qi Junzao memorialized recommending him; he was promoted to sub-prefect of Baoding Prefecture and put in charge of waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Qi Junzao recommended him for promotion to sub-prefect of Baoding Prefecture in charge of water control.

sentences.zh: 崇砥以府河港汊紛歧，苦易淤。

translations.literal: Chongdi found that the prefectural river had many branching channels and was difficult because it silted easily.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdi found Baoding's rivers and tributaries branched in every direction and silted up easily.

sentences.zh: 設水志，增夫役、器具，以時汰淤。

translations.literal: He established water registers, increased laborers and equipment, and dredged silt on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: He kept water registers, added labor and equipment, and dredged on a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 商船打壩阻水，為設壩船，給板椿，過淺構橋咸稱便。

translations.literal: Merchant boats damming the flow obstructed the water; he set up dam boats, supplied planks and piles, and where shallows required temporary bridges—all were called convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant boats that blocked the channel with dams were given dam boats, planks, and piles; where waters ran shallow he built temporary bridges—all to universal approval.

sentences.zh: 同治八年，署大名知府，兵亂時，民多築寨堡自衛，後事定，浸至藏奸抗官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Tongzhi reign he served as acting prefect of Daming; during the military turmoil the people had built stockaded forts for self-defense; afterward, when affairs settled, these gradually came to harbor criminals and resist officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he served as acting prefect of Daming. During the wars people had built fortresses for self-defense; after peace returned, those strongholds increasingly sheltered criminals and defied officials.

sentences.zh: 崇砥親履勘，收繳軍械，易正紳司之，澆風漸息。

translations.literal: Chongdi personally went to inspect on foot, confiscated weapons, replaced the stewards with upright gentry, and the corrupt practices gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdi inspected every site in person, confiscated weapons, and put respectable gentry in charge—the lawlessness slowly subsided.

sentences.zh: 畿南久苦旱，賑難普及，崇砥議有田十畝以上者不賑；

translations.literal: Southern Zhili had long suffered drought; relief could not reach everyone; Chongdi proposed that those with more than ten mu of land would not receive relief;
translations.idiomatic: Southern Zhili had endured a long drought and relief could not reach everyone. Chongdi ruled that anyone holding more than ten mu of land would be ineligible;

sentences.zh: 極貧，大口錢千，小口半之，壯者不給。

translations.literal: for the extremely poor, a thousand cash per adult mouth, half that for children, able-bodied men not given relief.
translations.idiomatic: the desperately poor would receive a thousand cash per adult and half that for children; able-bodied men received nothing.

sentences.zh: 先編保甲，造細冊，不曰賑而曰貸。

translations.literal: First he compiled household registers through the baojia system and made detailed rolls, calling it not relief but a loan.
translations.idiomatic: He registered households through the baojia system and recorded aid as loans rather than charity.

sentences.zh: 事畢，奏請蠲貸，民安之。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he memorialized requesting cancellation of the loans; the people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed he petitioned to forgive the loans, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 南樂縣民抗徭聚眾，令告變。

translations.literal: People in Nanle County resisted corvée labor and gathered in a crowd; the magistrate reported an emergency.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanle County the people resisted corvée duty and massed in protest; the local magistrate raised the alarm.

sentences.zh: 崇砥輕騎往，平其輕重，眾歡然輸納。

translations.literal: Chongdi went lightly mounted, balanced the burdens fairly, and the crowd gladly paid their dues.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdi rode out alone, adjusted the burdens fairly, and the crowd paid up willingly.

sentences.zh: 副將駐兵獻縣，兵不戢，鄉團疑其匪也，戕副將。

translations.literal: A vice commander was garrisoned at Xian County; his soldiers were undisciplined; the local militia suspected them of being bandits and killed the vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: A vice commander and his troops were stationed in Xian County; when his undisciplined soldiers were mistaken for bandits, the local militia killed the officer.

sentences.zh: 既而知誤，畏罪，眾聚不散。

translations.literal: When they afterward learned it was a mistake, fearing punishment, the crowd assembled and would not disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Once they realized their mistake, fear of punishment kept the crowd from dispersing.

sentences.zh: 檄崇砥往治，令縛首禍者，脅從皆免之。

translations.literal: An order was issued for Chongdi to go and settle it; he commanded that the ringleaders be bound, while those coerced into joining were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chongdi was ordered to the scene; he had the ringleaders bound and pardoned everyone who had followed under duress.

sentences.zh: 調署順德府，尋擢河間知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as acting prefect of Shunde Prefecture, and soon promoted to prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act as prefect of Shunde and soon promoted to prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 河間素多訟，崇砥剋期審結，數決疑獄，期年而清。

translations.literal: Hejian had always had many lawsuits; Chongdi set deadlines to try and conclude cases, repeatedly resolved doubtful cases, and within a year the docket was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian had long been awash in litigation, but Chongdi imposed firm deadlines on every case, cleared a string of doubtful convictions, and within a year the courts were clean.

sentences.zh: 滹沱下游為災，崇砥請築古洋河堤，自獻縣至肅寧六十里。

translations.literal: The lower reaches of the Hutuo suffered flooding; Chongdi requested the construction of dikes on the Gu Yang River, sixty li from Xian County to Suning.
translations.idiomatic: When flooding ravaged the lower Hutuo, Chongdi petitioned to build dikes along the Gu Yang River for sixty li from Xian County to Suning.

sentences.zh: 於蔡家橋作堤防支流，開溝六千丈，以資宣洩。

translations.literal: At Caijia Bridge he built dikes to contain tributary streams and dug canals six thousand zhang long to aid discharge.
translations.idiomatic: At Caijia Bridge he erected dikes against side streams and dug six thousand zhang of channels to carry floodwater off.

sentences.zh: 自馮家村至高旦口，造橋建徬，防子牙河暴漲。

translations.literal: From Fengjia Village to Gaodankou he built bridges and embankments to guard against sudden rises of the Ziya River.
translations.idiomatic: From Fengjia Village to Gaodankou he built bridges and levees to hold back sudden surges of the Ziya River.

sentences.zh: 於是古洋通流，近地皆大稔。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Gu Yang flowed freely, and nearby lands all enjoyed great harvests.
translations.idiomatic: The Gu Yang soon ran freely again, and the surrounding countryside saw bumper harvests.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，卒於官，祀名宦。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Guangxu reign he died in office and was enshrined in the shrine of distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the first year of the Guangxu reign and was honored in the shrine of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 夏子齡，字百初，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Xia Ziling, style name Baichu, was a native of Jiangyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Ziling, whose style was Baichu, came from Jiangyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年，會試第一，成進士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of the Daoguang reign he placed first in the metropolitan examination and became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Daoguang reign he topped the metropolitan examination and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 初官禮部主事，任事果決，尚氣節。

translations.literal: His first post was as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites; he was resolute in handling affairs and prized moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, handling business with brisk decision and a strong sense of principle.

sentences.zh: 庫丁賄當事，請準捐考，力持駁議，時稱之。

translations.literal: Treasury clerks bribed those in charge and asked that donation examinations be permitted; he strenuously upheld the objection and was praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When treasury clerks bribed officials to permit purchased examination slots, he held firm in opposing the scheme, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 改授河南汲縣知縣，勤聽訟，嚴治盜，遇事持大體。

translations.literal: Reappointed as magistrate of Jixian in Henan, he diligently heard lawsuits, strictly punished thieves, and when handling affairs upheld the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned as magistrate of Jixian in Henan, he heard cases diligently, cracked down on bandits, and always kept sight of the larger public interest.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，詔求人才，巡撫潘鐸特薦之，會母憂去官。

translations.literal: Early in the Xianfeng reign, an edict sought talented men; Governor Pan Duo specially recommended him, but he chanced to leave office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign the throne called for capable men and Governor Pan Duo singled him out for recommendation, but he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授直隸深澤，調饒陽。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed to Shenze in Zhili and later transferred to Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was posted to Shenze in Zhili and later moved to Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 比歲旱蝗，盜劫肆擾，選健役百人，教以技擊，更番直。

translations.literal: For several years running there were drought and locusts, and robbers rampaged; he selected a hundred strong runners, taught them martial arts, and rotated them on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Years of drought and locusts had unleashed rampant banditry; he picked a hundred strong runners, trained them in hand-to-hand combat, and kept them on rotating watch.

sentences.zh: 有事，雖午夜立率以出，捕劇盜幾盡。

translations.literal: When an incident arose, even at midnight he would immediately lead them out; he captured nearly all the chief robbers.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sign of trouble he would lead them out himself, even at midnight, and nearly wiped out the worst gangs.

sentences.zh: 分境內團練為八區，輪期會操，久之皆可用。

translations.literal: He divided the local militia within his jurisdiction into eight districts, rotating periodic drill assemblies; in time all became usable troops.
translations.idiomatic: He split the county militia into eight districts with rotating drill sessions, and before long they were fit for real service.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍入京師，畿南土匪蜂起，冀州王洛悅，河間劉四、賈漋等，各麕集千人，連擾郡邑。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied armies entered the capital; bandits rose everywhere south of the capital region; Wang Luoyue of Jizhou, Liu Si and Jia Zhang of Hejian, and others each gathered a thousand men and successively harassed counties and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Anglo-French forces entered Beijing and brigands flared across southern Zhili; Wang Luoyue of Jizhou and Liu Si and Jia Zhang of Hejian each massed a thousand men and raided one county seat after another.

sentences.zh: 子齡率團勇迎擊境上，斬獲數百。

translations.literal: Ziling led the militia to meet and attack them at the border, killing and capturing several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Ziling took the militia to the border and routed them, killing or capturing several hundred.

sentences.zh: 劉四受創遁，王洛悅聞風驚潰。

translations.literal: Liu Si was wounded and fled; hearing the news, Wang Luoyue was frightened and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Si was wounded and escaped; at the news Wang Luoyue's band panicked and broke apart.

sentences.zh: 劉四等尋於他縣被擒伏法，王洛悅亦就撫。

translations.literal: Liu Si and others were soon captured in another county and executed according to law; Wang Luoyue also submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Si and the others were soon seized in another county and executed; Wang Luoyue also accepted government terms and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 事平，優敘。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he received preferential reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored he was rewarded for his service.

sentences.zh: 縣舊為滹沱所經，北徙已久。

translations.literal: The county had formerly been traversed by the Hutuo, which had shifted north long before.
translations.idiomatic: The Hutuo had once run through the county, but it had shifted northward long ago.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上游決溢，水驟至，近郊為澤國。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an upstream breach caused overflow; water arrived suddenly and the near suburbs became a flooded country.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a breach upstream sent floodwater racing down, turning the suburbs into a vast shallow lake.

sentences.zh: 訪尋故道，濬老澗溝，上接安平境，下入獻縣之廉頗窪，以資宣洩。

translations.literal: He searched out the old channel, dredged the Old Stream Gully, connected upward with the border of Anping and descended into Lianpo Hollow in Xian County, to aid discharge.
translations.idiomatic: He traced the old riverbed, dredged the Old Stream Gully from Anping down to Lianpo Hollow in Xian County, and opened a path for the flood to drain away.

sentences.zh: 次年，水復至，暢流不為患。

translations.literal: The next year when water came again, it flowed freely without causing harm.
translations.idiomatic: The next year when the waters rose again, they passed through freely and did no damage.

sentences.zh: 城西官道沖刷成河，建長橋五十丈，民便之。

translations.literal: The official road west of the city was washed out into a river; he built a long bridge fifty zhang in length, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Flood erosion had cut the west road into a channel; he built a fifty-zhang bridge there, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 遷宛平京縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wanping, the capital county.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wanping, the metropolitan county.

sentences.zh: 擢易州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Yizhou Direct Prefecture in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Yizhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 西陵在州境，故事，護陵俸餉及祭品、牛羊、芻豆，州領帑給之。

translations.literal: The Western Tombs were within the prefecture; by precedent the prefecture received treasury funds and distributed the guard stipends and sacrificial offerings, cattle, sheep, fodder, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Tombs lay within his jurisdiction; by custom the prefecture drew treasury funds to pay the tomb guards and supply the ritual offerings, livestock, fodder, and grain.

sentences.zh: 陵員與州吏因緣為侵蝕，數煩朝使察治。

translations.literal: Tomb personnel and prefectural clerks seized opportunities to embezzle, repeatedly requiring imperial envoys to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb staff and prefectural clerks had long skimmed the funds, and imperial investigators had been sent repeatedly to clean up the abuses.

sentences.zh: 子齡與守陵大臣議訂章程，弊去泰甚，始相安焉。

translations.literal: Ziling discussed and set regulations with the minister guarding the tombs; abuses were removed to a very great degree, and only then did matters settle peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Ziling worked out new regulations with the tomb minister, cut the worst abuses, and at last brought the arrangement under control.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，奸民聚眾擾大戶，立杖斃煽眾者。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, wicked persons gathered crowds to harass wealthy households; he immediately had those inciting the mob beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year agitators rallied mobs against wealthy families; he had the ringleaders beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 勸捐賑恤，災不為害。

translations.literal: He urged charitable donations for relief; the disaster did not become harmful.
translations.idiomatic: He organized relief donations, and the drought never became a catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，河北馬賊起，擾及鄰境，募勇治團如饒陽時，匪懾其名不敢犯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Tongzhi reign horse bandits rose in northern Hebei and harassed neighboring borders; he recruited braves and organized militia as he had at Raoyang, and the bandits feared his name and did not dare violate his territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi, mounted bandits spread from northern Hebei into neighboring counties; he raised militia as he had at Raoyang, and the outlaws feared his name too much to raid his territory.

sentences.zh: 次年，捻匪竄擾畿輔，守要隘，清內匪，防軍久駐，有淫掠者，立斬以徇，闔境肅然。

translations.literal: The next year Nian bandits raided the capital region; he guarded strategic passes, cleared internal bandits; long-stationed defensive troops had some who raped and plundered—he immediately beheaded them as a warning, and the whole territory became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Nian raiders swept the capital approaches; he held the key passes and rooted out local bandits, and when garrison troops turned to looting he had offenders beheaded at once—the whole prefecture fell quiet.

sentences.zh: 論功，晉秩知府。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted in rank to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for his service, he was promoted to the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 美利堅教會私購民居為耶蘇堂，執條約與爭。

translations.literal: An American church privately purchased a dwelling as a Jesuit chapel; he cited treaty provisions and contested the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When an American mission bought a private house for a chapel, he contested the sale on treaty grounds.

sentences.zh: 以其無遊歷執照，購屋未先告，州境附近陵寢，有關風水，皆與約背，竟退價撤契，且杜其後至。

translations.literal: Because they had no travel permit, had not announced the purchase in advance, and the prefecture bordered the tombs in a matter affecting geomantic concerns—all contrary to treaty—he ultimately returned the price, revoked the deed, and blocked further attempts.
translations.idiomatic: They had no travel permit, had not notified the authorities before buying, and the site lay too close to the imperial tombs for geomantic reasons—in each case a treaty violation—so he forced them to return the price, cancel the deed, and blocked any repeat attempt.

sentences.zh: 尋請離任，以知府候補。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave from office and awaited assignment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to leave office and waited for a prefectural appointment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: 易州、饒陽並祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Both Yizhou and Raoyang enshrined him in the shrine of distinguished officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was honored in the shrines of eminent officials in both Yizhou and Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 子詒鈺，官永年​​知縣，亦以廉平稱，有治績。

translations.literal: His son Yiyu served as magistrate of Yongnian and was also praised for integrity and fairness, with administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiyu served as magistrate of Yongnian and likewise earned a reputation for honest, fair government.

sentences.zh: 世本，字廉甫，四川富順人。

translations.literal: Shiben, style name Lianfu, was a native of Fushun in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiben, whose style was Lianfu, came from Fushun in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授刑部主事，改直隸知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Tongzhi, selected as a Hanlin bachelor, upon leaving the academy appointed secretary of the Ministry of Punishments, then transferred to magistrate in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi in the second year of Tongzhi and serving as a Hanlin bachelor, he became a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and then a magistrate in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 先在籍治團練有聲，曾國籓蒞直隸，闢為幕僚。

translations.literal: Previously while at home he had gained repute for organizing local militia; when Zeng Guofan arrived in Zhili he recruited him as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: He had already made a name organizing home-district militia; when Zeng Guofan took charge of Zhili he brought Shiben onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 九年，天津民、教相閧，斃法國領事，幾肇大釁。

translations.literal: In the ninth year commoners and Christians clashed in Tianjin; the French consul was killed, nearly provoking a major incident.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year rioters in Tianjin killed the French consul in a clash between townspeople and Christians, nearly sparking a major diplomatic crisis.

sentences.zh: 遂以世本署天津縣，尋實授。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shiben was appointed acting magistrate of Tianjin County, soon receiving full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shiben was named acting magistrate of Tianjin and soon received the permanent post.

sentences.zh: 天津民悍好鬥，鍋夥匪動為地方害，世本嚴懲之。

translations.literal: The people of Tianjin were fierce and quarrelsome; pot-gang bandits frequently harmed the locality; Shiben punished them severely.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin folk were fierce and quick to fight; the "pot gangs" were a chronic scourge, and Shiben cracked down on them hard.

sentences.zh: 地為通商大埠，訟獄殷繁，世本手批口鞫，斷決如神。

translations.literal: The place was a major treaty port; lawsuits and cases were extremely numerous; Shiben wrote judgments by hand and questioned orally, deciding cases as if divinely inspired.
translations.idiomatic: As a major treaty port Tianjin was buried in litigation; Shiben wrote his own judgments, questioned suspects himself, and resolved cases with uncanny speed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，父憂去。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he left upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，仍補天津。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was still assigned to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，災

translations.literal: In a year of drought, disaster
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year, disaster struck

sentences.zh: 黎就食萬數，給粥、施醫無失所。

translations.literal: Ten thousands of people came for food; grain porridge was given and medicine dispensed without anyone being neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of refugees came for relief; he fed them porridge and provided medical care so that none went unserved.

sentences.zh: 調清苑，擢遵化直隸州知州，復以母憂去。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qingyuan, promoted to prefect of Zunhua Direct Prefecture in Zhili, again left upon mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Qingyuan, promoted to prefect of Zunhua in Zhili, and again left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以知府候補，筦天津守望局。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he awaited assignment as prefect and managed the Tianjin night-watch office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he waited for a prefectural posting and ran Tianjin's night-watch bureau.

sentences.zh: 捕誅大盜王洛八、謝昆，海道肅清。

translations.literal: He captured and executed the great bandits Wang Luoba and Xie Kun, and the sea routes were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed the bandit leaders Wang Luoba and Xie Kun, and the coastal routes were cleared.

sentences.zh: 倡修運河堤，以免水患。

translations.literal: He advocated repairing the Grand Canal dikes to avoid flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed to rebuild the Grand Canal embankments against flooding.

sentences.zh: 疏瀦龍河故道，開范家堤及石碑河、宣惠河、金沙嶺下水道四十餘裡。

translations.literal: He dredged the old channel of the Zhulong River, opened the Fan Family Dike and the Shibei, Xuanhui, and Jinshaling Downstream channels for over forty li.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the old Zhulong Riverbed and opened the Fan Family Dike plus more than forty li of channels along the Shibei, Xuanhui, and Jinshaling downstream routes.

sentences.zh: 皆藉賑興工，民利賴之。
