translations.literal: All were undertaken by using relief funds to launch projects; the people relied on the benefits.
translations.idiomatic: He funded the work out of relief budgets, and the people gained lasting benefit from it.

sentences.zh: 署天津、正定兩府。

translations.literal: He served as acting prefect of both Tianjin and Zhengding prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as prefect of both Tianjin and Zhengding.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 附祀曾國籓祠。

translations.literal: He was granted attached enshrinement in Zeng Guofan's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was honored with a place in Zeng Guofan's memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: =李炳濤=李炳濤，字秋槎，河南河內人。

translations.literal: =Li Bingtao= Li Bingtao, style name Qiucha, was a native of Henei in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingtao, whose style was Qiucha, came from Henei in Henan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，就職州判，謁曾國籓於軍中，尋佐皖軍營務。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng era he took office as subprefect, called on Zeng Guofan in the army, and soon assisted in Anhui army camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng era he entered service as a subprefect, sought out Zeng Guofan in the field, and soon took charge of camp administration for the Anhui forces.

sentences.zh: 能調和將士，積功晉同知，留安徽。

translations.literal: Able to harmonize officers and soldiers, he accumulated merit and was promoted to sub-prefect, remaining in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at keeping officers and men working together, he earned steady promotions to sub-prefect and stayed on in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，國籓北征捻匪，炳濤上書言四事：「一，專責防堵，以嚴分竄；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, when Guofan marched north against the Nian bandits, Bingtao submitted a memorial setting forth four points: "First, assign sole responsibility for blocking and sealing off, to tighten control over scattered raids;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi, as Guofan marched north against the Nian, Bingtao submitted a memorial with four proposals: "First, concentrate responsibility for blocking escape routes so raiders cannot slip through in small bands;

sentences.zh: 一，聯絡民團，以孤賊勢；

translations.literal: Second, coordinate with local militia to isolate the bandits' strength;
translations.idiomatic: Second, coordinate with local militia to cut the bandits off from support;

sentences.zh: 一，設局開荒，以資解散；

translations.literal: Third, establish bureaus to open wasteland, to provide means for disbandment;
translations.idiomatic: Third, set up land-reclamation offices to give surrendered men a livelihood;

sentences.zh: 一，多備火器，以奪賊長。」

translations.literal: Fourth, prepare more firearms, to seize the bandits' advantage in length."
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, stock more firearms to neutralize the bandits' reach."

sentences.zh: 國籓頗採其言。

translations.literal: Guofan largely adopted his recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan largely adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 檄查亳州圩，炳濤微服出入，盡得諸匪徒姓名及蠹役胡採林通匪虐民狀，誘採林誅之，竿其首，一州驚歡。

translations.literal: Ordered to inspect the Bozhou stockades, Bingtao went in and out in plain clothes, fully learning the names of all bandits and the conduct of the corrupt runner Hu Cailin in colluding with bandits and oppressing the people; he lured Cailin out and executed him, displayed his head on a pole, and the whole prefecture was astonished and rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect the Bozhou stockades, Bingtao moved among them in disguise until he had every bandit's name and proof that the corrupt runner Hu Cailin was shielding outlaws and preying on the people; he lured Cailin out and executed him, put his head on display, and the whole prefecture erupted in relief.

sentences.zh: 自是訟獄者咸取決於炳濤。

translations.literal: From then on all who brought lawsuits and cases looked to Bingtao for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From then on litigants looked to Bingtao to settle their cases.

sentences.zh: 按圩查閱，立條教，別良莠，戮悍賊二百，予自新者三千。

translations.literal: He inspected the stockades in turn, established regulations, distinguished good from bad, executed two hundred fierce bandits, and granted renewal to three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the stockades, issued new rules, sorted the trustworthy from the criminal, executed two hundred hardened bandits, and gave three thousand men a chance to reform.

sentences.zh: 期年而俗變，無盜竊者。

translations.literal: Within a year customs changed, and there were no thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year local habits had changed and theft disappeared.

sentences.zh: 五年，捻匪竄州境，曉諸圩以大義，雖與寇有親故者，無敢出應，捻匪引去。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Nian bandits raided into the prefecture; he instructed all the stockades in the larger moral principle, and even those with kin ties to the raiders did not dare go out to respond; the Nian bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Nian raiders entered the prefecture; he appealed to every stockade on grounds of public duty, and even men with relatives among the bandits dared not join them—the Nian withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六年，署蒙城縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as acting magistrate of Mengcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as acting magistrate of Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 蒙、亳接壤，瘠苦尤甚。

translations.literal: Mengcheng and Bozhou bordered each other, and poverty there was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcheng bordered Bozhou, and the land there was especially poor and hard-pressed.

sentences.zh: 炳濤耡強梗，撫良懦，振興書院，弦誦聲作。

translations.literal: Bingtao uprooted the violent and stubborn, comforted the good and weak, revived the academy, and the sound of recitation arose.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao rooted out the violent, protected the meek, revived the county academy, and the sound of students reciting their lessons filled the town again.

sentences.zh: 捻匪餘黨解散及各軍凱撤還鄉者數千人，彈壓安輯，民用晏然。

translations.literal: Several thousand remnant Nian bandits who had disbanded and soldiers returning home in victory needed control and settlement; the people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand demobilized Nian fighters and victorious troops returning home all had to be kept in order; under his firm hand daily life settled down.

sentences.zh: 巡撫英翰疏陳炳濤治行為安徽第一，被詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Governor Ying Han memorialized that Bingtao's administrative conduct ranked first in Anhui, and he received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ying Han reported that Bingtao's record ranked first in Anhui, and the throne issued a commendation.

sentences.zh: 十年，調署亳州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to serve as acting magistrate of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to act as magistrate of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋擢廬州知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 廬州故劇郡，中興以來，元勳宿將相望，豪猾藉倚聲勢為不法，官吏莫敢誰何，炳濤嚴治之，稍戢。

translations.literal: Luzhou had long been a difficult prefecture; since the restoration founding meritorious veterans and old generals had followed one after another, and the bold and cunning relied on their influence to act unlawfully—officials did not dare confront them; Bingtao governed them strictly, and they somewhat restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou was a notoriously tough prefecture; since the restoration a succession of war heroes had left local bullies who traded on powerful connections and defied the law with impunity—until Bingtao cracked down and they finally quieted down.

sentences.zh: 無為州江堤，官督民修，炳濤禁胥吏索規費，工必覈實。

translations.literal: The Yangtze dikes at Wuwei Prefecture were government-supervised and people-built; Bingtao forbade clerks and runners from demanding customary fees, and the work had to be verified as genuine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yangtze dikes at Wuwei were rebuilt under official supervision, Bingtao barred clerks from collecting kickbacks and insisted that every measure of work be verified.

sentences.zh: 府東施河口為衝途，冬涸，商船以數牛牽挽始行。

translations.literal: Shihekou east of the prefecture was a major thoroughfare; in winter it dried up, and merchant boats needed several oxen to haul them before they could proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Shihekou east of the prefecture was a major route; when it dried up in winter, merchant boats needed teams of oxen to haul them through.

sentences.zh: 時值旱災，以工代賑，濬河深通，運賑者皆至，商民便之。

translations.literal: At a time of drought disaster, he used labor in place of relief, dredged the river deep for free passage, relief transports all arrived, and merchants and commoners found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he put people to work on relief wages, dredged the river deep enough for full passage, brought in every grain shipment, and made life easier for merchants and townspeople alike.

sentences.zh: 西洋人欲於城內立教堂，成有日矣。

translations.literal: Westerners wished to build a chapel within the city walls, and completion was near at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners were about to finish building a chapel inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 炳濤諭地主曰：「爾不聞寧國之變耶？

translations.literal: Bingtao instructed the landowner, saying: "Have you not heard of the Ningguo incident?
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao told the landowner: "Have you not heard what happened at Ningguo?

sentences.zh: 他日民、教有爭端，爾家首禍。」

translations.literal: If someday commoners and Christians have a dispute, your household will be the first to bring calamity."
translations.idiomatic: If townspeople and Christians clash one day, your family will be blamed first."

sentences.zh: 其人懼，事得寢。

translations.literal: That person was afraid, and the matter was allowed to drop.
translations.idiomatic: The landowner was frightened, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，大江南北訛言有妖術剪人發者，民情洶洶，奸民藉以倡團立卡，多苦行旅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, rumors spread north and south of the Yangtze that sorcery was cutting people's hair; public sentiment was turbulent; wicked persons used this to organize militia and set up checkpoints, greatly harassing travelers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu rumors swept the Yangtze valley that sorcerers were clipping people's hair; panic spread, agitators set up militia checkpoints, and travelers were harassed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 炳濤遍示城邑無妄動，誅一真匪，其疑似者悉不問，人心旋定。

translations.literal: Bingtao posted notices throughout cities and towns against rash action, executed one genuine bandit, and did not question any who were merely suspected; public sentiment soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao posted notices in every town warning against panic, executed one real outlaw, and released everyone else on mere suspicion—and calm returned quickly.

sentences.zh: 三年，母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the third year he left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 皖南興辦保甲墾荒，大吏奏調炳濤主其事。

translations.literal: Southern Anhui launched baojia registration and wasteland reclamation; senior officials memorialized to transfer Bingtao to direct the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When southern Anhui launched baojia registration and land reclamation, senior officials had Bingtao transferred to lead the work.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒於寧國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died at Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Ningguo in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 炳濤機警，善斷獄。

translations.literal: Bingtao was quick-witted and skilled at deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao was quick-witted and had a gift for judging cases.

sentences.zh: 在蒙城，營馬為賊所劫。

translations.literal: While at Mengcheng, camp horses were robbed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at Mengcheng, he learned that bandits had stolen horses from the garrison.

sentences.zh: 乃傳諭，詰旦城但啟一門。

translations.literal: He then issued a proclamation that at dawn only one gate of the city would be opened.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that at dawn only one city gate would be opened.

sentences.zh: 見有馬奔出，有鞍而無轡，命羈之。

translations.literal: When he saw a horse gallop out with a saddle but no bridle, he ordered it seized.
translations.idiomatic: When a saddled horse with no bridle bolted through the gate, he had it seized.

sentences.zh: 俄一人手持一封，將出城，回顧者再，縛之。

translations.literal: Soon a man holding a sealed letter was about to leave the city; he looked back twice and was bound.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a man carrying a sealed letter tried to leave the city, looked back twice, and was seized and bound.

sentences.zh: 發其封，則轡與劫物皆在，其人伏罪。

translations.literal: When the seal was broken open, the bridle and loot were both inside, and the man confessed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking the seal, he found the bridle and stolen goods inside, and the man confessed.

sentences.zh: 在亳州，田父報子夜投井死，驗無傷，井旁有汲水器。

translations.literal: While at Bozhou, a farmer reported that his son had thrown himself into a well at night; examination found no wounds, and there was a water-drawing vessel beside the well.
translations.idiomatic: At Bozhou a farmer reported that his son had drowned himself in a well at night; the body showed no injury, but a water bucket lay beside the well.

sentences.zh: 炳濤念夜非取水時，既原死，何暇持器。

translations.literal: Bingtao reflected that night was not the time for drawing water; if he had truly intended death, why would he have had leisure to carry a vessel?
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao reasoned that no one draws water at night—and if the man had truly meant to die, why would he bother bringing a bucket?

sentences.zh: 詢其婦，無戚容。

translations.literal: He questioned the wife; she showed no grieving countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned the wife, who showed no sign of grief.

sentences.zh: 偵其平日與鄰婦往來，拘鄰婦鞫之，果得狀。

translations.literal: He investigated her usual dealings with a neighboring woman, detained the neighbor and interrogated her, and indeed obtained the full account.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing her daily contact with a neighbor woman, he detained the neighbor and interrogated her until the full truth came out.

sentences.zh: 蓋鄰婦弟與婦通，欲害其夫。

translations.literal: It turned out the neighbor woman's younger brother was carrying on an affair with the wife and wished to kill her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor's brother had been having an affair with the wife and wanted her husband dead.

sentences.zh: 適其夫以事忤父，鄰婦邀醉以酒而投之井。

translations.literal: Just then the husband had offended his father over some matter; the neighbor woman got him drunk with wine and threw him into the well.
translations.idiomatic: The husband had just quarreled with his father over some matter; the neighbor got him drunk and threw him into the well.

sentences.zh: 置汲器者，欲人信其取水投井也，於是皆伏法。

translations.literal: Placing the water-drawing vessel was meant to make people believe he had gone to draw water and fallen into the well; thereupon all were executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: They had placed the bucket to make it look as if he had gone to draw water and fallen in—and all were duly punished.

sentences.zh: 時皖北被兵久，撫輯遺黎，多賴良吏，炳濤為最。

translations.literal: At that time northern Anhui had long suffered war; comforting and organizing the surviving populace owed much to capable officials, and Bingtao was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Anhui had been at war for years; rebuilding order among the survivors depended largely on good officials, and Bingtao stood above the rest.

sentences.zh: 又有俞澍、硃根仁、鄒鍾俊、王懋勳，並為時所稱。

translations.literal: There were also Yu Shu, Zhu Genren, Zou Zhongjun, and Wang Maoxun, all praised in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Also notable were Yu Shu, Zhu Genren, Zou Zhongjun, and Wang Maoxun, all widely praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 澍，直隸天津人。

translations.literal: Shu was a native of Tianjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shu came from Tianjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 以縣丞發安徽，襄壽春鎮軍事。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to Anhui as assistant magistrate and assisted in Shouchun's garrison military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Anhui as assistant magistrate and helped manage garrison affairs at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，署蒙城知縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was appointed acting magistrate of Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時縣城初复，人煙寥落，招集流亡，以大義激紳民，築城籌守禦，趨工者踴躍，不費公家一錢。

translations.literal: At the time the county seat had just been recovered and population was sparse; he gathered the displaced, roused gentry and commoners with high purpose, built walls and planned defense—and workers rushed forward eagerly without costing the government a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: The county seat had just been retaken and was nearly empty; he rallied refugees, moved gentry and commoners with appeals to duty, rebuilt the walls and organized the defense—and workers volunteered so eagerly that not one penny of public funds was spent.

sentences.zh: 捻渠苗沛霖，反側叵測，窺縣城十餘次，不能破城。

translations.literal: The Nian chieftain Miao Peilin was treacherous and unpredictable; he watched the county seat more than ten times but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian chieftain Miao Peilin was notoriously double-dealing; he probed the county seat more than ten times but never breached its walls.

sentences.zh: 有內應賊者，捕斬三人而賊退。

translations.literal: There were traitors inside colluding with bandits; he captured and executed three, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he uncovered three collaborators inside the walls, he executed them and the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年，攻賊於酆墟，擒其酋徒成德等。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he attacked bandits at Fengxu and captured their chieftain Tu Chengde and others.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he attacked bandits at Fengxu and captured chieftain Tu Chengde and his men.

sentences.zh: 八年，攻克龍元賊壘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he captured the Longyuan bandit stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he took the Longyuan bandit stronghold.

sentences.zh: 捻酋孫葵心來犯，出奇計擊走之。

translations.literal: Nian chieftain Sun Kuixin came to attack; he employed a surprise stratagem and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chieftain Sun Kuixin attacked, he devised an unexpected stratagem and routed him.

sentences.zh: 附近捻墟，懾於聲威，往往反正受約束。

translations.literal: Nearby Nian stockades, awed by his prestige, often submitted and accepted restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby Nian strongholds, intimidated by his reputation, often surrendered and submitted to authority.

sentences.zh: 九年，實授。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 先後敘功，晉同知直隸州。

translations.literal: For accumulated merits he was promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated service was rewarded with promotion to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在官數年，潔己愛民。

translations.literal: During his years in office he was scrupulous toward himself and loving toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his years in office he kept himself honest and treated the people with genuine care.

sentences.zh: 及歿，民皆痛哭，送其柩二千里歸葬。

translations.literal: When he died the people all wept bitterly and escorted his coffin two thousand li home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the people wept openly and escorted his coffin two thousand li home for burial.

sentences.zh: 詔贈道銜，建專祠。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed a Circuit Intendant's rank posthumously and built a special shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him Circuit Intendant rank and ordered a memorial shrine built in his honor.

sentences.zh: 根仁，字禮齋，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Genren, style name Lizhai, was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Genren, whose style was Lizhai, came from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以州判從軍，晉秩知縣，留安徽。

translations.literal: He joined the army as prefectural judge, was promoted in rank to magistrate, and remained in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a prefectural judge in military service, he rose to magistrate and remained in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，署定遠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he served as acting magistrate of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he was appointed acting magistrate of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 兵燹初定，徵調尚繁。

translations.literal: The flames of war had just subsided and levies and requisitions were still heavy.
translations.idiomatic: War had only just ended and requisitions were still unrelenting.

sentences.zh: 前令試辦開徵，根仁以民不堪命，請緩之。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate had tried to begin tax collection; Genren, seeing the people could not bear the burden, requested deferral.
translations.idiomatic: The previous magistrate had tried to resume tax collection; Genren, finding the people at breaking point, pleaded for a delay.

sentences.zh: 籌備供億，民無所擾。

translations.literal: He arranged supplies and provisions, and the people were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He organized supplies for the troops without harassing the populace.

sentences.zh: 捕巨猾雍秀春未獲，得黨羽名冊，根仁曰：「我何忍興大獄以博能名？

translations.literal: Failing to capture the great rascal Yong Xiuchun, he obtained a register of accomplices; Genren said: "How could I bear to raise a great prosecution to win a reputation for competence?
translations.idiomatic: He failed to capture the notorious outlaw Yong Xiuchun but obtained a register of his accomplices; Genren said: "How could I launch a sweeping prosecution just to burnish my reputation?

sentences.zh: 喪亂未平，民氣未固，​​激之生變，可勝誅乎？」

translations.literal: Disorder is not yet settled, popular temper is not yet firm—provoke them into revolt, and could we execute them all?"
translations.idiomatic: The country is still unsettled and the people's loyalty is still fragile—provoke them into rebellion, and who could we possibly punish for it all?"

sentences.zh: 遂火其冊，聞者為之改行。

translations.literal: He then burned the register, and those who heard of it reformed their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: So he burned the register, and those who heard of it took it as a warning and mended their ways.

sentences.zh: 跕雞岡周姓聚族居，有從逆者已死，里人利其田廬，致周族人於獄，根仁一訊釋之。

translations.literal: The Zhou clan of Tiaojigang lived together as a community; one who had joined the rebels was already dead, but villagers coveted their fields and dwellings and had Zhou clansmen thrown in prison—Genren questioned them once and released them.
translations.idiomatic: At Tiaojigang the Zhou clan lived as an extended family; a member who had joined the rebels was already dead, but neighbors coveted their land and had Zhou clansmen thrown in jail—Genren heard them out once and set them free.

sentences.zh: 後再署定遠，捻匪擾境，根仁修城濬隍，聚糧固守。

translations.literal: Later he again served as acting magistrate of Dingyuan; Nian bandits harassed the borders, and Genren repaired walls, dredged moats, gathered grain, and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Later, serving again at Dingyuan when Nian bandits raided the borders, he repaired the walls, dredged the moats, stockpiled grain, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 暇輒輕騎巡鄉，勸民修復陂堰，十家治一井，田二頃闢一塘，旱不為災。

translations.literal: In spare moments he would ride lightly through the countryside, urging people to restore dykes and weirs—ten households to maintain one well, two qing of fields to open one pond—so drought brought no calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had a free moment he toured the countryside on horseback, urging villagers to rebuild dykes and dams—one well for every ten households, one pond for every two qing of farmland—so that drought no longer brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 歷署阜陽、懷寧，捕阜陽積匪程黑，置之法。

translations.literal: He successively served at Fuyang and Huaining; he captured the long-standing Fuyang bandit Cheng Hei and executed him by law.
translations.idiomatic: He later served at Fuyang and Huaining, captured the notorious Fuyang bandit Cheng Hei, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 補全椒，興水利，有實政。

translations.literal: Upon substantive appointment at Quanjiao he promoted waterworks, with real achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: At Quanjiao he undertook water conservancy projects that delivered tangible results.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1878.

sentences.zh: 鍾俊，字雋之，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhongjun, style name Junzhi, was a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhongjun, whose style was Junzhi, came from Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 同治中，以州判官安徽，積勞晉秩知縣，補太平。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi he served in Anhui as prefectural judge, and through accumulated labor was promoted to magistrate, receiving substantive appointment at Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi era he served in Anhui as prefectural judge, rose through merit to magistrate, and took permanent appointment at Taiping.

sentences.zh: 平反冤獄，慈祥而人不欺。

translations.literal: He redressed wrongful convictions, was kindly yet none dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He overturned wrongful convictions; he was gentle by nature, yet no one took advantage of him.

sentences.zh: 墾荒勸農，蒿萊盡闢，不追呼而賦辦。

translations.literal: He opened wasteland and encouraged farming until wild growth was all cleared—taxes were collected without pressure yet fully met.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged reclamation until every patch of wasteland was brought under the plow, and taxes were fully collected without coercion.

sentences.zh: 邑行淮鹽，與浙引接界，屢以緝私釀大獄，乃請以官牒領鹽，試辦分銷，民始安。

translations.literal: The county used Huai salt, bordering Zhejiang salt monopolies; repeated crackdowns on smuggling bred major prosecutions, so he requested official permits to receive salt and trial distribution, and the people finally had peace.
translations.idiomatic: The county sold Huai salt along a border with Zhejiang monopolies; repeated anti-smuggling drives had spawned major prosecutions, so he petitioned for government-licensed distribution—and the people finally had relief.

sentences.zh: 修復水利，興書院，儲書七萬卷。

translations.literal: He restored waterworks, established an academy, and stocked seventy thousand volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He restored irrigation works, founded an academy, and amassed a library of seventy thousand volumes.

sentences.zh: 輯儒先格言，曰人生必讀書。

translations.literal: He compiled maxims of the Confucian sages under the title "Every Life Must Read Books."
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a collection of Confucian aphorisms titled "Books Every Life Must Read."

sentences.zh: 訓士敦本行，旌節孝，修祠祀，舉行賓興鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: He instructed scholars to cultivate fundamental conduct, honored chastity and filial piety, repaired temples and shrines, and held the binxing and communal drinking ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He urged students to live upright lives, honored the chaste and filial, restored temples and shrines, and revived the binxing examinations and communal drinking rites.

sentences.zh: 在任五年，以興養立教為務。

translations.literal: During five years in office he made raising and nurturing the people and establishing teaching his chief task.
translations.idiomatic: For five years he made welfare and education the center of his work.

sentences.zh: 調太和，歷署懷寧、六安、阜陽、蕪湖、渦陽，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Transferred to Taihe, he successively served at Huaining, Lu'an, Fuyang, Wuhu, and Guoyang—wherever he went he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Taihe and later acting at Huaining, Lu'an, Fuyang, Wuhu, and Guoyang, he earned a reputation wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，乞休，卒於家。

translations.literal: During Guangxu he requested retirement and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu era he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 清貧如故。

translations.literal: He remained poor and upright as before.
translations.idiomatic: He died as poor and upright as he had lived.

sentences.zh: 子嘉來，官至外務部尚書，守其家法焉。

translations.literal: His son Jialai rose to Minister of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and upheld the family ways.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jialai became Minister of Foreign Affairs and upheld the family's standards of integrity.

sentences.zh: 懋勳，字弼丞，湖北松滋人。

translations.literal: Maoxun, style name Bicheng, was a native of Songzi in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoxun, whose style was Bicheng, came from Songzi in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，以議敘縣丞，發安徽，從軍有功，晉知縣。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng, through merit evaluation as assistant magistrate he was dispatched to Anhui; military service won merit and he was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era he entered Anhui as assistant magistrate, distinguished himself in military service, and rose to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷署潁上、合肥、亳州、泗州。

translations.literal: He successively served at Yingshang, Hefei, Bozhou, and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively at Yingshang, Hefei, Bozhou, and Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 補六安直隸州知州，因事去職。

translations.literal: Upon substantive appointment as prefect of Lu'an Directly Governed Prefecture, he left office over a matter.
translations.idiomatic: He received formal appointment as prefect of Lu'an but left office over a dispute.

sentences.zh: 尋因籌賑捐，獎以知府候補。

translations.literal: Soon, for organizing relief donations, he was rewarded with candidacy for prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his work organizing famine relief earned him candidacy for prefect.

sentences.zh: 懋勳先後官安徽近五十年，任亳州、泗州皆三次。

translations.literal: Maoxun served in Anhui for nearly fifty years in all, holding Bozhou and Sizhou three times each.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxun served in Anhui for nearly fifty years altogether, and held both Bozhou and Sizhou three times each.

sentences.zh: 初至亳，捻匪苗沛霖初平，清查戶口，收繳軍械，平毀寨堡數百，民始復業。

translations.literal: When he first arrived at Bozhou, the Nian bandit Miao Peilin had just been pacified; he checked household registers, collected weapons, leveled and destroyed several hundred stockades, and the people at last resumed their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: On his first arrival at Bozhou, with Miao Peilin's Nian just subdued, he took a census, confiscated weapons, razed hundreds of stockades, and people finally returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 懲械鬥，清積案，釐學產，復書院，士民戴之。

translations.literal: He punished armed feuding, cleared accumulated cases, sorted out academy endowments, restored the academy—the gentry and people revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down on clan feuds, cleared a backlog of lawsuits, put school endowments in order, and restored the academy—and gentry and commoners alike adored him.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去，會巡撫過境，州人萬眾乞留懋勳，巡撫許以俟服闋重任，後如其言，夾道歡迎。

translations.literal: He left on mourning for his father; when the governor passed through, ten thousand people of the prefecture begged to retain Maoxun—the governor promised he would be reappointed after mourning ended; later it happened as promised, with crowds lining the roads in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When he left for his father's mourning, the provincial governor passed through and ten thousand townspeople pleaded to keep Maoxun—the governor promised reappointment after mourning, and when he returned they lined the roads to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，洊飢，煮粥以賑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, repeated famines struck; he boiled porridge for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu years, when famine struck repeatedly, he set up gruel kitchens for relief.

sentences.zh: 河南、山西、陝西饑民流轉入境，留養資遣，全活無算。

translations.literal: Famine refugees from Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi drifted across the border; he sheltered, fed, and sent them on their way—countless lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Starving refugees from Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi poured in; he fed them, gave them passage home, and saved untold numbers of lives.

sentences.zh: 泗州瀕洪澤湖，為匪藪，捕誅劇盜數十，閭閻得安。

translations.literal: Sizhou bordered Hongze Lake and was a bandit haunt; he captured and executed dozens of notorious robbers, and neighborhoods found peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou lay on Hongze Lake and teemed with outlaws; he captured and executed dozens of hardened bandits, and peace returned to the neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 治獄無株連，禁差保擾民。

translations.literal: In handling cases he did not implicate by association, and forbade runners and guarantors from harassing the people.
translations.idiomatic: He avoided guilt by association in criminal cases and barred petty officials from harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 勸農事，勵風化，親歷鄉曲，民隱悉達。

translations.literal: He encouraged farming, promoted moral reform, personally traveled through villages, and fully understood hidden popular grievances.
translations.idiomatic: He urged farmers back to their fields, promoted moral reform, traveled the countryside himself, and knew every grievance of the people.

sentences.zh: 最後至泗，距前已二十餘年，盜賊聞風遠竄，姦胥皆避歸田野。

translations.literal: On his last arrival at Si, more than twenty years had passed since his previous term; bandits fled at the mere news of him, and corrupt clerks hid themselves in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: On his third arrival at Sizhou, more than twenty years after his first, bandits fled at the sound of his name and corrupt clerks went into hiding in the fields.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1909.

sentences.zh: =蒯德模=蒯德模，字子範，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: =Kuai Demo= Kuai Demo, style name Zifan, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Demo, whose style was Zifan, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐末，以諸生治團練，積功洊保知縣，留江蘇。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianfeng, as a licentiate he organized local militia; accumulated merit brought repeated recommendations to magistrate, and he remained in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: As a licentiate at the end of the Xianfeng era he organized local militia, earned repeated recommendations for magistrate through accumulated service, and remained in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，署長洲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he served as acting magistrate of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he was appointed acting magistrate of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蘇州新復，盜日數發，德模偵之輒獲。

translations.literal: Suzhou had just been recovered and robberies occurred daily; whenever Demo investigated he promptly made arrests.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou had just been retaken and robberies were daily occurrences—but whenever Demo investigated, arrests followed.

sentences.zh: 有匿鎮將營者，親往擒以歸，置之法。

translations.literal: Some hid in a brigade general's camp; he went in person to seize them and bring them back, and executed them by law.
translations.idiomatic: When some fugitives hid inside a brigade general's camp, he went in person to seize them and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 車渡民聚眾抗租，或欲懾以兵。

translations.literal: At Chedu the people gathered to resist rent payment; some wished to intimidate them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Chedu villagers assembled to resist tax collection, and some officials wanted to intimidate them with soldiers.

sentences.zh: 德模曰：「是激之變也。」

translations.literal: Demo said: "That would provoke rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Demo said: "That would only provoke a riot."

sentences.zh: 扁舟往，治首惡，散脅從，事立平。

translations.literal: Taking a small boat he went, punished the ringleaders, dispersed the followers, and the matter was immediately settled.
translations.idiomatic: He went alone in a small boat, punished the ringleaders, released the followers, and the affair was settled at once.

sentences.zh: 治有天主堂，雍正間鄂爾泰撫蘇，改祠孔子，泰西人伊宗伊以故址請。

translations.literal: In the district was a Catholic church; during Yongzheng Ortai as governor of Jiangsu had converted it to a Confucian shrine; the Western missionary Yizongyi requested the old site.
translations.idiomatic: The district had once held a Catholic church that Governor Ortai had converted to a Confucian shrine during Yongzheng; a Western missionary named Yizongyi now petitioned for the old site.

sentences.zh: 德模曰：「某官可罷，此祠非若有也。」

translations.literal: Demo said: "This official may be dismissed, but this shrine is not yours to claim."
translations.idiomatic: Demo replied: "Dismiss me if you will, but this shrine is not yours to reclaim."

sentences.zh: 卒不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 奸人誘買良家女，倚勢豪為庇，德模挈女親屬往出之，豪亦屈服，其不畏強禦類此。

translations.literal: Scoundrels enticed and bought daughters of decent families, relying on powerful brutes for protection; Demo took the girl's relatives to rescue her, and the bully also submitted—his fearlessness toward the powerful was like this throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When swindlers trafficked in respectable girls under the protection of local bullies, Demo took the girl's kin to retrieve her and even the bully backed down—he was always this fearless before the powerful.

sentences.zh: 常周行鄉陌，田夫走卒相酬答，周知民隱。

translations.literal: He often walked the country lanes; farmers and runners exchanged words with him, and he thoroughly knew hidden popular grievances.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly walked the village lanes, chatting freely with farmers and laborers, and kept his finger on the pulse of every hidden grievance.

sentences.zh: 馭下嚴而卹其私，胥役奉法，不敢為蠹。

translations.literal: Toward subordinates he was strict yet cared for their private needs; clerks and runners obeyed the law and dared not commit abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern with subordinates yet attentive to their personal needs; clerks and runners obeyed the law and dared not abuse their power.

sentences.zh: 附郭訟獄故繁，日坐堂皇判決，間用俳語鉤距發摘，豪猾屏息。

translations.literal: Litigation in the suburban district was naturally heavy; daily he sat in the hall to decide cases, sometimes using colloquial speech and probing questions to expose fraud—local bullies held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban lawsuits were legion; he sat in court every day to decide them, sometimes using plain speech and probing questions to trap liars—and local bullies fell silent.

sentences.zh: 然執法平，不為覈刻。

translations.literal: Yet he enforced the law fairly and was not harshly exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enforced the law fairly and never persecuted offenders.

sentences.zh: 上官遇疑獄，輒移鞫治，多所平反。

translations.literal: When superiors encountered doubtful cases they often transferred them for his interrogation and judgment—many wrongful convictions were overturned.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors faced difficult cases they often referred them to him—and many wrongful convictions he overturned.

sentences.zh: 治長洲四年，判八百餘牘，盡愜民意，或播歌謠焉。

translations.literal: Governing Changzhou for four years, he decided more than eight hundred cases, all to popular satisfaction—some even spread songs about him.
translations.idiomatic: In four years at Changzhou he decided more than eight hundred cases to general satisfaction—songs about him even spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 江北大水，災民麕集，德模請於大吏，分各縣留養，三萬餘人無失所。

translations.literal: Great floods struck north of the Yangtze; disaster victims gathered in crowds; Demo petitioned senior officials to divide them among counties for shelter and care—more than thirty thousand people did not lose their homes.
translations.idiomatic: When floods devastated the north bank of the Yangtze, refugees poured in; Demo petitioned his superiors to distribute them among the counties for shelter—and more than thirty thousand people were kept from destitution.

sentences.zh: 民有為飢寒偷竊者，設化莠室，給衣食，使習藝，藝成遣歸。

translations.literal: For people who stole from hunger and cold he established a "Transforming Weeds" chamber, gave them food and clothing, had them learn trades, and sent them home when skilled.
translations.idiomatic: For people driven to theft by hunger and cold he set up a reform house, fed and clothed them, taught them trades, and sent them home when they were ready.

sentences.zh: 為滸墅關營籌芻秣費，永免比閭供役。

translations.literal: For the Fushuguan customs station he arranged fodder funds, permanently exempting neighboring wards from corvée service.
translations.idiomatic: For the Fushuguan customs station he secured fodder funds and permanently freed neighboring wards from corvée duty.

sentences.zh: 修望亭塘，為橋二十八，以利行旅。

translations.literal: He repaired Wangting Pond and built twenty-eight bridges to benefit travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Wangting Pond and built twenty-eight bridges for the convenience of travelers.

sentences.zh: 兵祲之後，百廢待舉，壇廟、倉庾、書院、善堂、祠宇及先賢祠墓，率先修復；

translations.literal: After the calamities of war, a hundred neglected projects awaited attention—altars, temples, granaries, academies, charity halls, shrines, and shrines and tombs of former worthies—he took the lead in restoring them;
translations.idiomatic: After the war left everything in ruins, he took the lead in restoring altars, temples, granaries, academies, charity halls, shrines, and the tombs of former worthies;

sentences.zh: 不足，則斥俸助之。

translations.literal: when funds fell short he paid from his own salary to assist.
translations.idiomatic: when funds ran short he contributed from his own salary.

sentences.zh: 徵漕，舊有淋尖、踢斛、花邊、樣米、捉豬諸色目，又有截串、差追諸弊，一皆革除，不追呼而賦辦。

translations.literal: For tribute grain collection there had been items like "dripping tips," "kicking the measure," "decorative margins," "sample rice," and "catching pigs," and abuses like "cutting strings" and "runner pursuit"—he eliminated them all, and taxes were collected without coercion yet fully met.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished every exaction and abuse associated with grain tribute—from drip surcharges and kickbacks to sample rice and runner harassment—and taxes were fully collected without coercion.

sentences.zh: 惟大小戶均一，便於民而不便於紳，御史硃鎮以浮收劾奏，事下按治，總督曾國籓、巡撫郭柏廕奏雪之。

translations.literal: Only equal treatment of large and small households benefited the people but not the gentry; Censor Zhu Zhen memorialized charging over-collection; the matter was sent down for investigation, and Governor-General Zeng Guofan and Governor Guo Boyin memorialized clearing him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated large and small households equally—convenient for commoners but not for gentry; Censor Zhu Zhen charged him with over-collection, but Governor-General Zeng Guofan and Governor Guo Boyin cleared his name.

sentences.zh: 詔以「是非倒置」切責原奏官。

translations.literal: An edict sternly rebuked the original accuser with the words "right and wrong turned upside down."
translations.idiomatic: The throne sharply rebuked the accuser with an edict declaring that "right and wrong had been turned upside down."

sentences.zh: 旋署太倉直隸州知州、蘇州知府。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting prefect of Taicang Directly Governed Prefecture and as Suzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting prefect of Taicang and Suzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 九年，調署鎮江，時天津民擊斃法蘭西領事豐大業，沿江戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to serve at Zhenjiang; at the time Tianjin people had beaten to death the French consul Fontanier, and cities along the Yangtze were on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 9 (1870) he was transferred to Zhenjiang; the French consul Fontanier had just been killed in Tianjin and cities along the Yangtze were on high alert.

sentences.zh: 德模至，則葺外城，浚甘露港，召還居民之聞警遠徙者，人心始定。

translations.literal: When Demo arrived, he repaired the outer walls, dredged Ganlu Harbor, recalled residents who had fled far upon hearing the alarm—and public sentiment at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Demo arrived he repaired the outer walls, dredged Ganlu Harbor, called back residents who had fled in panic—and confidence slowly returned.

sentences.zh: 調署江寧，未幾，擢四川夔州知府。

translations.literal: Transferred to serve at Jiangning; before long promoted to prefect of Kuizhou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangning; soon afterward he was promoted to prefect of Kuizhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 府城濱江，屢圮於水，修築輒不就。

translations.literal: The prefectural city bordered the river, repeatedly collapsing from water; construction and repair always failed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural seat lay on the riverbank and repeatedly washed away; every attempt at repair failed.

sentences.zh: 德模自出方略，築保坎十三道，甃以方丈大石，層累而上。

translations.literal: Demo himself devised the strategy, building thirteen protective embankments faced with square one-zhang boulders, piled layer upon layer upward.
translations.idiomatic: Demo drew up the plan himself: thirteen protective revetments faced with massive square boulders, stacked tier upon tier.

sentences.zh: 捐萬金以倡其役，不二年遂成。

translations.literal: He donated ten thousand taels of silver to launch the work, and within less than two years it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He contributed ten thousand taels to kick off the project, and in under two years the work stood complete.

sentences.zh: 附郭有臭鹽磧，盛漲則沒水，水落，貧民相聚煎鹽。

translations.literal: In the suburbs was a stinking salt flat; at high water it was submerged, and when the water fell the poor gathered to boil salt.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the city lay a foul salt marsh—submerged at flood, but when the waters receded the poor gathered there to boil salt.

sentences.zh: 嗣為雲陽灶戶所持，請封禁，然冬令私煎如故，聚眾抗捕無如何。

translations.literal: Later the Yunyang salt-manufacturing households seized on this and petitioned for a ban; yet private boiling continued as before in winter, and crowds resisted arrest without remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yunyang salt producers petitioned for a ban; yet every winter the poor still boiled salt in secret, and when officials tried to arrest them mobs resisted—nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 德模請弛禁，官買其鹽，運銷宜昌。

translations.literal: Demo requested lifting the ban, having the government buy their salt and transport it for sale at Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Demo petitioned to lift the ban, have the government purchase the salt, and transport it for sale at Yichang.

sentences.zh: 不奪奉節貧民之業，不侵雲陽銷引之岸，遂著為令。

translations.literal: This did not deprive the poor of Fengjie of their livelihood, nor did it encroach on Yunyang's salt monopoly zone—and it was established as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: It kept the poor of Fengjie in their trade without encroaching on Yunyang's salt market, and the policy was written into law.

sentences.zh: 勸民種桑，奉節一縣二十二萬株，他邑稱是。

translations.literal: He urged the people to plant mulberry trees—two hundred twenty thousand in Fengjie county alone, and other counties followed suit.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged mulberry planting: Fengjie alone put in two hundred twenty thousand saplings, and other counties matched the effort.

sentences.zh: 在夔四年，卒於官。

translations.literal: After four years at Kuizhou he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Four years into his term at Kuizhou, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 長洲、太倉、夔州皆祠祀之。

translations.literal: Changzhou, Taicang, and Kuizhou all built shrines to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to him were erected at Changzhou, Taicang, and Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: =林達泉=林達泉，字海岩，廣東大埔人。

translations.literal: =Lin Daquan= Lin Daquan, style name Haiyan, was a native of Dapu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Daquan, whose style was Haiyan, came from Dapu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年舉人，江蘇巡撫丁日昌闢佐​​幕府。

translations.literal: A juren in the eleventh year of Xianfeng, he was invited by Jiangsu Governor Ding Richang to serve on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: A juren of 1861, he was invited by Jiangsu Governor Ding Richang to join his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 留心經濟，每論古今輿圖、武備及海外各國形勢，歷歷如指掌，日昌雅重之。

translations.literal: He studied practical statecraft; whenever he discussed ancient and modern maps, military preparedness, and the conditions of overseas countries he spoke with such clarity it was as if he held them in his palm—Ding Richang held him in the highest esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to practical statecraft, he could discuss maps, military readiness, and foreign nations with such precision it was as though he held them in the palm of his hand—and Ding Richang valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，粵匪餘孽竄廣東，達泉歸里練鄉勇，籌防禦，大埔得無患。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, remnant Cantonese rebels fled into Guangdong; Daquan returned home to drill local militia and organize the defense, and Dapu was spared disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when rebel remnants fled into Guangdong, Daquan returned home to train militia and organize the defense—and Dapu was spared.

sentences.zh: 敘績，以知縣選用。

translations.literal: For this service he was selected for appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His service was recognized with selection for magistrate appointment.

sentences.zh: 七年，隨剿山東捻匪有功，晉直隸州知州，發江蘇。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, campaigning against Shandong Nian bandits he won merit and was promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture, and was dispatched to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868, distinguished in the campaign against Shandong Nian bandits, he rose to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture and went to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 八年，署崇明知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as acting magistrate of Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he was appointed acting magistrate of Chongming.

sentences.zh: 亂後彫敝，達泉革陋規，清積獄，修城垣，濬河渠，建橋樑，置義塚，增書院膏火，設同仁育嬰堂。

translations.literal: After the chaos the district lay in ruins; Daquan abolished corrupt practices, cleared accumulated lawsuits, repaired walls, dredged canals, built bridges, established burial grounds for the destitute, increased academy stipends, and founded the Tongren Foundling Hospital.
translations.idiomatic: The district was devastated by war; Daquan abolished corrupt fees, cleared a backlog of cases, rebuilt walls, dredged canals, raised bridges, opened public graveyards, increased academy stipends, and founded the Tongren Foundling Hospital.

sentences.zh: 利民之政，知無不為。

translations.literal: Every measure that benefited the people—if he knew of it, he did it.
translations.idiomatic: Every policy that could help the people, he pursued without fail.

sentences.zh: 及去任，父老遮道攀留。

translations.literal: When he left office, elders blocked the road and clung to his carriage to keep him from going.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, elders blocked the road and begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 其後兵部侍郎彭玉麟巡閱過境，見老者飢踣於道，與之食，曰：「若林公久任於此，吾邑豈有飢人哉？」

translations.literal: Later when Vice Minister of War Peng Yulin passed through on inspection, he saw an old man collapsing from hunger on the road and gave him food, saying: "If Magistrate Lin had long remained in this district, how could our county have hungry people?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Vice Minister Peng Yulin passed through on inspection, he saw an old man collapse from hunger by the road and fed him, saying: "If Magistrate Lin had stayed here longer, would our county still have starving people?"

sentences.zh: 十一年，署江陰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as acting magistrate of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 11 (1872) he was appointed acting magistrate of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 城河通江潮，又縣境東橫河關，農田十餘萬畝，灌溉之利，亂後皆淤塞，大濬之。

translations.literal: The city moat connected to Yangtze tides, and within the county the Donghengguan sluice served over one hundred thousand mu of farmland; the irrigation benefits were all silted shut after the chaos, and he dredged them on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: The city moat linked to Yangtze tides; the Donghengguan sluice irrigated more than one hundred thousand mu of farmland—all choked with silt after the wars, and he dredged them on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 建義倉，勸捐積穀。

translations.literal: He built charity granaries and urged donations to stock grain reserves.
translations.idiomatic: He established charity granaries and urged donations to build grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 所定章程，歷久遵守。

translations.literal: The regulations he established were obeyed for years afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations he drew up were followed for years.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，授海州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he received appointment at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was appointed to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 達泉先奉檄勘海、沭鹽河，請以工代賑，下車次第舉辦。

translations.literal: Daquan had already been ordered to survey the Hai and Shu salt rivers; he requested relief work as employment, and upon taking office implemented the plans in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Already ordered to survey the Hai and Shu salt rivers, he petitioned for work-relief programs and, upon taking office, carried them out step by step.

sentences.zh: 浚甲子河及玉帶河，復橋路，增堤防，民咸稱便。

translations.literal: He dredged the Jiazi and Yudai rivers, restored bridges and roads, and strengthened dikes—people everywhere praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Jiazi and Yudai rivers, restored bridges and roads, and strengthened the dikes—and people everywhere praised the improvements.

sentences.zh: 州地瘠民貧，素為盜藪。

translations.literal: The prefecture was poor in land and its people impoverished—a longtime haunt of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was barren and its people poor—a longtime haven for bandits.

sentences.zh: 達泉時出巡，擒巨憝，置之法。

translations.literal: Daquan made regular inspection tours, captured notorious ringleaders, and executed them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Daquan toured the countryside regularly, seized hardened ringleaders, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 土宜棉，設局教民紡績，廣植桐柏雜樹於郭外錦屏山，所規畫多及久遠。

translations.literal: The soil suited cotton; he established offices to teach spinning and weaving, and widely planted tung, cypress, and mixed trees on Jinping Mountain outside the city wall—most of his plans looked to the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Cotton thrived there; he set up workshops to teach spinning and planted tung, cypress, and mixed trees on Jinping Mountain outside the walls—nearly everything he planned was built to last.

sentences.zh: 時方經營台灣，船政大臣沈葆楨疏薦達泉器識宏遠，潔己愛民，請調署新設之台北府。

translations.literal: Taiwan was then being developed; Maritime Affairs Minister Shen Baozhen memorialized recommending Daquan for his broad vision and integrity in serving the people, requesting his transfer to the newly established Taipei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Taiwan was being developed, Maritime Affairs Minister Shen Baozhen recommended Daquan for his far-reaching vision and integrity and petitioned for his transfer to the new Taipei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 格於部議，特詔從之。

translations.literal: The Board raised objections, but an imperial edict overruled them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry raised objections, but the throne issued a special edict overruling them.

sentences.zh: 達泉至，陳治台諸策。

translations.literal: When Daquan arrived, he presented his policies for governing Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he laid out his policies for governing Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 議建置，減徵收，整飭防軍，招民墾荒，皆因地制宜，事事草創，積勞致疾。

translations.literal: He discussed institutions, reduced tax collection, reorganized garrison troops, and recruited settlers to open wasteland—all adapted to local conditions, everything built from scratch; overwork brought on illness.
translations.idiomatic: He designed institutions, cut taxes, reorganized the garrison, and recruited settlers to open land—everything tailored locally and built from nothing, until exhaustion brought on illness.

sentences.zh: 四年，丁父憂，以毀卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered mourning for his father and died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he entered mourning for his father and died of grief.

sentences.zh: =方大湜=方大湜，字菊人，湖南巴陵人。

translations.literal: =Fang Dashi= Fang Dashi, style name Juren, was a native of Baling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Dashi, whose style was Juren, came from Baling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，以諸生從巡撫胡林翼軍中，洊保知縣，授廣濟縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, as a licentiate he joined Governor Hu Linyi's army; repeated recommendations for magistrate followed, and he was appointed to Guangji county.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, as a licentiate in Governor Hu Linyi's camp, he earned repeated recommendations for magistrate and received Guangji county.

sentences.zh: 清保甲，治團練，盜賊屏息。

translations.literal: He cleaned up the baojia system, organized local militia, and bandits disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened out the baojia system, organized local militia, and bandits vanished.

sentences.zh: 築盤塘石堤，下游數縣皆免水患。

translations.literal: He built the Pantang stone dike, and several downstream counties were all spared from flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Pantang stone dike, sparing several downstream counties from flooding.

sentences.zh: 十年，土匪何致祥等謀結皖賊，襲攻官軍，大湜偕員外郎閻敬銘馳往擒之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, local bandits He Zhixiang and others plotted to join with Anhui rebels to attack government troops; Dashi went with Vice Director Yan Jingming to capture them at speed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, when local bandits under He Zhixiang plotted with Anhui rebels to attack government troops, Dashi raced out with Vice Director Yan Jingming and captured them.

sentences.zh: 十一年，皖賊竄湖北，黃州、德安諸屬縣先後陷，廣濟亦被擾。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Anhui rebels fled into Hubei; Huangzhou, Dean, and their subordinate counties fell in succession, and Guangji was also raided.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Anhui rebels poured into Hubei; Huangzhou, Dean, and their dependencies fell one after another, and Guangji was raided as well.

sentences.zh: 大湜被吏議，革職留任。

translations.literal: Dashi faced a censor's investigation, was dismissed from rank but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: Censured by the bureaucracy, Dashi was demoted in rank but kept on in office.

sentences.zh: 調署襄陽，飛蝗遍野，大湜躡屩持竿，躬率農民撲捕，三日而盡。

translations.literal: Transferred to serve at Xiangyang, when locusts covered the fields Dashi wore straw sandals, took a pole in hand, and personally led farmers to drive them off—in three days they were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Xiangyang as locusts blanketed the fields, Dashi wore straw sandals, took up a catching pole, and personally led farmers to wipe them out in three days.

sentences.zh: 濬城南襄水故道，渠成，涸复田數万畝。

translations.literal: He dredged the old course of the Xiang River south of the city; when the canal was finished, tens of thousands of mu of parched land were restored to fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the old Xiang River channel south of the city; when the canal opened, tens of thousands of mu of dried-out land returned to cultivation.

sentences.zh: 同治初，巡撫嚴樹森疏陳大湜政績優異，復原職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, Governor Yan Shusen memorialized that Dashi's achievements were outstanding, and his original rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, Governor Yan Shusen memorialized that Dashi's achievements were outstanding and his original rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢宜昌知府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to prefect of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he was promoted to prefect of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 九年，大水，難民避高阜，絕食兩日。

translations.literal: In the ninth year came great floods; refugees took refuge on high ground and went without food for two days.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 catastrophic floods struck; refugees crowding high ground had gone without food for two days.

sentences.zh: 大湜捐貲煮粥糜，又為餺飥數万賑之。

translations.literal: Dashi donated funds to cook porridge and gruel, and also made tens of thousands of dumplings for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Dashi donated his own funds to cook porridge and gruel, and made tens of thousands of boiled dumplings for relief.

sentences.zh: 諭米商招民負米，日致數十石，計口散給，災戶無失所。

translations.literal: He instructed rice merchants to hire people to carry rice—in tens of shi per day—and distributed by head count, so disaster households did not lose their homes.
translations.idiomatic: He urged rice merchants to hire carriers and bring in dozens of shi daily, distributing rations by head count so no disaster household was left destitute.

sentences.zh: 攝荊宜施道。

translations.literal: He served as acting Jing-Yi-Shi circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Jing-Yi-Shi circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 十年，調武昌。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he was transferred to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 樊口有港蜿蜒九十餘裡，外通江，內則重湖環列，週五百里。

translations.literal: At Fankou was a channel winding more than ninety li; outward it connected to the river, inward a cluster of lakes ringed around, circumference five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Fankou had a channel winding more than ninety li—opening to the Yangtze on one side, ringed within by a chain of lakes spanning five hundred li in circuit.

sentences.zh: 江水盛漲，由港倒灌，近湖居者苦之。

translations.literal: When the Yangtze rose in flood, water poured back through the channel, and those living near the lakes suffered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yangtze swelled, water backed through the channel, and lakeside residents bore the brunt.

sentences.zh: 僉請築壩樊口，以御江水。

translations.literal: All petitioned to build a dam at Fankou to hold back the river water.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone petitioned to dam Fankou and block the Yangtze floodwaters.

sentences.zh: 大湜謂閉樊口則湖水無所洩，環湖數縣受其害，上下江堤亦危，力持不可。

translations.literal: Dashi argued that closing Fankou would leave the lake water nowhere to drain, harming several counties around the lakes and endangering dikes up and down the river—and he firmly opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Dashi insisted that damming Fankou would trap the lake waters, ruin counties around the lakes, and endanger dikes up and down the river—and he firmly blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，再署荊宜施道，尋擢安襄鄖荊道，歷直隸按察使、山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he again served as Jing-Yi-Shi circuit intendant, soon promoted to An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit intendant, then served as judicial commissioner of Zhili and financial commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he again served as Jing-Yi-Shi intendant, soon rose to An-Xiang-Yun-Jing intendant, and later served as judicial commissioner of Zhili and financial commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，開缺，另候簡用，遂乞病。

translations.literal: In the eighth year a vacancy opened; he awaited new appointment, and then requested leave for illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882, when his post fell vacant for reassignment, he pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 為言者所劾，鐫級歸。

translations.literal: Censured by critics, he was stripped of rank and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Attacked by critics in memorials, he was stripped of rank and sent home.

sentences.zh: 大湜生平政績，多在為守令時。

translations.literal: Dashi's achievements in life were mostly during his years as a magistrate or prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Dashi's life's achievements came during his years as a magistrate or prefect.

sentences.zh: 所至興學校，課蠶桑，事必親理，胥吏無所容姦，民親而信之。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he established schools and encouraged sericulture; he personally handled every matter, leaving clerks no room for fraud—and people trusted him intimately.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he founded schools and promoted sericulture; he handled everything himself, leaving no opening for clerks to cheat—and the people trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時周歷民間，一吏一擔夫自隨，即田隴間判訟。

translations.literal: From time to time he toured among the people with a single clerk and a single porter, judging cases right in the field ridges.
translations.idiomatic: He often toured the countryside with only one clerk and one porter, settling cases right there in the furrows.

sentences.zh: 守武昌時，勘堤過屬縣，暮宿民家，已去而縣官猶不知。

translations.literal: While governing Wuchang, inspecting dikes as he passed through subordinate counties, he lodged at a commoner's home at dusk and was gone before the county magistrate even knew.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting dikes through subordinate counties from Wuchang, he would lodge at a farmer's home at dusk and be gone before the county magistrate knew he had come.

sentences.zh: 嚴義利之辨，嘗曰：「以利誘者，初皆在可取不可取之間。

translations.literal: He strictly distinguished righteousness from profit and once said: "Those tempted by profit at first all stand between what may be taken and what may not.
translations.idiomatic: A rigorous judge of profit and principle, he once said: "Those seduced by profit always start in that gray zone between what may be taken and what may not.

sentences.zh: 偶一為之，自謂無損，久則顧忌漸忘。

translations.literal: Do it once and you tell yourself there's no harm; over time caution is forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Do it once and you tell yourself no harm is done—until, in time, every scruple fades.

sentences.zh: 自愛者當視為冘毒，飢渴至死，不可入口。」

translations.literal: One who cherishes himself should treat it as deadly poison—better die of hunger and thirst than let it pass your lips."
translations.idiomatic: The self-respecting official should treat it as poison—better starve and thirst to death than let a single tainted morsel pass your lips."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「居官廉，如婦人貞節，不過婦道一端。

translations.literal: He also said: "Integrity in office is like a woman's chastity—only one aspect of a wife's duty.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Official integrity is like a woman's chastity—only one facet of womanly conduct.

sentences.zh: 若恃貞節，而不孝、不敬、不勤、不慎，豈得謂賢乎？」

translations.literal: If one relies on chastity alone yet fails in filial piety, respect, diligence, and caution—can such a person be called virtuous?"
translations.idiomatic: Cling to chastity yet fail in filial piety, respect, diligence, and prudence—can you still be called virtuous?"

sentences.zh: 公暇輒讀書，所著平平言及蠶桑、捕蝗、修堤、區田諸書，皆自道所得。

translations.literal: In his leisure he read books; his works Pingping Yan and books on sericulture, locust-catching, dike repair, and contour farming all recorded what he had learned from experience.
translations.idiomatic: In spare hours he read ceaselessly; his Plain Words and his treatises on sericulture, locust control, dike repair, and contour farming all distilled what he had learned firsthand.

sentences.zh: 歸田後，謂所親曰：「官至兩司，不如守令之與民親，措置自如也。」

translations.literal: After retiring to his fields, he told his intimates: "Reaching the rank of provincial treasurer or judge is not as good as being a magistrate or prefect—closer to the people, able to act freely."
translations.idiomatic: After retiring he told close friends: "Reaching treasurer or judge is nothing compared with being a magistrate or prefect—close to the people, free to act."

sentences.zh: 遂不出，卒於家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he never went out again and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He never went out again and died at home.

sentences.zh: =陳豪=陳豪，字藍洲，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: =Chen Hao= Chen Hao, style name Lanzhou, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao, whose style was Lanzhou, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治九年優貢，以知縣發湖北，光緒三年，署房縣。

translations.literal: An eminent tribute student in the ninth year of Tongzhi, he was dispatched to Hubei as magistrate; in the third year of Guangxu he served as acting magistrate of Fang county.
translations.idiomatic: An eminent tribute student of 1870, he went to Hubei as magistrate; in 1877 he was appointed acting magistrate of Fang county.

sentences.zh: 勤於聽訟，每履鄉，恆提榼張幕，憩息荒祠，與隸卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: Diligent in hearing cases, whenever he toured the countryside he always carried a wine jar and set up a tent, resting in abandoned shrines and sharing hardships with runners.
translations.idiomatic: Tireless in hearing cases, on every rural tour he carried provisions, pitched a tent in some abandoned shrine, and shared every hardship with his runners.

sentences.zh: 會匪柯三江謀亂，立擒置之法。

translations.literal: When the secret-society bandit Ke Sanjiang plotted rebellion, he immediately captured and executed him by law.
translations.idiomatic: When secret-society ringleader Ke Sanjiang plotted rebellion, Hao seized him at once and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 置匭縣門，諭脅從自首，杖而釋之。

translations.literal: He placed a complaint box at the county gate and announced that coerced followers who surrendered would be flogged and released.
translations.idiomatic: He placed a complaint box at the county gate and promised that coerced followers who turned themselves in would be lightly flogged and released.

sentences.zh: 徵米斗斛必平，不留難，不挑剔，民大悅，刁紳感而戢訟。

translations.literal: When collecting grain every dou and hu was measured level—no obstruction, no quibbling—and the people rejoiced; quarrelsome gentry were moved to restrain their litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Grain collection was measured fair and full—no delays, no nitpicking—and the people rejoiced; even quarrelsome gentry settled down and stopped suing.

sentences.zh: 禁種鶯粟，募崇陽人教之植茶，咸賴其利。

translations.literal: He forbade opium poppy cultivation, recruited people from Chongyang to teach tea planting, and all relied on the profit.
translations.idiomatic: He banned opium poppies, brought in tea growers from Chongyang to teach cultivation, and the people thrived on the trade.

sentences.zh: 歷署應城、蘄水。

translations.literal: He successively served at Yingcheng and Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: He later served at Yingcheng and Qishui.

sentences.zh: 授漢川，頻年襄河溢，修築香花垸、彭公垸、天興垸諸堤，疏濬茶壺溝、縣河口，以工代賑。

translations.literal: Upon appointment at Hanchuan, with the Xiang River flooding year after year, he built dikes at Xianghua, Penggong, and Tianxing polders, dredged Chahu Gully and the county river mouth, and used labor in place of relief.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned to Hanchuan as the Xiang flooded year after year, he built dikes at Xianghua, Penggong, and Tianxing polders, dredged Chahu Gully and the county river mouth, and put flood victims to work for relief.

sentences.zh: 新溝者，毗漢陽，冬涸舟澀。

translations.literal: Xingou lay adjacent to Hanyang; in winter when the water dried up boats ran aground.
translations.idiomatic: Xingou bordered Hanyang—in winter when the channel dried up, boats stuck fast.

sentences.zh: 江口奸民輒恃眾索詐，捕治，諭禁之。

translations.literal: Ruffians at the river mouth habitually relied on their numbers to extort; he captured and punished them and issued proclamations forbidding the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians at the river mouth routinely extorted passing boats with strength of numbers; he captured and punished them and posted notices forbidding it.

sentences.zh: 因病乞休沐，將去任，有淹訟久未決，慮貽後累，舁胡床至廳事判定，兩造感泣聽命。

translations.literal: Requesting sick leave as he was about to leave office, there remained a long-pending lawsuit he feared would burden his successor; he had a folding chair carried to the hall to decide it, and both parties wept and accepted the judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On sick leave and about to depart, a case had languished for years; fearing it would burden his successor, he had a chair carried into court and decided it on the spot—both sides wept and submitted.

sentences.zh: 值年飢，發賑，大吏知豪得民心，強起，力疾往，民夾道歡呼。

translations.literal: When famine struck he opened relief; senior officials knew Hao had the people's hearts and forcibly recalled him; he went despite illness, and the people lined the roads shouting welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck and he opened relief; knowing Hao had the people's loyalty, senior officials forced him back into service—he went despite illness, and crowds lined the roads to cheer him.

sentences.zh: 賑未半，復以疾去。

translations.literal: Relief was only half done when he again left because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Relief was barely half finished when illness forced him out again.

sentences.zh: 尋署隨州，素多盜，豪如治房縣時，置匭令自首。

translations.literal: Soon he served at Suizhou, which had always been bandit-ridden; as at Fang county, he placed a complaint box and ordered self-surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to bandit-plagued Suizhou, he did as at Fang county—set out a complaint box and urged surrender.

sentences.zh: 選賢紳，行保甲，盜風頓戢。

translations.literal: He selected worthy gentry, implemented the baojia system, and banditry was instantly suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: He picked capable gentry, enforced baojia, and banditry collapsed overnight.

sentences.zh: 俗多自戕圖詐，豪遇訟，實究虛坐，不稍徇，澆風革焉。

translations.literal: The custom was for many to injure themselves to commit fraud in lawsuits; when Hao heard cases he investigated the truth and punished false claims without favor—and the decadent custom was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Locals often mutilated themselves to fake injuries in lawsuits; Hao sifted truth from fraud and punished liars without mercy—and the corrupt custom died away.

sentences.zh: 立輔文社，選才雋者親教之，多所成就。

translations.literal: He established the Fuwén Society, selecting talented youths to teach them personally, and many achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Fuwén Society, personally teaching gifted youths—and many went on to distinction.

sentences.zh: 治隨二年，瀕行，聞代者好殺，竭數晝夜之力，凡獄情可原者，悉與判決免死。

translations.literal: After governing Suizhou for two years, on the eve of departure he heard his successor was bloodthirsty; he exhausted day and night, and for every case where mercy was possible, he judged and commuted the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: After two years at Suizhou, about to leave, he learned his successor was trigger-happy; he worked day and night to decide every case where mercy was possible and commute death sentences.

sentences.zh: 後因養母，乞免，歸。

translations.literal: Later, to care for his mother, he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked leave to care for his mother and went home.

sentences.zh: 浙中大吏輒諮要政，多所匡益。

translations.literal: Zhejiang's senior officials often consulted him on important policies, and he contributed much corrective advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's senior officials often sought his counsel on major policies, and he offered much sound advice.

sentences.zh: 家居十餘年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than ten years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than a decade and died.

sentences.zh: 豪在隨州，重修季梁祠。

translations.literal: While at Suizhou, Hao rebuilt the Jiliang Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: At Suizhou he restored the shrine to Jiliang.

sentences.zh: 及卒，隨人思其德，於西偏為建遺愛祠祀之。

translations.literal: After his death the people of Suizhou missed his virtue and built a Yiai Shrine on the west side to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of Suizhou, remembering his kindness, built a Legacy Shrine on the west side to honor him.

sentences.zh: =楊榮緒=楊榮緒，字黼香，廣東番禺人。

translations.literal: =Yang Rongxu= Yang Rongxu, style name Fuxiang, was a native of Panyu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rongxu, whose style was Fuxiang, came from Panyu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，擢御史。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Xianfeng, selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed editor, then promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1853, he entered the Hanlin, was appointed editor, and rose to censor.

sentences.zh: 英法聯軍犯京師，駕幸熱河，榮緒與同官抗疏請回鑾，又劾參贊國瑞★法營私，風裁頗著。

translations.literal: When the Anglo-French allied forces attacked the capital and the emperor fled to Rehe, Rongxu and fellow officials submitted a joint memorial requesting the court's return; he also impeached Counselor Guo Rui for private dealings with the French—his moral courage was widely noted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Anglo-French allies attacked Beijing and the emperor fled to Rehe, Rongxu and fellow officials submitted a joint memorial demanding the court's return; he also impeached Counselor Guo Rui for private dealings with the French—and his moral courage was widely noted.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，出為浙江湖州知府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he went out to serve as prefect of Huzhou, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he left the capital to become prefect of Huzhou in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 粵匪據湖州四年，時甫克復，荒墟白骨，闃無人煙。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels had held Huzhou for four years; it had just been recovered—wasteland strewn with white bones, utterly without human habitation.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese rebels had held Huzhou for four years. When the city was finally retaken, it was a wasteland of bleached bones—deserted and lifeless.

sentences.zh: 榮緒置善後局，規畫庶政，安集流亡，閭閻漸復。

translations.literal: Rongxu established a relief bureau, planned general administration, settled displaced refugees, and neighborhoods gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxu set up a relief office, reorganized civil affairs, and resettled refugees until the neighborhoods slowly came back to life.

sentences.zh: 屬縣糧冊無存，榮緒招來墾闢，試辦​​開徵，歲有起色。

translations.literal: The subordinate counties' grain registers were lost; Rongxu recruited people to reclaim and open land, tentatively resumed tax collection, and year by year conditions improved.
translations.idiomatic: Grain registers for the subordinate counties had vanished; Rongxu encouraged reclamation and cultivation, resumed tax collection on trial, and conditions improved year by year.

sentences.zh: 湖蠶利甲天下，經亂，桑盡伐，課民復種，貧者給以桑苗，絲業復興。

translations.literal: Huzhou's silkworms were the most profitable in the empire; through the turmoil mulberry trees were all cut down—Rongxu ordered the people to replant, gave saplings to the poor, and the silk industry revived.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou's silkworms ranked first in all the realm—yet the war had stripped every mulberry tree. Rongxu pressed the people to replant, gave saplings to the poor, and the silk trade rose again.

sentences.zh: 郡稱澤國，匯天目諸山之水入太湖，烏程、長興境內舊有漊港，各三十六，以為宣洩，亂後多淤塞。

translations.literal: The prefecture was called a water country; waters from the Tianmu mountains flowed into Lake Tai—within Wucheng and Changxing there had formerly been drainage channels, thirty-six each, for discharge and relief; after the turmoil many were silted up.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was known as a land of lakes and marshes, where waters from the Tianmu range drained into Lake Tai. Wucheng and Changxing each once had thirty-six drainage channels to carry off floodwater—and after the rebellion most were choked with silt.

sentences.zh: 五年，榮緒奉檄開濬，至八年粗畢，烏程漊港尤易淤，賴設閘以御湖水之倒灌。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Rongxu received orders to dredge and open them; by the eighth year the work was roughly finished. Wucheng's drainage channels especially silted easily, and he relied on sluice gates to guard against backflow from the lake waters.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Rongxu received orders to dredge them; by 1869 the work was largely done. Wucheng's channels silted up fastest, so he installed sluice gates to hold back the lake's backflow.
