sentences.zh: 九年，重修諸閘，因經費不充，頻年經營，猶未盡也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he rebuilt the various gates; because funds were insufficient, year after year he carried on the work, yet it was still not complete.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he rebuilt the gates, but funds ran short and he labored at it year after year—the work still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 十年，內閣侍讀學士鍾佩賢疏陳其事，朝命大加濬治，時榮緒舉卓異入覲，宗源瀚代攝郡，源瀚亦能事，規畫舉工。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Hanlin Reader Zhong Peixian memorialized on the matter; the court ordered large-scale dredging. At that time Rongxu was recommended as outstanding and went to audience; Zong Yuanhan acted as acting prefect in his stead—Yuanhan was also capable and planned the commencement of work.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 Hanlin Reader Zhong Peixian memorialized on the project and the court ordered a major dredging campaign. Rongxu was recommended for exceptional merit and summoned to court; Zong Yuanhan served as acting prefect and, himself a capable man, drew up plans to launch the work.

sentences.zh: 及榮緒回任，集絲捐，得鉅款，以資興作。

translations.literal: When Rongxu returned to his post, he collected a silk levy and obtained a huge sum to fund construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Rongxu returned to office he levied a silk tax and raised a large sum to bankroll construction.

sentences.zh: 屏去傔從，輕舟巡驗，常駐湖濱，逾年工始竣。

translations.literal: Setting aside attendants, he toured inspections in a light boat, often staying on the lakeshore; only after more than a year was the work completed.
translations.idiomatic: He left attendants behind, toured in a light skiff, and often camped on the lakeshore—more than a year passed before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 以漊港旋開旋淤，議定分年疏濬之法及鏟蘆、撈淺、閘版啟閉章程，數十年遵守不輟。

translations.literal: Because the drainage channels silted up again as soon as opened, he established regulations for dredging by rotation over the years and for weed-cutting, shallow dredging, and sluice gate schedules—followed without lapse for decades.
translations.idiomatic: Since the channels silted as fast as they were cleared, he set rules for dredging in annual rotation—cutting reeds, scooping shallows, opening and closing sluice gates—rules kept faithfully for decades.

sentences.zh: 又開碧浪湖，疏北塘河及城河。

translations.literal: He also opened Biolang Lake and dredged the Beitang River and the city moat.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened Biolang Lake and dredged the Beitang River and the city moat.

sentences.zh: 葺學校，建考舍，修書院，建倉庫，造橋樑，复育嬰堂，百廢具舉。

translations.literal: He repaired schools, built examination halls, restored academies, erected granaries, constructed bridges, revived foundling homes—a hundred neglected works all taken up.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired schools, built examination halls, restored academies, put up granaries, built bridges, and revived foundling homes—every long-neglected project got done.

sentences.zh: 鞫獄詳審，吏胥立侍相更代，終日無倦容。

translations.literal: He examined cases with meticulous care; clerks stood attending in rotation, and he showed no weariness all day long.
translations.idiomatic: He heard cases with painstaking care; clerks stood by in relays, and he never showed fatigue all day.

sentences.zh: 親受訟牒，指其虛謬，曰：「勿為胥吏所用也。」

translations.literal: He personally received petitions, pointing out their falsehoods, saying: "Do not let yourselves be manipulated by clerks."
translations.idiomatic: He took petitions in person, pointed out fabrications, and said, "Do not let the clerks use you."

sentences.zh: 手書牒尾，輒數百言，剖析曲直，人咸服之。

translations.literal: He personally wrote at the foot of each petition, often hundreds of words, dissecting right and wrong—and everyone submitted to his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of each petition he would write hundreds of words himself, weighing right and wrong—and all parties accepted his rulings.

sentences.zh: 訟以日稀，刑具朽敝。

translations.literal: Lawsuits grew fewer day by day, and the torture implements rotted from disuse.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits dwindled daily, and the torture instruments rotted unused.

sentences.zh: 隸役坐府門，賣瓜果自活。

translations.literal: Runners sat at the prefectural gate selling fruit and melons to earn a living.
translations.idiomatic: Runners sat at the prefectural gate selling fruit to make a living.

sentences.zh: 客坐無供張，儉素如布衣時，遠近頌為賢守。

translations.literal: When guests sat there was no lavish spread; he lived as plainly as in commoner days—and far and near praised him as a worthy prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He offered guests no lavish hospitality and lived as plainly as when he was a commoner—men far and near hailed him as a model prefect.

sentences.zh: 在任十年，嗣為人所譖，遂求去。

translations.literal: After ten years in office, he was subsequently slandered by others and requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years into his term he was slandered and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 捐昇道員，離任。

translations.literal: He purchased promotion to circuit intendant and left his post.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased promotion to circuit intendant and departed.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 郡人思之，請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture missed him and petitioned for his enshrinement in the shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: The people missed him and petitioned to enshrine him in the hall of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: =林啟=林啟，字迪臣，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: =Lin Qi= Lin Qi, style name Dichen, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qi, whose style was Dichen, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Guangxu, selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed editor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1876, he entered the Hanlin, and was appointed editor.

sentences.zh: 督陝西學政，馭士嚴正。

translations.literal: He supervised Shaanxi provincial examinations and governed scholars with stern rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: As Shaanxi education commissioner he managed candidates with stern fairness.

sentences.zh: 任滿，遷御史，直言敢諫，稽察祿米倉，不受陋規，為時所稱。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he was transferred to censor; he spoke bluntly and dared remonstrate, inspected the salary-grain granary, accepted no improper fees—and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end he rose to censor, spoke frankly in remonstrance, audited the salary-grain granary, took no illicit gifts—and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出為浙江衢州知府，多惠政。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he went out to serve as prefect of Quzhou, Zhejiang, with many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1893 he became prefect of Quzhou in Zhejiang and governed with many kindnesses.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調杭州，除衙蠹，通民隱，禁無名苛稅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, transferred to Hangzhou—he rooted out yamen parasites, heard the people's hidden grievances, and banned nameless extortionate levies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1896 he was moved to Hangzhou, uprooted yamen parasites, gave voice to popular grievances, and banned nameless exactions.

sentences.zh: 餘杭巨猾楊乃武，因姦通民婦葛畢氏，興大獄。

translations.literal: The Yuhang great scoundrel Yang Naiwu, on account of an affair with the commoner's wife Mrs. Ge Bi, stirred up a major case.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Naiwu, a notorious Yuhang thug, had an affair with a commoner's wife, Mrs. Ge Bi—and a great scandal erupted.

sentences.zh: 刑部訊治，倖免重罪。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments tried the case; he fortunately escaped heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tried by the Ministry of Punishments, he narrowly escaped a heavy sentence.

sentences.zh: 歸則益橫，攬訟事，挾制官吏，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Upon returning he grew even more overbearing, monopolized lawsuits, coerced officials—and none dared cross him.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he grew bolder still, seized control of lawsuits, and bullied officials—none dared stand up to him.

sentences.zh: 啟捕治之，乃武控京師，不為動，卒論如法。

translations.literal: Qi arrested and punished him; Naiwu petitioned the capital but Qi was unmoved, and Naiwu was finally judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had him arrested; Naiwu petitioned Beijing, but Qi held firm and had him sentenced as the law required.

sentences.zh: 尤以興學為急務，時各行省學堂猶未普立，杭郡甫建求是書院，啟复養正書塾，並課新學。

translations.literal: He especially made promoting schools an urgent task; at the time new-style schools in provinces were not yet widespread—Hangzhou had just built the Qiushi Academy; Qi also restored the Yangzheng private school and taught new learning alongside.
translations.idiomatic: He made education his top priority. New-style provincial schools were still rare; Hangzhou had only just opened the Qiushi Academy. Qi also revived the Yangzheng school and taught modern subjects alongside the classics.

sentences.zh: 舊有東城講舍，益振興之。

translations.literal: The old Eastern City Lecture Hall—he further revived it.
translations.idiomatic: He also revived the old Eastern City Lecture Hall.

sentences.zh: 兼經義、治事，陰主程、硃之說，而變其面目。

translations.literal: Combining classical meaning and practical governance, he covertly upheld the teachings of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi but changed their outward form.
translations.idiomatic: He taught both classical philosophy and practical governance—privately upholding the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, but in a transformed guise.

sentences.zh: 誘諸生研尋義理，以成有用，一時優秀之士皆歸之。

translations.literal: He drew students to investigate principle and become useful men—and for a time all outstanding talents gathered under him.
translations.idiomatic: He drew students to pursue moral principle and practical skill—and for a time all the finest young men flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 又以浙中蠶業甲天下，設蠶學館於西湖，講求新法，成效頗著。

translations.literal: Also, because Zhejiang's sericulture ranked first in the realm, he established a Sericulture Academy on West Lake, seeking new methods—with marked results.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's sericulture ranked first in the realm, so he founded a Sericulture Academy on West Lake to teach modern methods—with notable success.

sentences.zh: 遇國外交涉事，持正無遷就，遠人亦心服。

translations.literal: In matters involving foreign relations, he held to rectitude without compromise—and even foreigners respected him in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: On matters of foreign relations he stood firm without compromise—even foreigners came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 治杭四年，剛直不阿，喜接布衣，士民翕然頌之。

translations.literal: Governing Hangzhou four years—upright and unyielding, fond of receiving commoners—scholars and people alike praised him in unison.
translations.idiomatic: Four years at Hangzhou: upright and unbending, he welcomed commoners freely—and scholars and townsfolk praised him as one.

sentences.zh: 卒官，葬於孤山林處士墓側，杭人歲設祭焉，號曰林社，久而勿輟。

translations.literal: He died in office; buried beside the Hermit of Gushan's tomb. Hangzhou people set up annual sacrifices, called it the Lin Society—and for long they did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was buried beside the Hermit of Gushan's tomb. Hangzhou people held annual rites there, calling it the Lin Society—a tradition that endured.

sentences.zh: 啟之治杭，​​得友高鳳岐為之助，後官廣西梧州知府，亦有聲。

translations.literal: In Qi's governance of Hangzhou, he had his friend Gao Fengqi to assist him; Gao later served as prefect of Wuzhou in Guangxi and also gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: Governing Hangzhou, Qi had the help of his friend Gao Fengqi; Gao later became prefect of Wuzhou in Guangxi and won renown of his own.

sentences.zh: 歿而杭人附祀於林社雲。

translations.literal: After his death Hangzhou people enshrined him alongside at the Lin Society.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao's death Hangzhou people added him to the rites at the Lin Society.

sentences.zh: =王仁福=王仁福，字竹林，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: =Wang Renfu= Wang Renfu, style name Zhulin, was a native of Wu county in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renfu, whose style was Zhulin, came from Wu county in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少誠愨，勇於任事。

translations.literal: From youth he was honest and sincere, bold in taking responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was honest and resolute, bold to take on hard tasks.

sentences.zh: 祖宦河南，歿後，仁福扶柩歸葬。

translations.literal: His grandfather served in Henan; after his death Renfu carried the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served in Henan; after his death Renfu escorted the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 道經徐州，遇捻匪，徒步率廝役出入烽火，肩行四十里，竟免。

translations.literal: Passing through Xuzhou, he encountered Nian bandits; on foot he led servants in and out of battle lines, carrying the coffin on shoulders forty li, and finally escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xuzhou he ran into Nian bandits; on foot he led servants through the fighting, bearing the coffin on their shoulders for forty li—and at last got away.

sentences.zh: 尋入貲為東河同知。

translations.literal: Soon he purchased appointment as Eastern River intendant sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he purchased appointment as sub-prefect on the Eastern River conservancy.

sentences.zh: 粵匪犯開封，城壕沙淤如平地，仁福奉檄督工濬治，剋期蕆事而賊至，城守賴之。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels attacked Kaifeng; the moat sand silted level as ground. Renfu received orders to supervise dredging, completed it on schedule just as the rebels arrived—the city's defense depended on this.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels attacked Kaifeng, the moat had silted flat as dry land. Renfu was ordered to dredge it, finished on schedule just as the rebels arrived—and the city held thanks to his work.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，署祥河廳同知。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi, he served as acting sub-prefect of Xianghe sub-prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he served as acting sub-prefect of the Xianghe office.

sentences.zh: 黃河自北徙，中原多故，工帑大減。

translations.literal: The Yellow River had shifted northward; the Central Plains faced many troubles, and engineering funds were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River had shifted north, the Central Plains were in turmoil, and conservancy funds plummeted.

sentences.zh: 頻年軍事亟，發帑復不以時。

translations.literal: Year after year military affairs were urgent, and treasury disbursements again were not timely.
translations.idiomatic: War after war drained the treasury, and funds no longer arrived on time.

sentences.zh: 歲修不敷，堤埽殘缺，料無宿儲。

translations.literal: Annual repairs could not cover costs; dikes and revetments were broken and missing; materials had no stock in reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Annual repairs fell short; dikes and revetments crumbled; there were no materials in store.

sentences.zh: 祥河汛地當衝，險工迭出，人皆視為畏途。

translations.literal: Xianghe's flood-season territory sat in the path of danger; perilous works appeared one after another—all regarded it as a road of dread.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghe's flood zone stood in the line of danger, one perilous breach after another—everyone treated it as a death trap.

sentences.zh: 仁福盡力修守，不避艱危。

translations.literal: Renfu exerted all strength in repair and defense, not shunning hardship and danger.
translations.idiomatic: Renfu threw himself into repair and defense without flinching from danger.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，汛水驟漲，掣埽去如削木★H9。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year flood waters suddenly rose; the revetments were torn away as if shaved from wood.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn floodwaters surged; revetments were torn away as if planed from wood.

sentences.zh: 仁福奔走風雨泥淖中，搶護曆七晝夜。

translations.literal: Renfu rushed about through wind, rain, and mire, emergency repairs through seven days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Renfu worked through wind, rain, and mud for seven days and nights straight.

sentences.zh: 款料俱竭，堤岌岌將破。

translations.literal: Funds and materials were all exhausted; the dike teetered on the brink of breach.
translations.idiomatic: Funds and materials gave out; the dike teetered on the verge of collapse.

sentences.zh: 居民蟻附堤上，仁福對之流涕，曰：「我為河官，擠汝等於死，我之罪也，當身先之！」

translations.literal: Residents clung to the dike like ants; Renfu wept before them, saying: "I am a river official who has driven you toward death—that is my crime. I must go first!"
translations.idiomatic: Villagers clung to the dike like ants. Renfu wept and said, "As a river official I have brought you to the edge of death—that is my guilt. I must go first!"

sentences.zh: 躍立埽巔。

translations.literal: He leapt and stood atop the revetment crest.
translations.idiomatic: He leapt onto the crest of the revetment.

sentences.zh: 風浪捲埽，走入大溜沉沒。

translations.literal: Wind and waves swept the revetment; he was carried into the main current and sank.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and waves tore away the revetment; he was swept into the main channel and drowned.

sentences.zh: 河聲如吼，堤前水陡落。

translations.literal: The river roared like thunder; the water before the dike suddenly fell.
translations.idiomatic: The river roared; the water in front of the dike dropped sharply.

sentences.zh: 風止浪定，大溜改趨，殘堤得保。

translations.literal: Wind ceased, waves settled; the main current changed course, and the damaged dike was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and waves died, the main current shifted course—and the battered dike held.

sentences.zh: 眾咸驚為精誠所格，令善泅者覓其屍，不得，乃以衣冠斂。

translations.literal: All were astonished, believing his sincere devotion had moved Heaven. They sent good swimmers to search for his corpse but found none, and so interred his clothes in lieu.
translations.idiomatic: All marveled that his devotion had moved Heaven. Skilled swimmers searched for his body in vain; they buried his clothing in his stead.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔依陣亡例賜卹，附祀河神祠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict granted condolence payments as for death in battle and enshrinement in the River God Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict granted battle-death compensation and enshrinement in the River God Shrine.

sentences.zh: =硃光第=硃光第，字杏簪，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: =Zhu Guangdi= Zhu Guangdi, style name Xingzan, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guangdi, whose style was Xingzan, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，幕游江南，奉汪輝祖佐治藥言為圭臬。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he traveled the south as a legal secretary, taking Wang Huizu's Yaoyan as his standard for assisting in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he clerked across the south, taking Wang Huizu's Yaoyan as his guide to magisterial practice.

sentences.zh: 咸豐末，捻匪方熾，佐蕭縣令籌防禦，屢破賊。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianfeng, Nian bandits were raging; he assisted the Xiao county magistrate in planning defense and repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xianfeng reign, as Nian bandits raged, he helped the magistrate of Xiao county plan defenses and broke the rebels again and again.

sentences.zh: 都統伊興額上其功，累晉秩知州，分發河南，佐讞局，治獄平。

translations.literal: Banner General Yi Xinge reported his merits; he was repeatedly promoted to prefect rank, assigned to Henan, assisted the judicial bureau, and tried cases fairly.
translations.idiomatic: Banner General Yi Xinge reported his service; he rose by stages to prefect, was assigned to Henan, served in the judicial bureau, and judged cases fairly.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，補鄧州。

translations.literal: During Guangxu, he was appointed to Deng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu he was posted to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，大祲之後，壹意休養。

translations.literal: Three years in office, after a great famine, he devoted himself wholly to recovery and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Three years in office after a great famine, he devoted himself entirely to recovery.

sentences.zh: 善治盜，民戴之。

translations.literal: Skilled at controlling bandits; the people revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at suppressing bandits, he won the people's devotion.

sentences.zh: 王樹汶者，鄧人，為鎮平盜魁胡體安執爨。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen was a man of Deng; he cooked for Hu Ti'an, a bandit chief of Zhenping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen of Dengzhou had cooked for Hu Ti'an, a bandit chief of Zhenping.

sentences.zh: 鎮平令捕體安急，乃賄役以樹汶偽冒，致之獄。

translations.literal: The Zhenping magistrate urgently sought to capture Ti'an; he bribed runners to substitute Shuwen as an impostor and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenping magistrate urgently hunted Ti'an; he bribed runners to substitute Shuwen and throw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 既定讞，臨刑呼冤。

translations.literal: Once the verdict was set, at execution he cried out his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict stood—at execution he cried that he was wronged.

sentences.zh: 重鞫，則檄光第逮其父季福為驗。

translations.literal: On re-trial, an order was sent for Guangdi to arrest his father Jifu for verification.
translations.idiomatic: On retrial, Guangdi was ordered to arrest the man's father, Jifu, for identification.

sentences.zh: 開歸陳許道任愷先守南陽，嘗讞是獄，馳書阻毋逮季福。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant Ren Kai of Kaigui-Chenxu, formerly prefect of Nanyang, had judged this case; he wrote urgently to block arresting Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai, intendant of the Kaigui-Chenxu circuit and former prefect of Nanyang, who had tried the case, wrote urgently to forbid arresting Jifu.

sentences.zh: 且誘怵之。

translations.literal: And also tried to entice and intimidate him.
translations.idiomatic: He also tried to bribe and intimidate Guangdi.

sentences.zh: 光第曰：「吾安能惜此官以陷無辜？」

translations.literal: Guangdi said: "How could I cherish this office and frame the innocent?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangdi replied, "How can I keep this office by framing an innocent man?"

sentences.zh: 竟以季福上，則樹汶果其子。

translations.literal: In the end he brought Jifu forward—and Shuwen indeed proved to be his son.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Jifu forward anyway—and Shuwen proved to be his son.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李鶴年袒愷，持初讞益堅。

translations.literal: Governor Li Henian sided with Kai and held to the original verdict all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Henian sided with Ren Kai and clung all the more to the original verdict.

sentences.zh: 河南官科道者，交章論其事。

translations.literal: Henan censorial and examining officials submitted successive memorials debating the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and examiners across Henan submitted memorial after memorial on the case.

sentences.zh: 命東河總督梅啟照覆訊，樹汶猶不得直，眾論大譁。

translations.literal: The Eastern River Governor-General Mei Qizhao was ordered to re-hear the case; yet Shuwen still could not get justice, and public outrage was great.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Mei Qizhao of the Eastern River was ordered to rehear the case—yet Shuwen still could not get justice, and outrage spread.

sentences.zh: 刑部提鞫，乃得實。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments took up the trial and finally established the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments took up the case and established the truth.

sentences.zh: 釋樹汶，自鶴年、啟照以次譴黜有差，而光第已先為鶴年摭他事劾去官，貧不能歸，卒於河南。

translations.literal: Shuwen was released; from Henian and Qizhao downward punishments and dismissals were meted out in order—but Guangdi had already been impeached on other charges by Henian and removed from office, too poor to return home, and died in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was freed; Henian, Qizhao, and others were punished in turn—but Guangdi had already been impeached on other grounds by Henian, stripped of office, too poor to go home, and died in Henan.

sentences.zh: 後鄧州士民請祀名宦，以子祖謀官禮部侍郎，格於例，不行。

translations.literal: Later Dengzhou scholars and people petitioned for his enshrinement among eminent officials; his son Zu Mou held office as vice minister of rites—but precedent barred it, and the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Later the people of Dengzhou petitioned to enshrine him—but his son Zu Mou was vice minister of rites, precedent barred it, and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: =冷鼎亨=冷鼎亨，字鎮雄，山東招遠人。

translations.literal: =Leng Dingheng= Leng Dingheng, style name Zhenxiong, was a native of Zhaoyuan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Dingheng, whose style was Zhenxiong, came from Zhaoyuan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治四年進士，即用知縣，發江西，署瑞昌。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourth year of Tongzhi, immediately appointed magistrate, assigned to Jiangxi, acting at Ruichang.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1865, he was immediately appointed magistrate, assigned to Jiangxi, and served at Ruichang.

sentences.zh: 地瘠而健訟，鄉愚輒因之破家。

translations.literal: The land was barren and litigation fierce; rustic fools often ruined their families thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The county was poor and litigious; simple country folk often lost everything in lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 捕訟師及猾吏數人，繩以法。

translations.literal: He arrested several litigation masters and corrupt clerks and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested litigation brokers and corrupt clerks and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 因事詣鄉，使胥役盡隨輿後，返則令居前而己殿之，未嘗以杯勺累民。

translations.literal: When business took him to the countryside, he had runners all follow behind the sedan; on the return he had them walk ahead while he brought up the rear—never burdening the people with even a cup or spoon of hospitality.
translations.idiomatic: On country visits he made runners walk behind his sedan; on the return he had them go ahead while he brought up the rear—never imposing even a cup of tea on the villagers.

sentences.zh: 調署德化，懲防軍之陵民者，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Transferred to act at Dehua, he punished garrison soldiers who bullied the people—and order reigned within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Dehua, he punished garrison soldiers who preyed on civilians—and the district grew calm.

sentences.zh: 修瀕江堤塘，費省工速。

translations.literal: He repaired riverfront dikes and embankments—costs saved, work speeded.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired river dikes and embankments at low cost and with speed.

sentences.zh: 德化、瑞昌、黃梅三邑民爭蘆洲，累歲相鬥殺。

translations.literal: People of Dehua, Ruichang, and Huangmei three counties fought over reed flats, killing each other year after year.
translations.idiomatic: People of Dehua, Ruichang, and Huangmei fought over reed flats, killing one another year after year.

sentences.zh: 鼎亨諭解之，建台於鬥所，官吏誓不私，民皆悅服。

translations.literal: Dingheng admonished and settled them, built a platform at the fighting ground, officials swore not to show favoritism—and the people all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Leng admonished and settled them, built a platform at the contested site, and had officials swear impartiality—the people submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 白鶴鄉人叔與侄爭田，即樹下諭解，遂悔悟如初。

translations.literal: In Baihe township, an uncle and nephew disputed fields; right under a tree he admonished and settled them—and they repented as at first.
translations.idiomatic: In Baihe township an uncle and nephew disputed fields; he settled them under a tree, and they made peace as before.

sentences.zh: 旱，蝗起，徒步烈日中，掩捕經月，露宿禱神，得雨，蝗皆死。

translations.literal: Drought—locusts arose; he walked in blazing sun, hand-catching them for a month, slept in the open praying to the gods; rain came and the locusts all died.
translations.idiomatic: During drought locusts appeared; he walked in the blazing sun catching them by hand for a month, slept outdoors praying for rain—and when rain came the locusts died.

sentences.zh: 歷署新昌、彭澤，皆有實政。

translations.literal: He served at Xinchang and Pengze in succession—both with concrete achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Stints at Xinchang and Pengze alike produced solid results.

sentences.zh: 上官以為賢，調補新建。

translations.literal: Superiors deemed him worthy and transferred him to fill the post at Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors judged him worthy and transferred him to Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 附省首邑，官斯者多昕夕伺上官，不遑治民事。

translations.literal: A first county adjacent to the provincial capital—magistrates there often rose early and stayed late attending superiors, with no leisure to govern the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xinjian was the premier county beside the provincial seat; magistrates there spent their days courting superiors, with no time left for the people's business.

sentences.zh: 鼎亨先與上官約，屏酬應，親聽斷，民歌頌之。

translations.literal: Dingheng first made an agreement with superiors to set aside social courtesies, hear cases personally—and the people sang his praises.
translations.idiomatic: First Leng struck a bargain with his superiors: no more currying favor—he would judge cases himself. The people sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 尋調鄱陽，值大水，發賑親勘給印票，盡除侵蝕舊習。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Poyang—great flood struck; he issued relief, personally inspected and gave stamped vouchers, fully abolishing the old practice of embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Poyang just as a great flood struck. He opened relief himself, inspected distribution in person, and issued stamped ration tickets—rooting out the old customs of graft.

sentences.zh: 次年，复災，跣足立沮洳中，濕疾遍體，十閱月。

translations.literal: The next year disaster struck again; barefoot he stood in mud and marsh, damp illness over his whole body—for ten months.
translations.idiomatic: The next year disaster came again. Barefoot he stood in the mire; damp sickness spread over his body and lingered ten months.

sentences.zh: 常小舟行駭浪中，屢瀕於危，深夜返署理訟牘。

translations.literal: Often in a small boat amid terrifying waves, repeatedly near peril—returning late at night to the yamen to handle case documents.
translations.idiomatic: He often crossed terrifying waves in a small boat, repeatedly near death—and returned to the yamen at midnight to handle the docket.

sentences.zh: 侍郎彭玉麟巡江過境，寄書巡撫曰：「某所至三江五湖數千里，未見堅剛耐苦如冷知縣者也。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister Peng Yulin, on patrol of the river, passed through and sent a letter to the governor saying: "In all the thousands of li I have traveled through the three rivers and five lakes, I have never seen one as steadfast and enduring hardship as Magistrate Leng."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Peng Yulin passed through on a river inspection and wrote the governor: "In all my thousands of li across rivers and lakes, I have never met a magistrate as tough and tireless as Magistrate Leng."

sentences.zh: 歷官十年，食無兼味，妻子衣履皆自製。

translations.literal: Ten years in office—meals without a second dish; wife and children's clothing and shoes all homemade.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years in office, his meals never had a second dish; his wife and children wore clothes and shoes they made themselves.

sentences.zh: 以廉率下，胥吏幾無以為生。

translations.literal: Leading subordinates by integrity, clerks and runners could barely make a living.
translations.idiomatic: He led by example in frugality, and his clerks and runners could barely scrape by.

sentences.zh: 俸入輒捐為地方興利，訓士以氣節為先。

translations.literal: Salary income he always donated for local public benefit; in instructing scholars he put integrity of character first.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his salary to local public works and taught scholars that moral backbone came first.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽俗好鬥，鼎亨曰：「化民有本，未教而殺之，非義也。」

translations.literal: Poyang's custom favored brawling; Dingheng said: "Transforming the people has its root—executing them before teaching is not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: Poyang was a brawling county. Leng said: "Reforming the people must begin at the root—putting them to death before teaching them is not just."

sentences.zh: 以孝經證聖祖聖諭廣訓為淺說，婦孺聞之皆感動。

translations.literal: Using the Classic of Filial Piety to illustrate the Sacred Edict of the Kangxi Emperor as plain discourse, women and children who heard it were all moved.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured from the Classic of Filial Piety and the Sacred Edict in plain language—and women and children who heard him were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 治教案必持平，屢遇民、教齟《齒吾》事，桀黠者欲藉以鼓眾毀教堂，慮遺禍好官而止，蓋有以感之。

translations.literal: In handling mission cases he always held the balance; repeatedly encountering friction between common people and Christians, the cunning wished to use it to stir crowds to destroy churches—yet fearing to bring harm upon a good official they desisted, having been moved by him in some way.
translations.idiomatic: In mission disputes he always held the balance. When friction arose between locals and Christians, the cunning tried to stir mobs to burn churches—but fearing to harm so good a magistrate, they held back, moved by his integrity.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，擢南昌府同知，巡撫潘霨疏薦入覲，遂乞歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu he was promoted to sub-prefect of Nanchang Prefecture; Governor Pan Yi memorialized recommending him for audience—he then begged to retire and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was promoted to sub-prefect of Nanchang. Governor Pan Yi recommended him for audience at court; he asked to retire instead and died at home.

sentences.zh: =孫葆田=孫葆田，字佩南，山東榮成人。

translations.literal: =Sun Baotian= Sun Baotian, style name Peinan, was a native of Rongcheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Baotian, whose style was Peinan, came from Rongcheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，授刑部主事，改知縣，銓授安徽宿松。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, changed to magistrate, and assigned by selection to Susong in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1874, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, then transferred to the magistracy and posted to Susong in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 勤政愛民，日坐堂皇，妻紡績，室中蕭然如寒士。

translations.literal: Diligent in governance and loving the people, he sat daily in the hall of justice; his wife spun and wove—the household bare as a poor scholar's.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and devoted to the people, he sat in court every day while his wife spun thread; their home was as bare as a poor scholar's.

sentences.zh: 調合肥，大學士李鴻章弟子之傔人橫於鄉，以逼債毆人死。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hefei—an attendant of Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang's disciple bullied the countryside and beat a man to death while pressing for debt.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hefei, he confronted an attendant of one of Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang's disciples who had been terrorizing the countryside and beat a man to death over a debt.

sentences.zh: 葆田檢驗屍傷，觀者數万人，恐縣令為豪強迫脅驗不實。

translations.literal: Baotian examined the corpse's wounds; tens of thousands watched, fearing the magistrate would be coerced by the powerful into a false finding.
translations.idiomatic: Baotian examined the corpse before tens of thousands of onlookers who feared the magistrate would be bullied into a false report.

sentences.zh: 葆田命仵作曰：「敢欺罔者論如律。」

translations.literal: Baotian ordered the coroner: "Whoever dares to deceive shall be punished according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Baotian told the coroner: "Anyone who falsifies the report will be punished by law."

sentences.zh: 得致命狀，人皆歡噪，謂包龍圖復出，讞遂定。

translations.literal: The fatal wounds were found; the crowd all cheered and clamored, saying Judge Bao had returned—the verdict was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The fatal wounds were confirmed. The crowd erupted in cheers, declaring that Judge Bao had returned—and the verdict stood.

sentences.zh: 有御史劾葆田誤入人死罪，詔巡撫陳彝按之，卒直原讞。

translations.literal: A censor impeached Baotian for wrongly imposing the death penalty; the throne ordered Governor Chen Yi to investigate—and in the end the original verdict was upheld.
translations.idiomatic: A censor accused Baotian of wrongly imposing the death sentence. The throne ordered Governor Chen Yi to investigate—and upheld the original verdict.

sentences.zh: 葆田遂自免歸，名聞天下。

translations.literal: Baotian then resigned and returned home—his fame spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Baotian resigned and went home, and his name spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 逾數年，安徽將清丈民田，巡撫福潤疏調葆田主其事，辭不赴。

translations.literal: After several years Anhui was to conduct a land survey of private fields; Governor Fu Run memorialized to transfer Baotian to head it—he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, when Anhui planned a land survey, Governor Fu Run asked Baotian to lead it. He refused.

sentences.zh: 貽書當事，言清丈病民，陳：「清賦之要，熟地報荒者，當寬其既往，限年墾复。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to those in charge, saying land surveys harmed the people, stating: "The key to clearing tax registers: for cultivated land reported as wasteland, past offenses should be forgiven and reclamation allowed within a set term.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the authorities that land surveys hurt the people and argued: "The key to fair taxation is this: where cultivated land was reported as wasteland, forgive the past and set a deadline for reclamation.

sentences.zh: 平歲報災者，當警其將來，分年帶徵。

translations.literal: For normal years reporting disaster, the future should be warned and arrears collected over several years.
translations.idiomatic: Where disaster was reported in normal years, warn them for the future and collect arrears in installments.

sentences.zh: 弊自可除，無事紛擾。」

translations.literal: Abuses can thus be removed without needless turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: Abuses can be removed without needless upheaval."

sentences.zh: 時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a celebrated saying.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was hailed as sage counsel.

sentences.zh: 葆田故從武昌張裕釗受古文法，治經，實事求是，不薄宋儒。

translations.literal: Baotian had studied ancient prose under Zhang Yujian of Wuchang, pursued the classics, sought truth from facts, and did not slight Song Neo-Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Baotian had studied classical prose under Zhang Yujian of Wuchang, devoted himself to the classics, sought truth from facts, and did not dismiss the Song Neo-Confucians.

sentences.zh: 歷主山東、河南書院，學者奉為大師。

translations.literal: He successively headed academies in Shandong and Henan; scholars revered him as a great master.
translations.idiomatic: He headed academies in Shandong and Henan in turn, and scholars hailed him as a master.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張曜疏陳其學行，賜五品卿銜。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Yao memorialized on his learning and conduct; he was granted the rank of fifth-grade honorary court official.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Yao memorialized on his scholarship and character, and he was granted fifth-rank honorary court rank.

sentences.zh: 中外大臣迭薦之，詔徵，不出。

translations.literal: Ministers at court and in the provinces recommended him in succession; the throne summoned him—he did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers at court and in the provinces recommended him again and again; the throne summoned him, but he would not leave home.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1909, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: =柯劭憼=柯劭憼，字敬儒，山東膠州人。

translations.literal: =Ke Shaojing= Ke Shaojing, style name Jingru, was a native of Jiaozhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Shaojing, whose style was Jingru, came from Jiaozhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年進士，即用知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifteenth year of Guangxu, immediately appointed magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1889, he was immediately appointed magistrate.

sentences.zh: 亦官安徽，署貴池，補太湖。

translations.literal: He also served in Anhui—acting at Guichi, then filling the post at Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Anhui as well, first acting at Guichi, then posted to Taihu.

sentences.zh: 貴池自粵匪亂後，地丁冊為吏所匿，託言已毀。

translations.literal: Since the Cantonese rebels' turmoil at Guichi, the land-and-poll tax registers had been hidden by clerks, who claimed they were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taiping rebellion, Guichi's land-tax registers had been hidden by clerks who claimed they were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 徵賦由吏包納，十不及四五，而浮收日甚，民苦之。

translations.literal: Tax collection was contracted to clerks who paid in lump sums—barely four or five parts in ten reached the treasury, while illegal surcharges grew daily; the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks collected taxes in lump sums and remitted barely forty or fifty percent—while illegal surcharges grew daily. The people suffered.

sentences.zh: 劭憼知其弊，令花戶自封投櫃，吏百計撓之，不為動。

translations.literal: Shaojing knew the abuse; he ordered registered households to seal their own payments and deposit them in the chest—clerks tried every scheme to obstruct him, but he did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing saw the abuse and ordered tax households to seal their own payments and drop them in the collection chest. Clerks tried every trick to stop him; he would not budge.

sentences.zh: 民輸將恐後，增收銀二萬餘兩，民所節省數且倍。

translations.literal: The people paid in fear of being late; collected revenue rose by more than twenty thousand taels of silver—the people's savings were nearly double that.
translations.idiomatic: Taxpayers rushed to pay ahead of deadline. Revenue rose by more than twenty thousand taels—while the people saved nearly twice as much.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄧華熙初聽浮言將奏劾，總督劉坤一曰：「柯令，皖中循吏，奈何登於彈章？」

translations.literal: Governor Deng Huaxi at first heard slander and was about to memorialize for impeachment; Governor-General Liu Kunyi said: "Magistrate Ke is Anhui's exemplary official—how can he appear on an impeachment memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: Governor Deng Huaxi, swayed by rumor, nearly impeached him. Governor-General Liu Kunyi said: "Magistrate Ke is Anhui's model official—how can he be named in an impeachment?"

sentences.zh: 華熙悟，遂疏薦送覲，晉秩直隸州。

translations.literal: Huaxi came to his senses, then memorialized recommending him for audience and promoted his rank to direct-controlled prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huaxi saw his error, recommended Ke for audience at court, and promoted him to direct-controlled prefect.

sentences.zh: 劭憼為治清簡，斷獄明決，所至民愛戴。

translations.literal: Shaojing's governance was clear and simple, his judgments decisive—wherever he went the people loved and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing governed with clarity and simplicity and judged cases decisively; wherever he served, the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 亦績學，善為古今體詩。

translations.literal: He was also a scholar of accomplishment, skilled in poetry in both ancient and modern styles.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a scholar and a fine poet in both classical and modern styles.

sentences.zh: 時與葆田並稱儒吏。

translations.literal: At the time he and Baotian were jointly called scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he and Sun Baotian were known together as scholar-magistrates.

sentences.zh: =塗官俊=塗官俊，字劭卿，江西東鄉人。

translations.literal: =Tu Guanjun= Tu Guanjun, style name Shaoqing, was a native of Dongxiang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Guanjun, whose style was Shaoqing, came from Dongxiang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，截取知縣，發陝西，署富平、涇陽、長安諸縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Guangxu, selected as magistrate, assigned to Shaanxi, acting at Fuping, Jingyang, Chang'an and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1876, he was selected as magistrate and sent to Shaanxi, serving at Fuping, Jingyang, Chang'an, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 補宜君，山邑地瘠民樸，官此者多不事事。

translations.literal: He filled the post at Yijun—a mountain county, land barren and people simple; magistrates there often neglected their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Yijun, a poor mountain county of plain folk, he found that magistrates there usually did little.

sentences.zh: 官俊勸農桑，興水利，成稻田數百畝。

translations.literal: Guanjun promoted farming and sericulture, developed waterworks, and brought several hundred mu of rice paddies into cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun promoted farming and sericulture, built irrigation works, and opened several hundred mu of rice paddies.

sentences.zh: 躬巡阡陌，與民絮語如家人。

translations.literal: He personally toured the fields and lanes, chatting with the people like family.
translations.idiomatic: He walked the fields himself and chatted with villagers like family.

sentences.zh: 調涇陽，歷官皆有聲。

translations.literal: Transferred to Jingyang—every post he held won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jingyang, he earned a reputation at every post.

sentences.zh: 凡兩任涇陽，政績尤著。

translations.literal: Having served twice at Jingyang, his achievements there were especially notable.
translations.idiomatic: He served Jingyang twice, and his achievements there were especially notable.

sentences.zh: 初至，值回亂後，清積訟千餘，庶政以次規复，期年而改觀。

translations.literal: On first arrival, after the Muslim rebellion, he cleared more than a thousand backlogged cases; general administration was restored step by step—in a year the county was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived after the Muslim rebellion, he cleared more than a thousand backlogged cases and restored civil administration step by step. Within a year the county was transformed.

sentences.zh: 龍洞渠，故白渠也，官俊倡言開濬，眾議以工鉅為難，獨毅然為之。

translations.literal: Longdong Canal was the old Bai Canal; Guanjun advocated dredging and opening it—the crowd argued the work was too vast, but he alone resolutely undertook it.
translations.idiomatic: Longdong Canal was the ancient Bai Canal. Guanjun proposed dredging it; others said the work was too costly, but he went ahead alone.

sentences.zh: 由梯子關而下，水量增三分之一，复於清冶河畔修復廢渠二，水所不至者，勸民鑿井以濟之。

translations.literal: From Tiziguan downstream, water volume increased by one third; he also restored two abandoned canals on the Qingye River bank—where water could not reach, he urged the people to dig wells to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: From Tiziguan downstream the flow increased by a third. He restored two abandoned canals on the Qingye River and urged villagers beyond the water's reach to dig wells.

sentences.zh: 先後增井五百有餘，無旱憂。

translations.literal: In all more than five hundred wells were added—no fear of drought.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred wells were dug in all, and drought ceased to be a worry.

sentences.zh: 涇民多逐末，不重蓋藏，義倉無實儲。

translations.literal: Jingyang people mostly pursued trade, did not value saving, and the charity granaries held no real stores.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyang people favored trade over thrift, and the charity granaries stood empty.

sentences.zh: 官俊謂積穀備荒，莫善於年出年收。

translations.literal: Guanjun said that storing grain against famine was best done by lending out and collecting back each year.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjun held that the best way to store grain against famine was to lend it out and collect it back each year.

sentences.zh: 躬詣各鄉勸諭捐穀，嚴定收放之法，民感其誠，輸納恐後，倉皆充實。

translations.literal: He personally went to each township to urge grain donations, strictly set rules for lending and return—the people were moved by his sincerity, paid in fear of being late, and the granaries were all filled.
translations.idiomatic: He went to every township to urge grain donations and set strict rules for lending and return. Moved by his sincerity, people rushed to contribute until every granary was full.

sentences.zh: 十九年，旱荒，全活凡數万人。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year drought and famine struck; he saved altogether tens of thousands of lives.
translations.idiomatic: In 1893 drought and famine struck, and he saved tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 編保甲，捕盜賊，地方靖謐。

translations.literal: He organized the baojia system, captured bandits and thieves—the district grew calm and secure.
translations.idiomatic: He organized the baojia system, captured bandits, and the district grew calm.

sentences.zh: 官俊故績學，立賓興堂，置性理、經濟有用之書，日與諸生講習。

translations.literal: Guanjun was originally a scholar of accomplishment; he established a Binxing Hall, stocked it with books on moral philosophy and practical statecraft, and lectured daily with students.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar himself, Guanjun founded a Binxing Hall, stocked it with books on moral philosophy and practical statecraft, and lectured students daily.

sentences.zh: 增義塾，定課程，親考校之。

translations.literal: He added charity schools, set curricula, and personally examined the students.
translations.idiomatic: He added charity schools, set curricula, and examined students himself.

sentences.zh: 凡有利於民者，為之無不力。

translations.literal: Whatever benefited the people, he pursued it with full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever benefited the people, he pursued with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1894.

sentences.zh: 疾篤時，猶強起治事，捐俸千金以恤孤貧。

translations.literal: When gravely ill he still forced himself up to handle affairs, donating a thousand taels of salary to succor orphans and the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Even on his deathbed he forced himself up to work and donated a thousand taels of salary to orphans and the poor.

sentences.zh: 民為祠，歲時祀之。

translations.literal: The people built a shrine and worshipped him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The people built him a shrine and worshipped him at the seasons.

sentences.zh: =陳文黻=陳文黻，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: =Chen Wenfu= Chen Wenfu was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wenfu came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以諸生入貲為通判。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he purchased appointment as sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he purchased appointment as sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治間，從軍，積功晉同知，留陝西。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi era he joined the army, accumulated merit and was promoted to sub-prefect, remaining in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi era he joined the army, earned promotion to sub-prefect through merit, and remained in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，署鄠縣知縣，以教化為先，政平訟理。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he acted as magistrate of Hu County, putting moral instruction first—government was peaceful and lawsuits settled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he served as acting magistrate of Hu County, putting moral instruction first; government was peaceful and lawsuits were settled.

sentences.zh: 九年，授留壩廳同知。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed sub-prefect of Liuba Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he was appointed sub-prefect of Liuba Circuit.

sentences.zh: 廳獄舊有棗茨，經費歲徵之民，文黻革之。

translations.literal: The circuit prison had an old levy for jujube-thorn bedding; funds were annually collected from the people—Wenfu abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit prison had long levied an annual fee on the people for bedding supplies; Wenfu abolished it.

sentences.zh: 境內無質庫，貧民稱貸，盤剝者要重息。

translations.literal: Within the jurisdiction there were no pawnshops; poor people borrowed on word, and usurers demanded heavy interest.
translations.idiomatic: There were no pawnshops in the district; the poor borrowed on word, and usurers charged crushing interest.

sentences.zh: 文黻設裕民公所，貸民錢，息以十一，取其贏以備公用，民便之。

translations.literal: Wenfu established a Public Benefit Office, lent money to the people at ten percent interest, and used the surplus for public needs—the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu opened a public loan office, lent money at ten percent interest, and used the surplus for public needs. The people welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 廳境山多於田，無物產以資生。

translations.literal: In the circuit mountains outnumbered fields; there were no products to sustain livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains outnumbered fields in the circuit, and there was little to live on.

sentences.zh: 乃週曆山谷，辨其土宜，作種橡說及山蠶四要，遍諭鄉民。

translations.literal: He then toured the valleys, distinguished what each soil suited, wrote essays on planting oaks and the four essentials of wild silkworms, and spread the word through the townships.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the valleys, tested what each soil would bear, wrote essays on oak planting and wild silkworm raising, and spread the word through every township.

sentences.zh: 頒給樹秧蠶種，募工導之。

translations.literal: He distributed saplings and silkworm eggs and hired workers to guide the people.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed saplings and silkworm eggs and hired instructors to guide the people.

sentences.zh: 絲成，制機教織，設局收買，重其值以招之。

translations.literal: When silk was produced, he set up looms to teach weaving, established a bureau to purchase it, and paid high prices to attract producers.
translations.idiomatic: When silk came in, he set up looms to teach weaving, opened a purchasing bureau, and paid premium prices to draw producers.

sentences.zh: 又購紫陽茶種，課之樹藝，於是地無棄利。

translations.literal: He also purchased Ziyang tea seeds and ordered their cultivation—thereafter no land's profit went unused.
translations.idiomatic: He also bought Ziyang tea seeds and ordered them planted—until no scrap of land went unused.

sentences.zh: 俗素樸陋，歲科試附鳳縣額，每試或不得一人。

translations.literal: The custom was plain and backward; the annual provincial examination quota was attached to Feng County, and each year sometimes not a single candidate qualified.
translations.idiomatic: The people were plain and backward; their examination quota was attached to Feng County, and some years not one candidate qualified.

sentences.zh: 建書院、義塾，置書籍，延高才者為之師。

translations.literal: He built an academy and charity schools, stocked books, and invited men of talent as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: He built an academy and charity schools, stocked them with books, and hired talented teachers.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，橫舍彬彬，遂請奏設廳學，建官置額。

translations.literal: After several years the halls were full of cultivated scholars; he then petitioned to establish a circuit school, build offices, and set a quota.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the halls brimmed with scholars. He petitioned to establish a circuit school with its own quota.

sentences.zh: 谿河多壅閼，橫溢為患。

translations.literal: Stream and river channels were often blocked and choked, overflowing to cause disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Streams and rivers were often choked with silt and flooded the land.

sentences.zh: 陳開河策，未果行，值水猝發，已逾報災例限，便宜開倉賑之。

translations.literal: He proposed a river-opening plan but it had not been carried out; sudden flood struck, already past the deadline for reporting disaster—he exercised discretionary authority to open the granary for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He had proposed dredging the rivers but the plan had not gone forward. When flood struck suddenly, past the deadline for disaster reports, he opened the granary on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 跋涉沮洳，勞疾不輟。

translations.literal: Trudging through mud and marsh, he labored on despite illness without pause.
translations.idiomatic: He waded through mud and marsh, working through illness without rest.

sentences.zh: 煮粥賑近郊，多所全活。

translations.literal: He cooked porridge to relieve the near suburbs—many lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: He set up porridge kitchens in the suburbs and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 久之，流民坌集，復申開河議，以工代賑，不得請。

translations.literal: After a time displaced people gathered in crowds; he again petitioned the river-opening plan, relief through labor—but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: As refugees poured in, he again petitioned to dredge the rivers and offer work-for-relief—but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 則因其眾治道路，濬溝渠，出私錢給值，負累至數千緡，民感其德。

translations.literal: Then using the crowd he repaired roads and dredged ditches, paying wages from private funds—the burden reached several thousand strings of cash; the people were moved by his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He put the crowd to work on roads and ditches instead, paying wages from his own purse until he was thousands of strings in debt. The people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 廳介萬山中，林谷深阻，奸民狙伏行劫，或掠婦孺賣境外。

translations.literal: The circuit lay amid ten thousand mountains, forests and valleys deep and obstructed—villains lurked to rob on the roads, or seized women and children to sell beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit lay deep in the mountains; villains lurked in the forests to rob travelers or kidnap women and children to sell across the border.

sentences.zh: 文黻密圖其處示捕役，時復微服蹟之，多就擒治。

translations.literal: Wenfu secretly mapped the places and showed the constables, sometimes going in disguise to track them—many were captured and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu secretly mapped their haunts for his constables and sometimes tracked them in disguise—many were captured.

sentences.zh: 實行保甲，於民戶職業、田產、丁口、年歲、婚嫁，載冊不厭煩瑣。

translations.literal: He fully implemented the baojia system, recording in registers without tiring of minutiae each household's occupation, land, population, ages, and marriages.
translations.idiomatic: He fully implemented the baojia system, recording every household's occupation, land, population, ages, and marriages in painstaking detail.

sentences.zh: 及賑饑，稽之冊，如家至戶覿，訴訟亦莫敢欺，事益簡焉。

translations.literal: When distributing famine relief he checked the registers as if visiting each home in person; in lawsuits too none dared deceive—affairs grew simpler.
translations.idiomatic: At famine relief he checked the registers as if visiting every home; in lawsuits too no one dared deceive him—and affairs grew simpler.

sentences.zh: 民有殺子婦匿其尸者，母家以無左驗，不得直。

translations.literal: A man killed his daughter-in-law and hid the corpse; her mother's family, lacking corroborating evidence, could not obtain justice.
translations.idiomatic: A man killed his daughter-in-law and hid the body; her family could not obtain justice for lack of evidence.

sentences.zh: 文黻偶行山徑，群鴉噪於前，索而得之，一訊具服，人以為神。

translations.literal: Wenfu happened to walk a mountain path; a flock of crows clamored ahead—searching, he found the body; one interrogation and the full confession came—people thought it divine.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu happened along a mountain path where crows were clamoring; he searched and found the body. One interrogation brought a full confession, and people called it miraculous.

sentences.zh: 十八年，調署潼關廳，未任，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to act at Tongguan Circuit—before taking office he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1892 he was transferred to Tongguan Circuit but died before taking office.

sentences.zh: =李素=李素，字少白，雲南保山人。

translations.literal: =Li Su= Li Su, style name Shaobai, was a native of Baoshan in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su, whose style was Shaobai, came from Baoshan in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 同治六年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the sixth year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of 1867.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，授陝西商州直隸州知州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was appointed prefect of Shangzhou Direct-Controlled Prefecture in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu era he was appointed prefect of Shangzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 值州境歉收，饑民聚掠。

translations.literal: Just as the prefecture had a poor harvest, hungry people gathered to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the prefecture suffered a poor harvest, hungry mobs began to loot.

sentences.zh: 時山西大祲，商州為轉運要衝。

translations.literal: At the time Shanxi suffered great famine; Shangzhou was a vital transit point for relief transport.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi was in the grip of famine, and Shangzhou lay on the vital route for relief grain.

sentences.zh: 素招民運賑糧，使飢者得食。

translations.literal: Su recruited the people to transport relief grain so the hungry could eat.
translations.idiomatic: Su enlisted the people to haul relief grain so the hungry could eat.

sentences.zh: 集貲數万緡，購籽糧散給。

translations.literal: He collected funds of tens of thousands of strings of cash, purchased seed grain, and distributed it.
translations.idiomatic: He raised tens of thousands of strings of cash, bought seed grain, and distributed it widely.

sentences.zh: 設粥廠十餘所，災後倉儲一空，捐穀萬石。

translations.literal: He set up more than ten porridge kitchens; after the disaster the granaries were empty—he donated ten thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He opened more than ten porridge kitchens. When the granaries stood empty after the disaster, he donated ten thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 六年，大水，加意撫卹，災不為害。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, great flood—he gave extra care to relief and consolation, and the disaster did not become ruinous.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year a great flood struck; his painstaking relief kept the disaster from becoming ruin.

sentences.zh: 州城濱丹河，遇盛漲則負郭田廬漂沒，城中亦半為澤國。

translations.literal: The prefectural city bordered the Dan River—when the flood swelled, fields and homes beyond the wall were swept away, and half the city became a waterlogged land.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on the Dan River. When the river swelled, fields and homes beyond the walls were swept away and half the city turned into a lake.

sentences.zh: 素創築石堤二百餘丈，城門月堤十餘丈，遂無水患。

translations.literal: Su pioneered construction of a stone dike more than two hundred zhang long and crescent dikes at the gates more than ten zhang—thereafter there was no flood trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Su built a stone dike more than two hundred zhang long and crescent-shaped dikes at the city gates, and thereafter floods ceased to plague the city.

sentences.zh: 開州東隸花河山路三十餘裡、州西麻蒦嶺山路二十餘裡，行旅便之。

translations.literal: He opened the mountain road along Huahua River east of the prefecture, more than thirty li, and the mountain road over Mahe Ridge west of the prefecture, more than twenty li—travelers found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a mountain road along the Huahua River east of the prefecture—more than thirty li—and another over Mahe Ridge to the west—more than twenty li—greatly easing travel.

sentences.zh: 擴充商山書院，延碩儒課士，設義塾三十餘區，弦誦聞於比戶。

translations.literal: He expanded Shangshan Academy, invited eminent scholars to instruct students, set up more than thirty charity schools—the sound of reading reached every household.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded Shangshan Academy, invited eminent scholars to teach, and founded more than thirty charity schools until the sound of reading filled every household.

sentences.zh: 陋規病民者悉除之。

translations.literal: Shameful customary fees that harmed the people were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished every abusive customary fee that oppressed the people.

sentences.zh: 每歲寒冬，出私錢給孤寡。

translations.literal: Every year in deep winter he disbursed private funds to the orphaned and widowed.
translations.idiomatic: Every winter he paid the orphaned and widowed from his own purse.

sentences.zh: 緝捕籌經常之費。

translations.literal: He arranged regular funds for arrest and capture operations.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside regular funds for policing and arrests.

sentences.zh: 綠營餉薄，歲資助之。

translations.literal: Green Standard Army pay was thin—each year he subsidized them.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard Army pay was meager, and each year he subsidized the troops.

sentences.zh: 凡賑饑、積穀、築堤、修城、興學，莫不以鉅貲倡。

translations.literal: In famine relief, grain storage, dike building, wall repair, and founding schools—in all he led with large contributions.
translations.idiomatic: Whether famine relief, granaries, dikes, city walls, or schools—he invariably led each effort with a large contribution of his own.

sentences.zh: 一署同州知府。

translations.literal: Once he served as acting prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as acting prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 先後在官十八年，兩舉卓異。

translations.literal: Altogether eighteen years in office; twice cited for outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen years in office in all; twice cited for outstanding merit.

sentences.zh: 以病免歸，卒。

translations.literal: Illness led to dismissal and return home—he died.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his retirement; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 士民感之，多私祠祀焉。

translations.literal: Scholars and common people were moved by him; many privately enshrined and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and common people revered him, and many built private shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: =張楷=張楷，字仲模，湖北蘄水人。

translations.literal: =Zhang Kai= Zhang Kai, style name Zhongmo, was a native of Qishui in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai, whose style was Zhongmo, came from Qishui in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 同治十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷至侍講。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the tenth year of Tongzhi; selected as Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, promoted repeatedly to lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of 1871, he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, became a compiler, and rose to lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，疏論伊犁事，又請撤銷總兵周全有卹典，為時所稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he memorialized on the Ili affair, and also requested revocation of the posthumous honors of Brigade-General Zhou Quanyou—acts praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu era he memorialized on the Ili affair and petitioned to revoke posthumous honors for Brigade-General Zhou Quanyou—acts widely praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為浙江金華知府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as prefect of Jinhua in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he was appointed prefect of Jinhua in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 永康山中七堡、八堡，地險僻，盜藪也。

translations.literal: Qibao and Babao in the mountains of Yongkang—land rugged and remote, a bandits' nest.
translations.idiomatic: Qibao and Babao in the Yongkang mountains were remote and defensible—a bandits' nest.

sentences.zh: 楷設方略，捕誅匪首蔣元地，移縣丞駐山麓，獷​​俗一變。

translations.literal: Kai devised a plan, captured and executed the bandit chief Jiang Yuandi, moved the county assistant magistrate to station at the mountain foot—the wild custom changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Kai devised a strategy, captured and executed the bandit chief Jiang Yuandi, and posted the county assistant at the mountain foot—the wild country was transformed.

sentences.zh: 父憂去，服闋，補山西汾州。

translations.literal: Parental mourning took him away; when mourning ended, he was assigned to Fenzhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning; when the mourning period ended, he was assigned to Fenzhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 汾陽、平遙兩縣瀕河，鄉民冬令攔河築堰，引水灌田，水不得暢流。

translations.literal: Fenyang and Pingyao counties bordered the river; villagers in winter dammed the river to build weirs, drawing water to irrigate fields—the water could not flow freely.
translations.idiomatic: Fenyang and Pingyao lay on the river. Each winter villagers dammed it to irrigate their fields, choking the natural flow.

sentences.zh: 夏秋漲溢，各築護堤。

translations.literal: In summer and autumn floods swelled; each side built protective dikes.
translations.idiomatic: When summer and autumn floods came, each side built protective dikes.

sentences.zh: 以鄰為壑，輒械鬥蔓訟。

translations.literal: Treating neighbors as drainage ditches, they repeatedly fought with weapons and lawsuits spread.
translations.idiomatic: Each treated the other's land as a spillway; armed clashes and endless lawsuits followed.

sentences.zh: 楷禁築攔河堰，濬引渠以洩水，患紓而訟息。

translations.literal: Kai forbade building river-blocking weirs, dredged diversion canals to release water—calamity eased and lawsuits ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Kai banned river dams, dredged diversion canals to release floodwater, and both disasters and lawsuits subsided.

sentences.zh: 以南方戽水法導民，使開稻田，植桑課蠶。

translations.literal: Using southern water-lifting methods to guide the people, he had them open rice paddies, plant mulberry, and raise silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: He taught southern irrigation methods, had the people open rice paddies, planted mulberry, and organized sericulture.

sentences.zh: 有山曰黑煙，與交山葫蘆峪相連，匪徒窟穴其間，偵其姓名，掩捕盡獲之。

translations.literal: There was a mountain called Black Smoke, connected with Jiaoshan and Huluyu—bandits lurked in caves between them; he investigated their names and raided to capture them all.
translations.idiomatic: Black Smoke Mountain connected with Jiaoshan and Huluyu Valley, where bandits had dug in. Kai learned their names and raided their lairs, capturing them all.

sentences.zh: 治汾州七年，考績為山西最。

translations.literal: Governing Fenzhou seven years, his performance review ranked first in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years governing Fenzhou, his performance review ranked first in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 調太原，未任，母憂去。

translations.literal: Transferred to Taiyuan—before taking office, mother's mourning took him away.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiyuan but left for his mother's mourning before taking office.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補河南府。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, assigned to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was assigned to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鞏、洛之間素多盜，捕治巨魁，椎埋斂跡。

translations.literal: Between Gong and Luo bandits had always been many; capturing and punishing the chief ringleaders, grave-robbers and smugglers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The region between Gong and Luo had long been bandit country. He captured the chief ringleaders, and grave robbers and smugglers went to ground.

sentences.zh: 治獄多平反。

translations.literal: In handling prisons many wrongful convictions were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 調開封。

translations.literal: Transferred to Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，畿輔拳匪亂起，大河南北，群情洶洶，大吏持重不敢決。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the Boxer uprising rose in the capital region; north and south of the Yellow River public sentiment was turbulent—the senior officials held back and dared not decide.
translations.idiomatic: In 1899 the Boxer uprising erupted in the capital region. North and south of the Yellow River the public mood turned volatile, and senior officials hesitated, afraid to act.

sentences.zh: 楷力陳邪教不可信，外釁不可開。

translations.literal: Kai forcefully argued that heterodox cults were not to be trusted and foreign troubles must not be invited.
translations.idiomatic: Kai forcefully argued that heterodox cults could not be trusted and foreign war must not be invited.

sentences.zh: 揭示：「義和團既號義民，謂能避槍砲。

translations.literal: He posted a proclamation: "Since the Boxers call themselves righteous militia and claim to ward off bullets and cannon—
translations.idiomatic: He posted a proclamation: "Since the Boxers call themselves righteous militia and claim they can ward off bullets and cannon—

sentences.zh: 令詣城外空營候試，以槍擊果不入，編伍充兵。」

translations.literal: order them to the empty camp outside the city to await testing—if gunfire truly does not penetrate, enlist them in ranks as soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: send them to the empty camp outside the city for a test. If gunfire truly fails to pierce them, enlist them as soldiers."

sentences.zh: 奸民不得逞。

translations.literal: — wicked commoners could not have their way.
translations.idiomatic: With that, troublemakers lost their opening.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入都，潰兵南下，楷創議守河。

translations.literal: When the allied armies entered the capital, routed troops swept south—Kai was first to propose defending the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered Beijing, routed soldiers poured south. Kai was the first to propose defending the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 自汜水迄蘭儀，嚴稽渡口，凡持械之士，悉阻之不令入城，屬境安堵。

translations.literal: From Sishui to Lanyi he strictly inspected ferry crossings—every armed man was blocked and not allowed into the city; within his jurisdiction all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: From Sishui to Lanyi he tightened ferry crossings, turned back every armed man at the river, and kept his jurisdiction calm.

sentences.zh: 論者謂微楷之堅定，中原禍未艾也。

translations.literal: Commentators said had it not been for Kai's firmness, the Central Plain's calamity would not yet have ended.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that without Kai's steadfastness, the Central Plain would still have been in flames.

sentences.zh: 事定，開缺，以道員候補。

translations.literal: When affairs settled, his post was vacated; he awaited assignment as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs settled his post was vacated, and he awaited reassignment as a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1904.

sentences.zh: =王仁堪=王仁堪，字可莊，福建閩縣人，尚書慶雲之孫。

translations.literal: =Wang Renkan= Wang Renkan, style name Kezhuang, was a native of Min County in Fujian, grandson of Minister Wang Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renkan, whose style was Kezhuang, came from Min County in Fujian—grandson of Minister Wang Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he placed first among first-class metropolitan graduates and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 he placed first in the metropolitan examination and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 督山西學政，歷典貴州、江南、廣東鄉試，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He supervised Shanxi educational administration, successively presided over provincial examinations in Guizhou, Jiangnan, and Guangdong, and entered service in the South Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Shanxi education commissioner, presided over provincial examinations in Guizhou, Jiangnan, and Guangdong, and entered the South Study.

sentences.zh: 時俄羅斯索伊犁，使臣崇厚擅定條約，仁堪與修撰曹鴻勛等合疏劾之。

translations.literal: At the time Russia demanded Ili; envoy Chonghou arbitrarily fixed a treaty—Renkan with Compiler Cao Hongxun and others jointly memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: When Russia demanded Ili and envoy Chonghou signed a treaty on his own authority, Renkan joined Compiler Cao Hongxun and others in impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 太和門災，復與鴻勛應詔陳言，極論時政。

translations.literal: When the Taihe Gate burned, again with Hongxun he responded to the imperial call to speak, exhaustively discussing current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Taihe Gate, he joined Hongxun again in answering the imperial call to counsel, speaking bluntly on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 其請罷頤和園工程，謂：「工費指明不動正款，夫出之筦庫，何非小民膏血？

translations.literal: His request to halt the Summer Palace project said: "The construction costs specify no use of regular funds—but what comes from the treasury is not the common people's lifeblood?
translations.idiomatic: In petitioning to halt the Summer Palace project he wrote: "The budget says no regular funds will be touched—but what leaves the treasury if not the people's lifeblood?

sentences.zh: 計臣可執未動正款之說以告朝廷，朝廷何能執未動正款之說以謝天下？」

translations.literal: Can the finance minister hold to the claim of untouched regular funds when reporting to the court—and how can the court hold to that claim when answering the empire?"
translations.idiomatic: The finance minister may tell the court the regular funds remain untouched—but how can the court tell the empire the same?"

sentences.zh: 言尤切直。

translations.literal: — his words were especially blunt and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: His words were especially blunt and forthright.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出為江蘇鎮江知府。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out as prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1891 he was appointed prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 甫下車，丹陽教案起，由於教堂發見孩屍。

translations.literal: Barely having taken office, the Danyang missionary case erupted—from corpses of children discovered at the church.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken office when the Danyang missionary case erupted after child corpses were found at a church.

sentences.zh: 仁堪親驗孩屍七十餘具，陳於總督劉坤一曰：「名為天主教堂，不應有死孩骨。

translations.literal: Renkan personally examined more than seventy child corpses and stated to Governor Liu Kunyi: "Called a Catholic church—it should not contain dead children's bones.
translations.idiomatic: Renkan personally examined more than seventy child corpses and told Governor Liu Kunyi: "It is called a Catholic church. It ought not hold dead children's bones.

sentences.zh: 即兼育嬰局，不應無活嬰兒。

translations.literal: Even if it also runs an orphanage, there should not be no living infants.
translations.idiomatic: Even as an orphanage, it should not have no living infants.

sentences.zh: 傳教約本無準外國人育嬰之條，教士於約外兼辦育嬰，不遵奏行章程，使地方官得司稽察，禍由自召。

translations.literal: The missionary treaties originally had no provision allowing foreigners to raise infants; missionaries running orphanages beyond treaty scope, not following approved regulations so that local officials could inspect—disaster they invited upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The treaties never authorized foreigners to raise infants. Missionaries who ran orphanages beyond treaty bounds, ignoring regulations that left inspection to local officials, had brought disaster on themselves.

sentences.zh: 請曲貸愚民之罪，以安眾心；

translations.literal: I ask leniency for the ignorant commoners to settle public hearts;
translations.idiomatic: I ask clemency for the ignorant populace to calm public anger;

sentences.zh: 別給撫卹之費，以贍彼族。」

translations.literal: separately provide consolation funds to support that community."
translations.idiomatic: and separate consolation payments to satisfy their community."

sentences.zh: 坤一迂之，卒定犯罪軍流有差。

translations.literal: Kunyi was evasive; in the end fixed punishments of exile and military service with varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyi hedged. In the end the guilty were sentenced to exile and penal servitude in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 時外使屢責保護教堂，仁堪請奏定專律，謂：「條約無若何懲辦明文，每出一事，任意要挾。

translations.literal: At the time foreign envoys repeatedly demanded church protection—Renkan petitioned to enact dedicated laws, saying: "The treaties lack clear provisions on punishment—each incident becomes arbitrary coercion.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys kept demanding church protection. Renkan petitioned for dedicated laws, arguing: "The treaties spell out no punishments—so envoys coerce us at will with every incident.

sentences.zh: 宜明定焚毀教堂，作何賠償；

translations.literal: It is fitting to specify plainly: for burning churches, what compensation;
translations.idiomatic: Burning a church should carry a fixed indemnity;

sentences.zh: 殺傷教士，作何論抵；

translations.literal: for killing or wounding missionaries, what penalty;
translations.idiomatic: killing or wounding a missionary a fixed penalty;

sentences.zh: 以及口角斗毆等事，有定律可遵。

translations.literal: and for quarrels, brawls, and the like—fixed laws to follow.
translations.idiomatic: and brawls and disputes of every sort should have fixed laws to follow.

sentences.zh: 人心既平，訛言自息。」

translations.literal: Once hearts are settled, slander will cease of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Once hearts are settled, rumor will die of itself."

sentences.zh: 英人梅生為匪首李鴻購軍火，事覺，領事坐梅生罪僅監禁，仁堪上書總理各國事務衙門論之。

translations.literal: The Englishman Mason bought arms for the bandit chief Li Hong; when the affair came to light, the consul punished Mason with only imprisonment—Renkan wrote the Foreign Office to argue the point.
translations.idiomatic: When the Englishman Mason was caught buying arms for the bandit chief Li Hong, the consul sentenced Mason only to prison. Renkan wrote the Foreign Office to protest.
