sentences.zh: 又洋人忻愛珩遍謁守令，募捐義學，無遊歷護照。

translations.literal: Also the foreigner Xin Aiping visited prefects and magistrates everywhere, collecting donations for charity schools—without a travel passport.
translations.idiomatic: When the foreigner Xin Aiping toured prefects and magistrates fundraising for charity schools without a travel passport,

sentences.zh: 仁堪請關道送領事查辦，复議無照私入內地，應按中國律法科罪。

translations.literal: Renkan asked the customs circuit intendant to deliver him to the consul for investigation, and again argued that entering the interior without a passport should be punished under Chinese law.
translations.idiomatic: Renkan asked customs to deliver him to his consul—and argued that entering the interior without a passport should be punished under Chinese law.

sentences.zh: 雖皆未果行，時論韙之。

translations.literal: Though none of these was ultimately carried out, contemporary opinion approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Though none of these proposals prevailed, contemporaries praised him for them.

sentences.zh: 郡地多岡壟，旱易成災，仁堪以設渠塘為急務，不欲擾民，捐廉為倡。

translations.literal: The prefecture had many hills and ridges—drought easily became disaster; Renkan made building canals and ponds urgent business, unwilling to burden the people, donating his salary to lead.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was hilly and drought-prone. Renkan made canals and ponds an urgent priority, donated his salary to lead the effort, and refused to burden the people.

sentences.zh: 馳書乞諸親舊，商富感而輸助，得錢​​三萬緡，開塘二千三百有奇，溝渠閘壩以百計。

translations.literal: He hurried letters begging kin and friends; merchants and rich men were moved to contribute—obtaining thirty thousand strings of cash, opening more than twenty-three hundred ponds, canals, sluices, and dams numbering in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote kin and friends begging help. Moved merchants and gentry contributed thirty thousand strings of cash; more than twenty-three hundred ponds were dug and canals, sluices, and dams numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 十八年秋，丹陽大祲，恩賑之外，勸紳商捐貲，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighteenth year, Danyang suffered great famine—beyond imperial grace relief, he urged gentry and merchants to donate funds; very many lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1892 Danyang suffered severe famine. Beyond imperial relief he persuaded gentry and merchants to donate, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 又假官錢於民，使勿賣牛，名曰牛賑。

translations.literal: Also he lent official money to the people so they would not sell their oxen—called "ox relief."
translations.idiomatic: He also lent public funds so farmers would not sell their oxen—a program called "ox relief."

sentences.zh: 濬太平港、沙腰河、練湖、越瀆、蕭河、香草、簡瀆之屬，凡二十餘所，支溝別渠二百三十有奇。

translations.literal: He dredged Taiping Harbor, Shayao River, Lian Lake, Yuedu, Xiao River, Xiangcao, Jiandu, and the like—more than twenty places; branch ditches and separate canals more than two hundred thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged Taiping Harbor, Shayao River, Lian Lake, Yuedu, Xiao River, Xiangcao, Jiandu, and more than twenty other waterways, with more than two hundred thirty branch ditches and canals besides.

sentences.zh: 又鑿塘四千六百，以蓄高原之水。

translations.literal: Also he dug four thousand six hundred ponds to store highland water.
translations.idiomatic: He dug four thousand six hundred ponds to store highland runoff.

sentences.zh: 皆以工代賑，東西百餘里間，水利畢舉。

translations.literal: All used work-for-relief; within more than a hundred li east and west, water works were fully completed.
translations.idiomatic: All was work-for-relief; within a hundred li east and west, every water project was completed.

sentences.zh: 次年春，賑畢，餘四萬金，生息備積穀。

translations.literal: The next spring, relief finished, forty thousand taels remained; interest was collected to prepare grain storage.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, when relief ended, forty thousand taels remained; he invested the surplus to build up granaries.

sentences.zh: 牛賑餘錢，仿社倉法創社錢，按區分儲，為修溝洫、廣義塾之用。

translations.literal: Surplus funds from ox relief—following the communal granary method he created communal funds, stored by district, for dredging ditches and expanding charity schools.
translations.idiomatic: With surplus ox-relief funds he followed the communal granary model to create district communal treasuries for dredging and charity schools.

sentences.zh: 郡西鄉僻陋不知學，立榛思文社以教之。

translations.literal: The western townships of the prefecture were remote and backward, knowing no learning—he established the Zhensiawen Society to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: The western townships were remote and unlearned. He founded the Zhensiawen Society to teach them.

sentences.zh: 出私錢於府治前建南畾學舍。

translations.literal: He disbursed private funds to build the Nanlei academy before the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Nanlei academy before the prefectural yamen at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 在任兩年，於教養諸端，盡力為之。

translations.literal: Two years in office—in education, nurture, and every respect he exerted full effort.
translations.idiomatic: In two years in office he gave his full strength to education, relief, and every public duty.

sentences.zh: 調蘇州，已積勞致疾，日坐讞局清積案，風采動一時。

translations.literal: Transferred to Suzhou—already worn ill by accumulated labor, daily he sat in the review bureau clearing backlog cases; his presence moved the age.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Suzhou, already worn ill by overwork, he daily sat in the review bureau clearing backlogged cases—and his authority stirred the province.

sentences.zh: 甫三閱月，猝病卒，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Barely three months passed when sudden illness killed him—contemporary opinion mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: After barely three months he died suddenly. Contemporaries mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 鎮江士民列政績，籥請大吏上聞，謂其「視民事如家事，一以扶植善類、培養元氣為任，卓然有古循吏風」。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang scholars and people listed his achievements, petitioned senior officials to report upward, saying he "treated people's affairs like family business, taking as his charge supporting the good and nurturing fundamental vitality—standing out with the air of ancient exemplary officials."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang scholars and people petitioned the authorities to report his record, praising him for "treating the people's affairs as his own household business, devoted to nurturing the good and restoring the community's strength—a true exemplar in the ancient mold."

sentences.zh: 詔允宣付史館立傳，以表循良。

translations.literal: An edict approved transmitting to the Historiography Institute for biography, to honor exemplary governance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his record sent to the Historiography Institute for a biographical entry, honoring his exemplary service.

sentences.zh: 自光緒初定制，官吏歿後三十年，始得請祀名宦。

translations.literal: Since regulations set at the beginning of Guangxu, thirty years after an official's death was required before petitioning enshrinement in the hall of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Since regulations established in the early Guangxu era, an official could not be enshrined in the hall of eminent officials until thirty years after his death.

sentences.zh: 於是疆臣率徇眾意，輒請宣付立傳表章，曠典日致猥濫，仁堪為不愧雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon frontier governors generally followed popular will, readily petitioning transmission for biography and commendation—grand honors daily grew cheap and excessive; Renkan was one who did not disgrace the title.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter border governors routinely bowed to popular demand and petitioned for biographical honors—once rare tribute growing ever cheaper. Renkan was one who truly deserved it.
